stories.summary: Nagina MP Chandrashekhar said that law and order in UP is destroyed while the government remains carefree. No one is safe in the state. Bullets are being fired openly on the streets. UP government is committing atrocities by intoxicating people with religion. Some are being shot while others are being sent to jail. Now, even judges are upset with the government. It is being said that UP has conditions like an undeclared emergency. The state has a double-engine government of corruption and hooliganism. No caste or religion is benefiting from this. The public will respond to this in the 2027 assembly elections. Chandrashekhar arrived in Jaunpur on Wednesday. Here, he accused the forced demolition of the Dal Mandi market in Varanasi and the forceful land acquisition. He said that the statue of Ahilyabai Holkar was broken. A child from the Pal community who raised a voice against this was sent to jail. Now read the major points of Chandrashekhar's statement... 1. Children's safety is my responsibility Regarding the matter of Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, Chandrashekhar said - The case is in court. He wants an impartial investigation. On the UGC issue, the Azad Samaj Party is ready. If they need to travel across India for the children's safety, they are ready. Protecting children is their responsibility. Before being a politician, they were a social worker, so they understand children's pain. 2. Youth wandering with degrees, govt is misleading Chandrashekhar prominently raised the issue of youth employment. He said that youth are wandering with degrees, while the government is misleading them instead of providing employment. He called the insult of educated youth an insult to the country. 3. Police personnel should have 8-hour shifts Chandrashekhar said - When our government comes, the exploitation of police personnel will end. The government should stop treating police personnel like animals. Fix their duty to 8 hours. The Bahujan society has now recognised its rights and entitlements. He gave the slogan 'Now we will neither vote for Manuvadis nor give them notes'. The Birbhanpur case was also emphasised in the rally. He alleged that the administration is taking one-sided action. Victims are not getting justice. We will raise this entire matter in Parliament from March 9 and demand answers from the government. 4. Panchayat election dates extended due to fear of our party Whether it's the 3-tier panchayat elections or the upcoming assembly elections, the Azad Samaj Party is ready. This time, the party will send its workers to win elections in large numbers and liberate the common people from the poor condition of Uttar Pradesh. If any party is afraid, it is of the Azad Samaj Party. The party has been continuously holding rallies for the past 3 months, while other parties have not yet started rallies. Due to this fear, government ministers are postponing the panchayat election dates. If elections were held today, the Azad Samaj Party would become the largest party. 5. Will conduct padyatra in protest against new UGC rules If needed, a padyatra will be conducted across India to implement UGC rules. People will be made aware of how children's rights are being violated. On the question of American pressure on the Prime Minister, he said that Modi ji should tell the truth to the public.

stories.title: 2 people injured by Chinese kite string in Lucknow:Doctor's nose and teenager's hand got injured, 12 injured in 15 days; 1 death
stories.summary: Two people were injured by a Chinese kite string in Lucknow. In the first incident, a girl riding a scooter was injured by a string near the DAV College overbridge in the Hussainganj police station area. She suffered deep wounds on her hand. In the second incident, a doctor from the Community Medicine Department at KGMU got his nose cut by the kite string. This is the 13th case of kite string injuries in 15 days. According to eyewitnesses, the girl was passing through the overbridge on Wednesday afternoon. Suddenly, a kite reel came towards her neck. She immediately tried to remove the string with her hand. During this, her hand was badly cut by the string. People present nearby helped her and took her to a nearby hospital for primary treatment. Doctor's nose cut by kite string Dr. Deepak Gupta from the Department of Community Medicine at KGMU was hit by a Chinese kite string on the Charak intersection bridge. This caused serious injuries to his nose and ear. After primary treatment at a nearby hospital, he was sent home. Series of throat cutting incidents started from Haiderganj, youth died On February 5, 2026, Mohammed Shoaib, a 33-year-old medical worker, was riding his bike on the Haiderganj flyover. A Chinese kite string was stuck there. Shoaib couldn't see it, and it cut him. He was taken to the hospital but couldn't be saved. The incident shook the entire city. On the same day in Gomti Nagar Extension, an electricity department contract worker's neck was cut by a kite string. He needed 4 stitches. He was climbing a pole for repair work. The very next day, a retired army man's jaw was cut about 10 inches by the string. Fortunately, the string hit a little away from his neck. 4 serious cases in 14 hours on February 9 On February 9, within 14 hours, 4 people were injured by a kite string at Kudiya Ghat, Bandha Road (Thakurganj), Hewett Road, and Naka Flyover. Some had neck cuts, while others had bloody faces. On February 12, 29-year-old Dr. Surbhi was injured by a kite string at Hahnemann Crossing in Gomtinagar. She was riding a scooter when the kite string suddenly caused deep wounds near her forehead and ear. On February 14, advocate Shailendra Kumar was injured in Aliganj. On February 15, journalist Dhruv Narayan Pandey was hit by a kite string near Pakaria Bridge in Alambagh. On February 16, Mohammad Musharraf and his wife were also injured near Husainganj Flyover. Raids conducted in 48 hours, inspections at over 700 locations After one death in Lucknow due to a kite string, the police conducted large-scale raids on February 5 and 6. They claimed to have inspected around 700 shops and locations. Kite strings were seized from many places, warnings were issued, and FIRs were also registered. Flying kites with strings was also traced using drones. Bazar Khala police arrested two youths who were allegedly found with Chinese manjha. The youths were going somewhere on a bike when police caught them based on an informer's tip. It was claimed they were going kite flying. Police actions became lax within 2-4 days. High Court also strict... Government order alone not enough, law making necessary The Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court took a strict stance on the purchase, sale, and use of Chinese kite string. During the hearing on February 10, the court said that government orders alone are not sufficient to stop this; legal provisions will have to be made. The court warned that if the sale and use of kite strings continues, the government will have to compensate the victims. A division bench of Justice Rajan Roy and Justice AK Chowdhury passed this order on a public interest petition filed by local advocate Motilal Yadav. The court clarified that a strong legal framework is necessary for a complete ban on lead-coated and nylon strings known as Chinese kite string. The court has asked the UP government to file a counter-affidavit by March 11. Impose Complete Ban, don't be active on death headlines The government also argued to the High Court that these are synthetic strings and they have been wrongly named 'Chinese Manja', which creates confusion that they are imported from China. However, the court was not satisfied with these arguments of the government. The court clarified that merely issuing government orders is not a permanent solution to the problem. More concrete steps need to be taken. The court said - Whenever serious injuries or deaths occur due to such a kite string. They make media headlines, and only then do officials become active. Don't act only on headlines. File a new affidavit and make laws to prevent the manufacturing, sale, and use of such kite strings. Impose a complete ban on it. Present the proposal to implement legal provisions.

stories.title: Passenger collapses at Bareilly station, jawan revives him:GRP constable performs CPR; doctors confirm heart attack symptoms
stories.summary: A GRP jawan saved a passenger's life after a heart attack at Bareilly Railway Junction. The passenger was standing at the junction when his health deteriorated. He experienced severe chest pain and collapsed on the ground. That's when family members started screaming for help. Upon receiving information, the GRP constable stationed at the platform came to them. The constable gave CPR three times for 30 seconds each. Within 90 seconds, the passenger started breathing again. Seeing this, tears welled up in the eyes of the passenger's relatives. After this, he was taken to the hospital, where his treatment is ongoing. The incident occurred on February 21, and the video emerged on February 25. Dinesh had arrived in Bareilly from Bihar Dinesh Monia (50), a resident of Gaya district in Bihar, works as an auto driver in Dhanbad. His family includes wife Lakshmi, son Vishal (16), and daughter Gudiya (19). On February 21, he arrived in Bareilly with 25 people, including his five sisters and 3 sisters-in-law. As soon as he got down on platform number 2 from the Howrah-Delhi Amrit Bharat train, he experienced severe chest pain. He suddenly collapsed on the platform. His family members started screaming for help in panic. Upon receiving the information, GRP Constable Hari Om, who was on duty, immediately reached the spot. He checked the passenger's pulse and breathing, which had almost stopped. Hari Om immediately started giving Cardio Pulmonary Resuscitation (CPR). Doctors say - 3 to 5 minutes are crucial in heart attack Just a few seconds later, movement was seen in the passenger's body. After 90 seconds, his breathing returned. Seeing this, tears came to the eyes of family members. After this, the family immediately took Dinesh to the hospital, where he was treated. Doctors said that if CPR had not given at the right time, the situation could have been fatal. According to experts, the initial 3-5 minutes are extremely important in case of a heart attack or cardiac arrest. Wife Lakshmi said that we were supposed to go to Manauna Dham in Aonla, Bareilly. But her husband's health deteriorated. After a heart attack, he was admitted to Bareilly District Hospital. Then we went for darshan. After this, the next day we returned home. Now my husband is undergoing treatment at a private hospital in Dhanbad. GRP constable said he was patrolling on the platform GRP constable Hariom said - I was patrolling at the junction. Then I received information that a passenger had fainted on platform number 2. I ran to the spot. I first checked his pulse. Then gave him CPR. When his breathing returned, I said wait, let me call an ambulance. But the passenger's family took him to the district hospital by car. I have been a medical science student. I had taken CPR training on the Police Department's Karmayogi app. That's why I was able to properly give CPR to the passenger. CMO said - Dinesh had symptoms of heart attack Meanwhile, CMO Dr. Vishram Singh said that a patient named Dinesh came to the district hospital. Upon examination, it was found that he had symptoms of a heart attack. His life was saved by getting CPR in time. He was discharged after primary treatment.

stories.title: Leopard enters Ghaziabad school, caught after 7 hours:Animal tranquilised and taken to Saharanpur; exams cancelled
stories.summary: A leopard entered a school in Ghaziabad on Wednesday morning, causing panic. The school immediately declared a holiday and sent messages to parents asking them not to send their children. Exams of more than 100 students were cancelled. The school administration informed the Forest Department, whose team quickly reached the spot. Nets were laid along the school boundary to trap the leopard. After about 7 hours, it was tranquilised and captured. It will be taken to Saharanpur and later released in the Shivalik hills by the Forest Department. CCTV footage from 6:45 am showed the leopard walking in a park inside the campus before entering a room. Police from Kavinagar station sealed the surrounding area, deploying over 50 personnel. Barricades were set up, and the road in front of the school was closed. Fortunately, the school was empty due to the early hour. The security in-charge spotted the leopard while checking CCTV on his phone while reporting for duty. He immediately shared the video with the school management and the Forest Department. The incident occurred at Green Field Public School, a CBSE-affiliated institution in Govindpuram.

stories.title: BSNL GM, DGM removed for assigning staff to fetch underwear:‘Royal Protocol’ made for Sangam snan; Scindia calls it shocking
stories.summary: The case of making royal arrangements for the private visit of BSNL Director Vivek Banzal in UP has reached Delhi. Action has been taken against 2 senior officers. Principal General Manager (GM) Brijendra Kumar Singh and DGM Jageshwar Verma of Prayagraj Business Area have been transferred. Brijendra Singh has been sent to Srikakulam in Andhra Pradesh, and Jageshwar Verma to the Network Transmission North Unit. Its office is in Delhi. Vivek Banzal was going to visit Prayagraj. On February 18, GM Brijendra Kumar Singh issued a VIP protocol, which was signed by DGM Jageshwar Verma. 50 employees were assigned duty for Vivek Banzal. A minute-to-minute program was set for everything from his bathing to underwear, oil, comb, and chips, etc. Everything was happening at government expense. When the protocol copy was leaked, the government faced heavy criticism. Bansal cancelled his visit. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia has taken cognisance of the matter. He said, A show cause notice has been sent to Vivek Banjal. He has been given seven days to respond. This matter is not acceptable in any way and is extremely shocking. Appropriate action will be taken in this matter. Ministry considered the matter highly objectionable Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said, I have made it clear that this is inappropriate and violates established rules and traditions. This is absolutely not acceptable to me. This is shocking. The Director has been given seven days to respond. After receiving the response and investigation, appropriate action will be taken. Sources said that the way officers were assigned duty in the protocol was considered condemnable and objectionable. This matter will not be taken lightly. Strict action may be taken against Banjal and other officers. Sir's royal hobbies, 50 officers deployed in royal arrangements BSNL's Director (CFA, Consumer Fixed Access) Vivek Banzal was coming to Prayagraj. A protocol was issued on February 18. It stated that the Director would be on a visit to Prayagraj on February 25 and 26. During this time, he would hold meetings with officers. Also, he would visit different places in Prayagraj and the Jain pilgrimage site in Kaushambi. Assigned responsibility from oil-soap to shopping and packing Committees of 50 officers were formed and assigned duties for everything from Director Vivek Banzal's drinking water to soap and oil. Different responsibilities were assigned to each. One of these committees was also given the responsibility of purchasing and packing various types of kits. One of these kits includes a water bottle, chocolate, chips, fruit juice, a glass, napkin. While another kit includes instructions for arranging a towel, underwear, mirror-comb, soap-shampoo, oil and slippers. This protocol was issued by the DGM posted at the GM office in Prayagraj Business Area. Now read what was written in the order... According to the Director (CFA)'s tour program, their visit to Prayagraj BA is proposed that is scheduled for February 25-26 with CGM UP (East) Circle and PGM (CFA), UP(East) Circle. All officers/employees are requested to actively participate in making the scheduled visit successful. Try to contribute. The committee officers/officials listed below have been nominated to complete the work written against their names on time. The order was cancelled the very next day The day after the protocol was issued, someone posted it on social media. Along with this, it was also criticized calling it a royal arrangement. Many users also made various comments about it. After this, on February 19 itself, an office order was suddenly issued by the DGM. It stated that the previously issued order regarding the proposed visit is cancelled with immediate effect. Also, any previous guidelines issued in this regard should be considered ineffective. This is what was written in the cancellation order... It is informed that the office order, which was issued regarding the Director (CFA)'s proposed visit to Prayagraj BA, has been cancelled with immediate effect. All concerned officers/employees are requested to take note of this cancellation. Take action accordingly. Any instructions issued earlier regarding the above order shall be considered invalid. BSNL has been running at a loss for the past 18 years. It was supposed to return to profit in fiscal year 2025, but according to recent reports, the company has gone into losses again. In the second quarter (July-September) of fiscal year 2025, BSNL incurred a net loss of Rs 1,357 crores. Why BSNL remained continuously in loss, let's understand in 6 points

stories.summary: A young man was shot dead in broad daylight in the Ramraj area of Meerut. The attacker, who came on a bike, shot the youth twice. The first bullet hit him in the back at the waist, while the second bullet was fired point-blank at his temple. The victim's brain matter was scattered. After firing the first shot, the killer shouted in the market, "Is there any brave soul who can save him?" Then he fired the second bullet at his temple. Police investigation has revealed that the young man had an affair with the killer's wife. He had eloped with her. The deceased was planning to marry the killer's wife doing love marriage. It is reported that there had been an argument between them a few days ago regarding the love affair. The incident happened on Wednesday afternoon, right in front of the Sanatan Dharma temple in Bahsuma market. Surendra (28), a resident of Jagjiwan Puri locality in Ramraj, was passing through the market. He was alone on his bike. Around 2:30, an attacker who came on a bike shot Surendra in the back in front of the Sanatan Dharma temple in Ramraj's main market. As soon as the bullet hit, Surendra fell from the bike. After this, the attacker ran close to Surendra. He put a pistol to his temple and fired a second shot. Then he started his bike and fled from the scene. People present at the spot ran to Surendra. They rushed him to the hospital in a bloodied condition, where doctors declared him dead. Chaos erupted in market after gunshot As soon as shots were fired, chaos erupted in the market. People started running here and there due to the stampede. Upon receiving information, the SP Rural also reached the spot along with the local police. They gathered information about the incident by questioning people in the market. Necessary directions were given to the police team. Police have sent Surendra's body for a post-mortem. SP Abhijeet Kumar said that CCTV footage is being examined to identify the attacker. Information will also be taken from the deceased's family members to understand the reason behind the incident. Surendra was going to have love marriage with married woman Police investigation has revealed that the deceased Surendra had eloped with a married woman about one and a half years ago. She was a resident of Sanauta village in the Falawda police station area. Surendra was soon going to have a court marriage with her. The woman's husband had been seeking revenge from Surendra since she ran away. The killer and Surendra had once argued about a woman in the middle of the market. Today, when the opportunity arose, the woman's husband killed Surendra. The area where the murder took place borders Meerut. According to the boundary area, Ramraj town is in Muzaffarnagar district, while the police station area falls under Bahsuma, Meerut. SP Rural Abhijit Kumar said - Surendra was traveling by bike. The attacker also came alone on a bike. The young man was shot. He was taken to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The police team is investigating the murder case. The attacker will be identified and arrested soon.

stories.title: SP Chief attacks Deputy CM over Kanpur incident:Akhilesh says, 'NRC targeted Muslims and SIR forces Hindus to find documents'
stories.summary: Akhilesh Yadav said that Batuk, who is revered in their tradition, was insulted in Kanpur by having his hair pulled. He criticised the Deputy Chief Minister, saying such actions bring great sin and that the Deputy CM lacks influence and credibility, adding that he should resign. He also referred to past bulldozer actions in the city, alleging that a Brahmin mother and daughter were burned during the drive. He said the Deputy CM had once promised respect, calling current leaders self-serving. He further claimed that over 3 lakh people in Unnao received notices. He alleged that BJP leaders earlier sought documents from Muslims through the NRC, and now, after the SIR, Hindus are also being forced to search for papers. Akhilesh attended a wedding in Kanpur with his daughter Aditi Yadav. They later visited Ghata Para Restaurant in Swaroop Nagar, where Aditi Yadav and SP MLA Naseem Solanki inaugurated the outlet by cutting a ribbon. He also ate samosas at the famous Munna Samosa shop on Birhana Road. During a previous visit on February 12, he had asked whether kachori or samosa was more popular and had expressed his wish to try the samosas.

stories.title: Mock drill simulates attack on CM Yogi in Lucknow:Commandos rescue within 3 mins; agencies test VIP security and evacuation methods
stories.summary: A mock drill was conducted in Lucknow simulating an attack on CM Yogi and an emergency rescue. The CM had gone to an event. Suddenly, he was attacked. A youth sitting in the crowd opened fire. In the blink of an eye, commandos deployed for CM's security immediately covered him. He was rescued within 3 minutes. This scene was shown at the Indira Gandhi Pratishthan (IGP) in the capital. Currently, CM Yogi Adityanath is on a foreign tour. He is in Japan after Singapore. On Wednesday, a mock drill was conducted to test his security arrangements. In the mock drill, CM arrived from his residence at Kalidas Marg to attend a private event. During this time, a hypothetical attack situation was created during his speech at the event venue. Practiced taking Chief Minister to hospital In the mock drill, a scene was created of a youth firing. In which the situation of the Chief Minister getting shot was depicted. As soon as the firing alert was received, NSG commandos immediately took position and safely evacuated the Chief Minister. After this, police and other security personnel practiced the procedure of taking the Chief Minister for treatment in an injured condition. According to officials, this entire process was done to test VIP security protocol and emergency response time. Lohia Hospital put on alert After the shooting, Lohia Hospital was immediately alerted. During this time, all police personnel and hospital administration went into alert mode. Patients arriving there were immediately stopped to one side, and a path was prepared for the convoy to enter. However, seeing the serious condition, they were sent to Delhi from the airport. Taken to Delhi when condition deteriorated CM's condition was becoming critical. After which, he was taken to Delhi. The vehicles carrying him were diverted towards Amausi airport. From there, a mock drill was conducted to take him to Delhi AIIMS.

stories.title: Sanju Samson may return vs Zimbabwe:Rinku Singh to rejoin team before must-win clash, says Sitanshu Kotak
stories.summary: Team India batting coach Sitanshu Kotak hinted at Sanju Samson's return in the playing XI in the Super 8 match against Zimbabwe. India, after beginning their Super 8 campaign with a defeat to South Africa, now face a must-win situation against Zimbabwe in their second match on 26 February. India and Zimbabwe will battle it out at the MA Chidambaram Stadium in Chennai. Not just a win but India also need to improve their Net Run Rate (NRR) which took a massive hit and is at -3.800 after the 76-run loss to the Proteas. 'There can be changes' says Sitanshu Kotak in pre-match presser When speaking on India potentially making changes in their playing XI, Kotak said that it was a possibility. Despite boasting of an explosive top-order, India have not had a noteworthy opening partnership with Abhishek Sharma and Tilak Varma not being amongst the runs. With India's top three batters all being left-handers, the opposition have turned to off-spin to strike early and that has happened in all five matches that the defending champions have played. "There can be changes. It goes without saying because there are two lefties at the top and the opposition are bowing off spinners. I personally think it is not a problem, but since we have lost early wickets, there will be thoughts," Kotak said, when speaking at the pre-match press conference in Chennai. : Sanju Samson's return, net run rate pressure: 3 talking points for India in do-or-die match vs Zimbabwe Sitanshu Kotak 'not really concerned' about batting failure against SA India had a horrifying batting performance against South Africa, losing three wickets inside the powerplay and were eventually bowled out for just 111 in 18.5 overs while chasing 188. The highest partnership that India had was of 35 runs between Hardik Pandya and Shivam Dube. Prior to the T20 World Cup, India's batting performance in bilaterals sent warnings to other teams but so far, the Men in Blue have not had a complete performance with the willow. "During the bilaterals, the batting was clicking. Last game, the batting was concerning. I'm not looking at individual failures," he said. Kotak added, “We should take the last game in stride. That is the lowest we have scored in two years. Openers haven't clicked either. It's fine, I wouldn't stress too much about it. Not really that concerned.” : Ishan Kishan rises to No. 5 in T20I rankings:Tilak Varma slips to seventh spot; Jasprit Bumrah enters top 10 Rinku Singh to rejoin Indian camp before Zimbabwe match A day ago, Rinku Singh had rushed back home after his father was admitted to a hospital, reportedly due to liver cancer. That had left his participation against Zimbabwe in doubt, but Kotak confirmed that the left-hander would rejoin the camp this evening. Sitanshu Kotak backs Tilak, Abhishek amid form slump One of India's underperformers with the bat has been Tilak Varma. The left-hander, who cemented the number three spot for himself in the Indian batting order, has managed just 107 runs in five matches while striking at 118.88. Kotak backed Tilak amid his form slump and said that there were no problems with the way he has played so far. He also backed Abhishek Sharma who could score just 15 against South Africa, a match where he broke his streak of three ducks. "There are no issues with how Tilak is batting. He batted well against Pakistan. For Tilak, it is a matter of two boundaries (on his strike rate). There's no concern about his run-a-ball innings. There is no tension regarding Abhishek, Tilak or even the loss against SA," he said. On Abhishek's form slump, Kotak added, “I never liked overthinking about one individual as we are playing with two all-rounders and six batters.” India's batting struggled big-time on a black soil pitch at the Narendra Modi Stadium against South Africa, but Kotak brushed aside all such concerns. He explained, "I don't think we struggle on black soil. If pitches become slow in T20, batting becomes a struggle. If there's a collapse, we can't blame the surface. We have done reasonably well, there isn't much concern."

stories.title: Congress protests across UP in Shankaracharya's support:Party accuses BJP govt of targeting religious leaders and traditions
stories.summary: The Congress party has launched statewide protests in support of Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand following the filing of an FIR against him. Demonstrations were held across several cities in Uttar Pradesh, including Varanasi, Agra, Lucknow, Meerut, Bulandshahr, Gorakhpur, Lalitpur and Gonda. Party leaders and workers staged demonstrations against the government, raising slogans and performing symbolic ‘shankhnaad’ (conch blowing) as a warning. In several locations, minor scuffles were reported between protesters and police. Protests across major cities In Agra, Congress workers waved posters of the Shankaracharya while protesting. In Lucknow, demonstrators marched and submitted a memorandum to the District Magistrate. Similar protests were organised in Meerut, Bulandshahr, Gorakhpur and Lalitpur, where party members raised slogans criticising the state government. During the protests, Congress leaders alleged that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government was ‘anti-Hindu’. One leader remarked that the government was not merely confronting a Shankaracharya but was ‘tampering with a nuclear bomb’, suggesting the gravity of the issue. The student wing, the National Students' Union of India (NSUI), installed a hoarding in Lucknow targeting Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, referring to him by his birth name, Ajay Singh Bisht. The hoarding read: ‘Sanatan opponent Ajay Singh Bisht, when destruction befalls a man, wisdom dies first.’ Demand for judicial scrutiny Congress leaders demanded that the background of those who lodged the FIR against the Shankaracharya be investigated by a retired High Court judge. They argued that only an independent and transparent inquiry would bring out the truth and safeguard the dignity of religious traditions. According to party representatives, a fair probe is essential to ensure that members of the saint community are not subjected to unjust treatment under the pretext of legal proceedings. Memorandum submitted in Gonda In Gonda, Congress workers staged a protest at the Collectorate premises and submitted a memorandum addressed to the Prime Minister in support of the Shankaracharya. Former district Congress president Pramod Mishra stated that alleged misconduct against the saint community in the name of an FIR should be stopped with immediate effect. He called for the FIR to be withdrawn to prevent what he described as the humiliation of religious leaders. Demonstration and slogans in Bulandshahr In Bulandshahr, Congress workers gathered to protest against the FIR and attempted to gherao the Collectorate. Protesters sat on the road as a mark of dissent and later submitted a memorandum addressed to the Prime Minister through the Additional District Magistrate. During the demonstration, slogans of ‘Yogi government down, down’ were raised, reflecting anger against the state administration. The Congress has indicated that it will continue its agitation until its demands for an impartial inquiry and withdrawal of the FIR are addressed.

stories.title: Son says ‘sorry’ after killing father:Pathology lab owner’s plastic-wrapped body cremated in Lucknow; nephew performs last rites
stories.summary: The cremation of Lucknow’s well-known pathology owner, Manvendra Singh, was performed on the sixth day after his murder. On Wednesday morning, his nephew Kritya Singh carried out the last rites at Bhainsakund Ghat’s Vaikunth Dham, as his son Akshat, the accused in the case, remains in jail. Manvendra was murdered on February 20 at around 4:30 am. According to police, his son shot him in the head, then beheaded him and dumped the severed head in a nearby forest. The final rites were conducted on February 25 in the presence of family members and relatives. Following ritual traditions, the priest had the nephew take the son’s oath before performing the ceremonies. Nephew Kritya Singh, younger brother Arvind Singh and other relatives were present at the cremation ground. The deceased’s elderly father, Surendra Pal Singh, could not attend due to his fragile condition. During the funeral, the cover over the body was not removed. Ritual bathing was performed from above, and relatives placed the funeral wood. Nephew Kritya then lit the pyre and performed the final rites, circling the pyre as per tradition. The atmosphere turned emotional as Manvendra’s brother Arvind Singh broke down in grief during the cremation. See 5 photos Read complete story Manvendra Singh (49) lived in L sector of Ashiana. He had been missing since February 20. His 21-year-old son Akshat Pratap Singh, who was studying B.Com, had filed a missing person report. Investigation revealed that Akshat himself committed the murder. When police interrogated him, he confessed to the murder. Based on his information, Manvendra's body was found in a blue drum in a room of the house on February 23. Both his hands and feet were missing. He had cut them off and thrown them in Sadrauna about 21 kilometers away. Akshat's sister is an 11th grade student. She was also present at the time of the incident.

stories.title: UP BJP announces 200 mandal presidents:Teases party worker about money spent on 'gamcha'; shares light hearted moment with supporters
stories.summary: UP BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary told his party workers that with elections approaching, everyone will get work, and there is work for all. On Wednesday in Lucknow, a large number of party workers came to meet him. One worker welcomed him by draping a saffron gamcha. After the welcome, Chaudhary said, “Why spend money on this? The 150–200 rupees you spent could have been useful to you.” Another worker gifted him a bulldozer. Seeing it, Pankaj smiled and remarked, “You have brought the entire bulldozer!” The BJP has already begun the process of forming its new state executive. After meeting the top leadership, the newly elected state president has started assembling his new team. Leaders, office-bearers, and workers from across the state are arriving to register their presence and stake their claim for a position in the new team. Women workers also arrived to demand positions A large number of women workers also came to meet State President Pankaj Chaudhary. They met him personally to claim positions in the new executive. New executive will be announced after Holi A major organisational reshuffle in the BJP’s UP unit is expected after Holi. The first round of deliberations regarding Pankaj Chaudhary’s new team has been completed, but issues of caste and regional balance remain unresolved. The final decision will be made only after a second round of meetings from Lucknow to Delhi.

stories.title: IT raid at Lucknow home of BSP MLA:Officials arrive as wedding guests; minister alleges cancer claim, hints at political vendetta
stories.summary: The Income Tax Department conducted a raid at the residence of Umashankar Singh, the sole Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) MLA in Lucknow. Over three dozen officials arrived at his home, accompanied by a strong police presence. Documents at the residence were examined, creating a stir in political circles. Team conducted early morning raid The IT team reached the MLA’s residence around 7 a.m. and immediately cordoned off the premises, restricting movement in and out. Sources say the team of around 30 officials, supported by local police, is scrutinising documents related to financial transactions and property. The department has not issued an official statement regarding the raid. Officers engaged in scrutinizing documents During the operation, officials began examining files, electronic devices, and other records inside the house. The raid is expected to continue for several hours. Security personnel have been stationed outside, and media access has been restricted. MLA is suffering from cancer Umashankar Singh is reportedly suffering from cancer, which has raised concern among his supporters regarding the ongoing raid. The investigation is continuing in the presence of family members and close aides. Singh is the only BSP MLA elected in 2022, making this Income Tax operation politically significant. Opposition parties are closely watching the developments.

stories.title: Roadways contractual staff rally in Lucknow:Protest over 13 demands, rally from Swasthya Bhawan crossing to DM office
stories.summary: Contractual employees of the Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation held a strong protest in the state capital on Tuesday. Workers marched on foot from Swasthya Bhawan crossing to the District Magistrate’s office and submitted a memorandum to the administration listing their 13 demands. During the protest, employees raised slogans against the government and transport corporation administration, saying their demands have long been ignored, which has caused anger among staff. Traffic was affected for some time due to the march. Job security, salary disparity and regularization are main demands Contractual workers said they have served in Roadways for years but neither receive facilities equal to permanent staff nor parity in pay scales. Protesters demanded an end to the contract system and the start of a regularisation process. The memorandum also included demands for salary hikes, payment of pending dues, service security, improved duty hours and access to social security schemes. Demand for concrete decision on 13-point charter Employees made it clear that their agitation is peaceful, but if no positive decision is taken soon, the movement will be intensified. After the protest, a delegation submitted the memorandum at the DM office, urging government intervention. Workers said they are ready for talks with the government, but their issues should be resolved within a fixed timeframe. Memorandum submitted to administration Officials at the DM office accepted the memorandum and assured that it would be forwarded to the government level. For now, employees warned that if demands are not met, a larger state-wide agitation will be launched.

stories.title: Groom survives after car plunges into pond:Baraat delayed 2 hours; guests seen drying clothes at venue
stories.summary: In Chandauli, a speeding car carrying a teacher groom lost control and fell into a pond. The groom, two girls, and a relative were inside. The groom managed to swim out, while locals helped rescue the other three. The accident occurred about 300 metres from the wedding venue. Due to the incident, the wedding procession started two hours late. The groom later rode a horse carriage and reached the lawn at 11 pm, where the rituals were completed. The family said the groom’s ₹75,000 smartphone, gold chain, and ring also fell into the pond. The driver fled after the incident. See pictures of the incident... Read the full matter... Pawan Kumar Prajapati (34), son of Ramnaresh Prajapati from Bairi village under Chakia police station limits, works as a lecturer at Alert Polytechnic College in Prayagraj. His marriage had been fixed with Shalu, the third daughter of Jawahir alias Lakhendra Prajapati from Hasanpur village under Baburi police station. Shalu is a graduate, her two brothers are teachers in a convent school, and her father is a farmer. The wedding was scheduled at a lawn in Baburi. The procession left the groom’s house for Baburi. Pawan was travelling in a Swift car along with two girls from the family and a relative, seated in the front. On the way, the driver stopped and drank alcohol. In an intoxicated state, he began driving at high speed. The car went out of control, and the driver jumped out while it was still moving. The vehicle fell into the pond and began sinking. The driver-side door was open, allowing Pawan to escape. He swam about 20–25 metres to reach safety. Vehicles carrying other members of the procession were behind the groom’s car. With help from locals, they rescued the girls and the relative. No one was injured. The bride’s family arrived soon after being informed. If the gate driver hadn't opened the gate, it would have been a major accident When the car veered off the road, the driver opened his door and jumped. As the car fell into the pond, it slowly sank into deeper water. The groom exited through the open door, and within two minutes the vehicle’s wheels were completely submerged. Later that night, a crane was used to pull the car out. Changed clothes in another car and arrived The incident occurred around 9 pm Tuesday. The groom was shifted to another vehicle, given fresh clothes, and taken to the venue. He then wore his sherwani and the procession resumed. He set out on the carriage at 11 pm. Clothes kept in the car were soaked, so guests dried them under fans in a room at the lawn. Father said - driver was under influence of alcohol The groom’s father, Ramnaresh Prajapati, said he was travelling in another vehicle. He alleged that the driver taking the groom was intoxicated, which caused the car to plunge into the pond near Baburi town. In the accident, the groom’s ₹75,000 smartphone, gold chain, and ring were lost in the water. The groom’s elder brother, Chandrabhan Kumar Prajapati, said the driver had been told not to drink, but he still drove under the influence. Baburi station in-charge Vibhuti Narayan Rai confirmed that although the car fell into the pond, all occupants were rescued safely.

stories.title: Ashutosh Maharaj says, 'Deputy CM involved in Magh Mela conspiracy':Allegations confirmed in child abuse case, Shankaracharya rejects involvement
stories.summary: Ashutosh Maharaj, who filed the case alleging sexual abuse of children against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand, addressed the media in Prayagraj on Wednesday evening. He claimed that Avimukteshwaranand sexually exploited young disciples (batuks) at monasteries and ashrams in Madhya Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and Varanasi, asserting that he possesses evidence and that medical reports confirm abuse. He said justice would be delivered soon. Ashutosh Maharaj also accused a Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh of orchestrating a conspiracy during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj, though he did not name anyone. He alleged that several Samajwadi Party and Congress leaders visited the Shankaracharya’s camp and questioned whether their roles were being investigated. He further claimed the Deputy CM had advised protesters to continue demonstrations until his arrival. In response, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand held a press conference in Varanasi and rejected the allegations. He said the child cited in the medical claims never came to his camp and argued that his legal team has presented evidence showing the children were not under his care. He maintained that if any wrongdoing occurred, it must have happened where the children were staying, adding that the complainant would come under scrutiny during the investigation. Earlier on Wednesday morning, the Shankaracharya told the media that Hinduism faces threats from people who merely adopt its appearance without following its values. He questioned why, if abuse had affected more students as claimed, only two cases had been filed, suggesting a conspiracy behind the allegations. Meanwhile, Prayagraj police have been stationed in Varanasi for the past three days and may question the Shankaracharya, though they have not yet visited the ashram. Sources say investigators are gathering evidence and proceeding cautiously due to the high-profile nature of the case. It is believed that questioning will take place only after thorough preparation. The Indian National Congress has come out in support of the Shankaracharya and announced protests in all 75 districts of Uttar Pradesh backing him. Know complete matter A dispute reportedly arose between the Shankaracharya and the administration on Mauni Amavasya, January 18, during the Prayagraj Magh Mela. Eight days later, on January 24, Ashutosh Maharaj, a disciple of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, submitted a complaint to the Police Commissioner, alleging incidents of child sexual abuse during Magh Mela-2026 and Mahakumbh-2025. On February 8, a petition was filed in the Special POCSO Court, alleging inaction by the police. Subsequently, two children were produced before the court on February 13, and their statements were formally recorded on February 21. Following court directions, an FIR was registered the same day at Jhunsi Police Station. The FIR named the Shankaracharya, his disciple Mukundanand, and two to three unidentified individuals as accused. On February 24, the Shankaracharya accused Prayagraj Additional Commissioner Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring against him. He also filed an anticipatory bail petition before the Allahabad High Court.

stories.title: Stepmother kills 3-year-old girl in Gorakhpur:Married a month ago, says husband’s fondness for child triggered act
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, a stepmother allegedly killed her three-year-old stepdaughter with an axe. She first threw the child to the ground and then attacked her, leading to the girl’s death. Blood spread across the room after the incident, staining the walls. During this time, the child’s father reached the spot and screamed on seeing the body. The woman tried to flee, and the father chased her shouting. Hearing the noise, nearby residents also ran after her and caught her after about one kilometre. Her hands and feet were tied with a rope. When asked why she killed the child, she allegedly said that her husband loved the girl more and she wanted to teach him a lesson. Police reached the scene after being informed, arrested the accused woman and recovered the axe used in the crime. The incident took place around 11 pm on Tuesday in Bijhara village of Pipraich. Now read the complete sequence of events- Triveni Maurya (40) lives in Bijhara village. He married Laxmi in 2012. Laxmi died two years ago, and they had a three-year-old daughter, Aditi. A month ago, Triveni married Pooja (35) as his second wife. Since then, the three had been living together in the village house. Triveni loved his daughter deeply, which Pooja reportedly disliked. Triveni said, “On Tuesday night, Pooja, Aditi and I were sleeping. I went outside to urinate. During that time, my wife carried out the act.” He said Pooja threw the sleeping child from the bed to the floor, picked up an axe kept nearby and attacked her neck, killing her on the spot. The father added that he could not believe someone could do such a thing to a small child. Villagers chased and caught the accused woman Triveni said that when he returned and saw the scene, he screamed. Seeing him, Pooja tried to run away. He chased her shouting, and villagers joined in and caught her after running some distance. They then tied her with a rope. Villagers handed over the accused to police On receiving information, Pipraich station in-charge Atul Kumar Srivastava reached the spot with a police team. Villagers handed the accused over to them. Police detained her and, based on her indication, recovered the axe used in the killing. Station in-charge Atul Kumar Srivastava said that- The accused woman has been arrested. The girl's body has been sent for postmortem. Police are now investigating every aspect of this case so that the accused can be given the strictest punishment.

stories.title: Vandalism erupts at Kanpur’s PSIT College:BCA student dies after crashing into JCB on campus; hundreds of students protest for justice
stories.summary: Students created a ruckus on Wednesday morning at PSIT Engineering College in Panki, Kanpur. Hundreds entered the campus and vandalised property, breaking doors, windows and tables. The protest follows the death of a final-year BCA student on Monday after his bike collided with a JCB engaged in construction work on campus. The impact was severe, causing fatal internal injuries. Students have been raising slogans demanding justice. Students allege the accident happened due to lack of safety arrangements during ongoing construction work inside the campus. The college management, however, claimed the incident took place outside the campus. The deceased was identified as Prakhar Singh, a resident of Ratanlal Nagar. Know the full matter Prakhar could not see anything in the dust cloud Prabhakar Singh, a fertiliser trader from Ratanlal Nagar, has a family comprising his wife Priyanka and two sons—Prakhar Singh (21) and Praveen Singh. Cousin Abhay Singh, a resident of Keshavpuram, said Prakhar was a final-year BCA student at PSIT College, while Praveen is pursuing BTech from Chandigarh University in Lucknow. According to him, Prakhar had gone to college on his bike as usual on Monday. At around 5 pm after classes, he was exiting through the rear gate of the college. Construction work had been going on for a long time in that part of the campus. A car passed at high speed in front of his bike, raising a cloud of dust. Because of this he could not see ahead and crashed into a stationary JCB, suffering serious injuries. Doctors declared dead at 2 AM Fellow students rushed him to BMC Hospital in Kalyanpur, from where he was referred onward. The family then took him to Regency Hospital in Sarvodaya Nagar, where doctors declared him dead at about 2 am during treatment. Meanwhile, PSIT Group Director Prof. Manmohan Shukla denied that such an incident occurred inside the campus. He stated that the accident took place about 200 metres away from the college.

stories.title: Yogi welcomed with 'tilak' in Japan:Urges business leaders to invest in UP, says challenges match opportunities
stories.summary: CM Yogi has reached Japan. On Wednesday, he took part in the ‘UP Investment Roadshow’ in Tokyo, the capital of Japan. He interacted with investors. Addressing them, he mentioned the vast possibilities in UP. He invited Japanese investors to come to UP. He said— the number of challenges in Uttar Pradesh is matched by the number of opportunities. Yogi said— under PM Modi’s leadership, India-Japan relations have strengthened. UP is the country’s largest state by population. The bigger the population, the bigger the challenges, and equally greater the opportunities. We have been working for nine years to bring these possibilities onto the ground. He said— UP has established itself as one of the fastest-growing states in India. It has succeeded in tripling its economy and per capita income. Once considered a BIMARU state in India’s economy, UP today stands as an engine of the country’s economy. Yogi said— come, invest in UP’s safe environment and fulfil your dream of taking your business to new heights. We and our government are ready to welcome you to our state. Key points from Yogi's address- 1. Began speech by mentioning Lord Ram and Buddha Yogi said— I bow to the Land of the Rising Sun. The relationship between India and Japan begins with the first ray of the sun and connects with Uttar Pradesh, the capital of the Suryavansh, through a bond of warmth. I have come among you to strengthen that connection. I have come to take forward the heights India is achieving under PM Modi’s leadership. I am here to highlight UP’s role in further strengthening India-Japan bilateral relations. He said— UP is the sacred birthplace of Lord Ram. It is also the holy land of Lord Buddha. His kingdom Kapilvastu is in UP. The sacred land where he delivered his first sermon, Sarnath, is in UP. Shravasti, associated with Chaturmas, is in UP. Kushinagar, where he attained Mahaparinirvana, is also in UP. Today, work is being advanced on the Ramayana and Buddhist circuits to promote spiritual tourism in UP. Whenever Lord Ram and Buddha are discussed, both are linked to that great Suryavansh tradition whose first ray of sun the people of Japan always await. 2. 56% of UP’s 25-crore population is working He said— the population is large, but UP’s land is equally fertile. Only 11% of India’s cultivable land is in UP, yet the state produces 21% of the country’s food grains. UP has emerged as India’s food basket. There are possibilities for value addition in this field. From seed to market, new work can be done in packaging. Work is being done on logistics and warehousing opportunities. UP is also the state with the highest water resources in India. These can be used in agriculture and in producing green hydrogen. Yogi said 1. Of UP’s 25-crore population, 56% are working people. They are young. There is skilled manpower available for work in any field. Affordable and good manpower is available in UP today. 2. For this, UP worked on infrastructure. Many expressways have been built in nine years. 95% of the country’s expressways are in UP. The state has the largest rail network. Work has begun on developing 27 industrial parks. I invite Japan’s business leaders to come to UP and contribute to advancing private industrial parks. 3. The success UP has achieved in air connectivity has no parallel. In the last nine years, we have operated 16 domestic and 4 international airports. India’s largest airport in Noida is going to become operational very soon. 3. Many Investment Opportunities in UP Yogi said— there are immense possibilities for investment in UP. Many Japanese companies have invested in the state. Whoever has invested in UP has felt not only that their investment is safe in a secure environment, but has also worked to expand their business with new hopes for a bright future. We have more than 34 sectoral policies. 55% of mobile manufacturing is done in UP alone. 60% of electronic components are manufactured in UP. Proposals have been received for setting up data centres. Recently, the foundation stone of a semiconductor unit was laid. We have come here to further these sectoral possibilities and seek your cooperation. 4. UP's ability to transform scale into skill He said— UP has a safe environment, scale, and the capability to convert that scale into skill. There is stability and speed— you will find all this in UP. You will get a sufficient young workforce. There is no problem. Four-lane connectivity for industrial parks and adequate energy supply are available in UP today. There is a land bank of 75,000 acres. Along with NCR and expressways, a new industrial city named BIDA has been launched near Jhansi in Bundelkhand over 56,000 acres. 5. Received investment proposals worth 40 lakh crore from domestic and international investors Yogi said— improved law and order resulted in the Global Investors Summit held in 2023. In it, UP received investment proposals worth ₹40 lakh crore from investors across the country and the world. Proposals worth ₹15 lakh crore have already been implemented on the ground. Proposals worth ₹7 lakh crore are in the pipeline. These will also be brought to ground level in the groundbreaking ceremony. UP has the largest base of MSMEs. There are 96,000 units. More than 3 crore people are working. They have been kept free from every NOC for 1,000 days. The government is supporting them at every level.

stories.title: ‘What is your rate?’ Singer lashes out on hearing remark:Throws sandal at anchor during Gorakhpur live show; says he also commented on her body
stories.summary: A Bhojpuri singer has accused a stage anchor of using obscene language and insulting her during a wedding event in Gorakhpur. The singer, Nisha Upadhyay, said the anchor asked her, “What is your rate?” and also made comments about her body and singing. She claimed she had ignored his behaviour earlier, but this time she could not tolerate it. The incident took place on February 21 at a reception programme held at the Railway Officers Club. According to Nisha, she was getting ready for her live performance when the anchor made the remark about her rate. She said this angered her, and she went on stage during the show and hit him with her sandal. The anchor, Golu Raja alias Mukesh Rai, also tried to attack the singer. People present at the function stepped in and stopped both of them. A video of the incident later surfaced on social media. Speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, Nisha said the anchor had been using abusive words on stage and had crossed all limits with his comments. She said both she and the audience felt insulted. On Tuesday, the singer filed a complaint with Gorakhpur SP City Abhinav Tyagi. She accused the anchor of abusing her and giving her death threats. The SP has ordered an investigation into the matter. What Nisha said about the incident, read Nisha Upadhyay told Bhaskar- On February 21st in Gorakhpur, Grijesh Shukla ji had a reception for his daughter. Other artists were also present there. Mukesh Rai, a resident of Ara district, was hosting the stage. He started using obscene words on stage, which made me angry. Currently, I have come to SP City Sir's office. I am confident that the police will help me. I am also being continuously threatened. They will get me killed, they will have me murdered, they will show me my place. Regarding acquaintance with the anchor, she said- Nisha Upadhyay said- I knew him before. We used to meet on stage at programs frequently. I have seen him do this with others many times. It has also happened once or twice that I was not on stage, but he commented on my body, my marriage, and my singing. I don't know what problem he has with me that he keeps doing this to me. I just want the police to fully help me on the land of Baba Gorakhnath, under Yogi's rule. Now read the matter A video of Bhojpuri singer Nisha Upadhyay had surfaced, in which she is seen hitting the anchor with a sandal during a live show. The incident began when the anchor said from the stage, "Now it's the turn of our dear Nisha Didi. Clap loudly and yes Didi, what is today's rate? One song 10 thousand, 2 songs 20 thousandor something else?" As soon as she heard this, Nisha Upadhyay got furious and took off her sandal and ran to hit the anchor. She angrily said - Will he tell my rate? Give me the mic, I will tell his rate. I will hit him, who is he to tell the rate? During this, the anchor started running away from there. However, after some time, the people present there intervened and took the singer off the stage and sent her to the hotel room. This video of Nisha Upadhyay is going viral on social media. In the video, Nisha is seen wearing a blue colored saree. She is standing angrily on stage with a sandal in her hand. Meanwhile, the anchor is trying to escape. People on social media are now divided into 2 groups - some are calling it Nisha's right move, while others say she should have maintained her dignity. All about Nisha Upadhyay Nisha Upadhyay is a well-known Bhojpuri singer from Gaur Basant village in Saran district, Bihar. She is highly appreciated for her stage performances due to her distinctive voice. An FIR was also lodged against her for gathering a crowd and breaking COVID protocols during a cultural program in the Corona period. She also has a strong fan following on social media, where she often shares videos of her shows and rehearsals. She has 478K followers on Instagram. Nisha Upadhyay has two brothers in her family. Not much information about other family members or her personal life is publicly available. She keeps a very low profile regarding her private life. Nisha has not yet made any relationship public. She is currently living a single life.

stories.title: 59% marriages break due to cheating:9 of 100 marriages fail in Uttar Pradesh; couple took divorce over pet dog
stories.summary: Reports of marriages breaking, divorces, and couples separating surface daily from Uttar Pradesh. Sometimes domestic disputes, sometimes affairs, and sometimes mutual disagreements are cited as reasons. The question is whether this is limited to a few personal cases or whether broken marriages are slowly becoming a social crisis. How many people in India are divorced? Why are divorce cases rising? Is the law capable of saving marriages? Where does India stand globally in divorce rates? Read this report for answers to all these questions. First read this case On 18 February in Fatehpur, UP, bride Tanu called off her wedding because a member of the groom’s procession kicked her pet dog. The couple had already married in an Arya Samaj temple and had also registered their court marriage. The social wedding ceremony was scheduled for 18 February. After the garland exchange, during rituals, the dog-kicking incident sparked a dispute that later turned into a physical fight. Several people were injured in the chaos. The bride’s finger was also fractured. Despite police persuasion, she remained firm on cancelling the marriage. The bride sent back the procession simply because a wedding guest kicked her pet dog. Why are relationships breaking so quickly these days? Lucknow-based relationship expert Deepak Verma says the biggest reason is ego problems. People are unwilling to tolerate each other. Women do not want to listen to men, and men are not ready to understand women. He says the younger generation does not want to follow traditional values and rules. Many people imagine marriage like films and dreams. But when reality appears, they find it difficult to handle relationships. Verma believes social media contributes nearly 95% to this trend. People try to manage relationships by watching TV serials, reels, and social media content. They begin living in a reel-like world, while failing to accept real-life responsibilities. When desires are not fulfilled, the result appears in the form of divorce, separation, and broken relationships. He adds that earlier people tried to maintain relationships by adjusting to circumstances, but now anger, ego, and hasty decisions are breaking them. How many divorced people are there in India? According to the 2011 Census, more than 13.62 lakh people in India were divorced, which is 0.11% of the total population. Surprisingly, the number of divorced women was almost double that of men. At that time, 4.52 lakh men were divorced, whereas more than 9.09 lakh women were in this category. Even more surprising, the number of people living separately after marriage was three times higher than divorced individuals. More than 35.35 lakh people were living apart from their spouse, and women again formed the majority. Around 24 lakh women were living separately from their husbands. Another striking figure shows that villages had more divorced people than cities. Cities had 5.04 lakh divorced individuals, while villages had over 8.58 lakh. Additionally, about 24 lakh people in villages were living separately from their spouse. At what age do most divorces occur? Between 2021 and 2022, a National Family and Health Survey study found that people aged 25–34 accounted for the highest number of divorces nationwide. They were followed by those aged 18–24, then 35–44, and then 45–54. The list also included people aged 55–64 and above. According to a Mumbai Family Court study, 40% of marriages break within three years. Most women seeking divorce are aged between 25 and 34. Another study shows divorce petitions peak in January, September, and May, while October–November, December, and March see the lowest numbers. Reasons cited include festivals, children’s holidays, and summer court vacations. What are the psychological reasons for frequently changing relationships? Psychiatrist Dr Amit Shahi from Gorakhpur District Hospital says fear of commitment, emotional insecurity, and unrealistic expectations are major reasons. Ego, lack of patience, and trauma from past relationships also increase instability. Because of social media and too many options, people start comparing, making it harder to sustain stable relationships. Patience is essential in relationships Psychologist Dr Priyanka Gautam from Deen Dayal Upadhyay Gorakhpur University says marriage is not just a union of two people but a deep bond between two hearts. Patience and understanding are most important. Husbands and wives should communicate openly, celebrate small joys together, and make time for each other. Saying sorry and thank you in a relationship is not weakness but a way to strengthen love and trust. How much is social media affecting relationships? Dr Gautam says social media itself is not bad, but excessive and uncontrolled use is creating challenges in relationships. When people spend more time on phones and social platforms, face-to-face conversation and emotional depth decline, increasing emotional and physical distance. Talking to others online, likes and comments, or secret chats can create suspicion, jealousy, and distrust. Seeing others’ “perfect” lives leads to comparison, dissatisfaction, and psychological stress like depression. Social media is not the enemy of relationships, but when it becomes central to life, real-world relationships weaken. Can couple counselling save relationships? Dr Amit Shahi says if counselling is done at the right time, relationships can be saved. It helps couples understand each other, express emotions openly, and discuss problems. He says counselling is effective in removing ego, misunderstandings, and communication gaps. It allows couples to realise that the problem is not the partner but the situation. What does BHU's research say about marriage breakdown? In October 2025, three professors from Banaras Hindu University revealed findings after six months of research. They said mismatched horoscopes were a major reason behind marital breakdowns. The research involved Professors Vinay Pandey, Ashutosh Tripathi, and Amit Kumar Mishra, along with researcher Ganesh Prasad and Nepalese PhD scholar Rodna Ghinre. It found that 37% of marriages break because horoscopes of bride and groom are not properly matched. According to the study, marriages are conducted despite planetary defects, which later cause serious conflicts. In such cases, some couples enter love affairs, seek new partners, and in some instances situations escalate to crime. Prof Vinay Pandey said matching 32 qualities between bride and groom does not guarantee favourable planetary positions. If planets are imbalanced, the marriage later becomes unstable. He added that cases have emerged in UP and other states where husbands and wives have killed each other in extremely brutal ways, which he described as shocking. Do planetary defects really affect married life? According to BHU astrologer Prof Vinay Pandey, astrology evaluates both nature and tendencies. During horoscope matching, compatibility for marriage is assessed by analysing charts, planetary positions, and defects. Many people believe that Mars defects, weak Venus, or other planetary unfavourable positions can affect married life. Astrology links such combinations to delays, tension, or conflict in marriage. However, relationship experts believe planetary defects are only a possible factor, not decisive. Real impact usually comes from lack of communication, ego, excessive expectations, and social and psychological factors such as social media influence. While believers attribute conflict to planetary defects, sociologists and psychologists consider it linked to lifestyle and mindset. What does the law say about divorce? The Hindu Marriage Act applies to Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, and Buddhists. Section 13 provides for divorce and lists the grounds. If a couple wants divorce by mutual consent, Section 13B applies. Under this, an application can be filed only after at least one year of marriage. Usually, family courts grant six months for reconsideration and reconciliation. If no settlement occurs, divorce is granted. However, the Supreme Court has clarified that if a marriage has completely broken down and there is no chance of reconciliation, the six-month waiting period can be waived. This means waiting is not mandatory for mutual consent divorce.

stories.title: Another ‘blue drum’ murder case in UP:Son enjoys chicken paneer dish with sister after killing father; planned to burn body in container
stories.summary: A sensational twist has emerged in the murder of a well-known pathology lab owner in Lucknow. Police say the victim, Manvendra Singh, who ran Vardhman Pathology, was planning to remarry. His children were reportedly unhappy with the decision. Investigators believe this led to his murder, after which his body was hidden inside a blue drum. During questioning, the main accused, 21-year-old son Akshat Pratap Singh alias Raja, allegedly confessed to the crime. Police said that after killing his father, he and his sister went to their aunt’s house and asked her to cook chicken and paneer curry for them. Later, he returned home and had food sitting near his father’s body. According to the police, the siblings tried to act normal to avoid suspicion. The sister, Kriti, continued to attend her exams. The accused told officers that he bought a saw and a blue drum to dispose off the body. They also kept visiting their aunt, Namrata, so that she would not enter the room where the body was kept. Police are now closely examining the sister’s role in the case. Investigators suspect she may also have been involved in the murder of their father. First, read what Akshat told the police during interrogation Planned all night During police interrogation, Akshat revealed - I stayed awake all night planning my father's murder. On February 20, around 4:30 AM, I shot my sleeping father in the chest with a licensed rifle. I stood there until my father's breathing stopped. I watched him suffer with my own eyes. When my father died, I planned to dispose of the body. I moved his body from the third floor to the bathroom of a ground-floor room. Couldn't cut the torso into two pieces, so stuffed it in a drum After that, he bought a saw and a blue drum. He cut off the hands and feet with the saw in the bathroom. During this, he had kept the tap open to drain off the blood. After cutting off the hands and feet, he put them in a polythene bag and threw them about 20 kilometers away in Sadrauna, Kakori. He tried to cut the torso into two parts, but couldn't. He stuffed it in a drum and kept it. After that, he planned to burn it with turpentine oil. For this, he bought 10 liters of turpentine oil. He was planning to take the torso somewhere far away and burn it, but was caught before that. To mislead he had switched on his father's phone in Kakori In order to evade the police, Akshat went to Kakori on February 20. There, he turned on his phone so that his last location would be Kakori and not his home. Neighbor Alpana Singh said that they came to know that Manvendra had not been seen since February 20. When my husband and several others asked Akshat, he said that father had gone to Delhi. Later, it was found that he had gone missing. His location was found to be Kakori. After this, everyone went to Kakori with Akshat looking for him. They were not found there. After this, everyone returned. The motive.... Father's strictness and displeasure with parties Police investigation also reveals that Manvendra was fond of parties. Before the murder, around 1:30 AM on the night of February 20, Manvendra had messaged an acquaintance to arrange a party. His two children were upset with their father's partying. Mother had committed suicide The investigation revealed that about seven years ago, Manvendra's wife had committed suicide. After that incident, the responsibility of the house completely fell on Manvendra. After his wife's death, Manvendra was raising his son Akshat and daughter Kriti alone. Manvendra lived in his house with his son Akshat, daughter Kriti, brother Arun, his wife Namrata, and their two children. Everyone's food was cooked together. Manvendra lived on the third floor with his daughter and son. His brother's family lives on the second floor. The ground floor room is used as a guest room. Reports of displeasure emerging due to discussions about Manvendra's second marriage Local people say that about a month ago, Manvendra was preparing to go on a Vaishno Devi tour. During this time, a bracelet, 2 rings, and other items were stolen from the house. Manvendra had accused the maid and complained to the police. The police investigation found that the maid was not the accused in the theft. Meanwhile, the maid also filed a report against Manvendra. After this, Manvendra had tightened security at his house. After this, the items were found. People say that after this, Manvendra started acting strict at home. It is also discussed that during this time, he had also sought advice from a friend in the neighborhood about getting married again. He used to talk to people in the neighborhood about this. Akshat also used to be upset by this. Change in brother-sister's behavior a week ago Local people said that for about a week, there was a change in the behavior of both the brother and sister. Both of them spent more time together. The uncle had gone to the village. In such a situation, there was an aunt and her two children at home. Akshat spoke limitedly with them. His conversations with his grandfather (Baba) were also formal and occasional. Akshat used to run a branch of Vardhman Lab, wanted to grab the property Vardhman Pathology has labs in several districts. Manvendra Singh used to operate them with other business partners. He had given the responsibility of operating the Vardhman Lab located in Kakori to his son Akshat alias Raja. From this, he used to cover his expenses. However, he wanted to do another business instead of the lab. Manvendra was strict about this. Manvendra Singh also operated 2 liquor shops. Two mobile towers are also installed on the roof of his house in Ashiana. Rent also comes from them. Akshat wanted to grab the entire property. Now know how Akshat behaved after the murder was revealed.... Akshat entered the house, avoiding eye contact with people On February 24, when the police brought the accused son Akshat home, all eyes were fixed on him. He went inside, avoiding people's gaze. According to the people present nearby, there were no signs of worry or remorse on his face. People say that about 3 years ago, Manvendra sent about 5 lakh rupees to the accounts of his son Akshat and daughter Kriti. After this, Akshat ran away from home after writing a 6-page letter. He had written that he would now do business. Dad, don't try to find us. After this, the family contacted his friends and recovered him from Kanpur. However, Akshat had been clever during this time. When his friends were going to Kanpur with the family to pick him up, he became suspicious. He had video called his friend and seen the scene inside the car, but Akshat's family was in another car, so he couldn't see them. Akshat had given his friend the address in Kanpur. The family, along with the friend, reached him. Now read what the sister revealed... It has come to light during police interrogation that sister Kriti was present in the room at the time of the incident. The incident happened in front of her. Even after Akshat was caught, she kept this information hidden for about 24 hours. The police interrogated Kriti for about 40 minutes and recorded her statement. Investigating officers are trying to find out whether she just remained silent or if she had prior knowledge of any conspiracy. Kriti kept going to give papers According to the police, Kriti stated - After killing Dad, Akshat scared me a lot. He pressured me to do routine tasks so that people wouldn't suspect anything. Out of fear, I went to APS School to take my 11th-grade exam on February 20 and 21. However, local residents and family members said that Kriti is very scared by the incident. She is also not talking much to anyone. She stated that on February 20, she, Dad, and her brother were sleeping in the same room on the third floor. Around 4 AM, Akshat shot Dad. I said, 'Brother, we don't have Mom. You've killed Dad too.' Akshat then threatened her and warned her of death if she told anyone. Frightened, she fell silent. Now read which questions the police are looking for answers to... Police also investigating the role of Kriti and the aunt At the time of the incident, Manvendra's brother's wife Namrata (Akshat's aunt) was on the second floor with her 2 children. Kriti was in the same room where Manvendra was murdered. Therefore, the police are also investigating the role of both of them. Police have also interrogated Kriti for 40 minutes. She has stated that Akshat committed the murder and threatened her. However, the police are not completely satisfied with her statement. Police believe that if Kriti saw the murder happening, how did she go to give both papers? Why didn't she tell any of her friends or teachers at school about it? Because Akshat wasn't even there at that time. Why didn't she call a relative and give this information? Meanwhile, Namrata was on the second floor, so why didn't she hear the gunshot? When the body was taken down the stairs, did not a single drop of blood fall, which Namrata could have seen? When the body was found, it was smelling, so why didn't Namrata feel the smell earlier? The police are looking for answers to all these questions. Now read what the whole matter is Manvendra Singh (49), who lived in Ashiana's L Sector. He had been missing since February 20. His 21-year-old son, Akshat Pratap Singh, who was studying B.Com, had filed a missing person report for him. The investigation revealed that Akshat himself had committed the murder. When the police interrogated him, he confessed to the murder. Based on his confession, Manvendra's body was found on February 23 in a blue drum in a room at home. Both his hands and feet were missing. He had cut them off and thrown them about 21 kilometers away in Sadrauna. Akshat's sister, Kriti, is an 11th-grade student. She was also present at the time of the incident.
