stories.title: ‘Secret rooms in Shankaracharya’s monastery, entry only for women aides’:Ghaziabad author claims presence of swimming pool and vast hidden wealth in ashram
stories.summary: Difficulties continue to mount for Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand. After a case was registered against him under charges of sexual exploitation and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, author Dr Bhumika Dwivedi has come forward with a series of claims regarding him and his Vidyamath in Varanasi. Dr Dwivedi stated that in 2022 she was conducting research in Kashi and Prayagraj. She said she had been encouraged in her research by Avimukteshwaranand’s guru, Shankaracharya Swaroopanand Saraswati. During that period, she stayed at Avimukteshwaranand’s monastery for nearly two months. However, she alleged that what she witnessed inside the premises changed her perception. Claims of Luxury and Restricted Areas According to Dr Dwivedi, instead of the simplicity expected of a spiritual centre, the monastery has extensive luxury amenities, including air conditioning, LED televisions and expensive carpets. She described grand halls and a royal ambience. She alleged that a woman residing there introduced herself as ‘Swamiji’s sakhi’ (female confidante) and appeared to exercise complete control over the premises. She made four major claims- Allegations Regarding Young Disciples Dr Dwivedi further alleged that young batuks from economically disadvantaged backgrounds are made to perform substantial work within the monastery. She claimed that even their belongings are sometimes taken by the manager and cook. She recounted that an eight-year-old batuk refused to be photographed with her, stating that “Swami Shri” had instructed them not to take pictures with outsiders. She also alleged that Avimukteshwaranand had provided several houses to his sisters, based on local accounts, although she acknowledged having no documentary proof. She claimed that significant wealth, including jewels and stored valuables, exists within the monastery. She questioned why access to the highest floor via internal stairs is prohibited and alleged that Avimukteshwaranand travels in a specially designed luxury bus equipped as a vanity van, where he resides. No pressure, says author Dr Dwivedi maintained that she is speaking without any pressure and is recounting only what she personally observed. She also claimed to possess photographs with the sakhi. She further alleged that unlike traditional monasteries, where residents rise at 4am and follow strict discipline, no rigid routine was evident here. Referring to her earlier visit in May 2022, she said Swaroopanand Saraswati’s room had been accessible and filled only with books and scriptures, whereas now everything appears concealed and mysterious. She stated that when she attempted to meet Swaroopanand during her stay, she was informed that he was unwell and undergoing treatment in Bengaluru. Background and response Shankaracharya Swaroopanand Saraswati passed away on 11 September 2022 at the age of 99 at Paramhansi Ganga Ashram in Jhoteshwar, Narsinghpur district, Madhya Pradesh. He had served as Shankaracharya of Dwarka in Gujarat and Jyotir Math in Badrinath. After his death, Avimukteshwaranand was declared head of Jyotish Peeth Badrinath, while Swami Sadanand was appointed to lead Dwarka Sharada Peeth. Responding to the allegations, Avimukteshwaranand stated that he has already performed his own shraddha and pind daan and therefore has no fear. Regarding claims about a 'glass palace' and swimming pool, he said people are venting their frustrations. He added that his guru had constructed a pool for health reasons. On approaching the High Court, he said he feared being arrested and harmed. Concerning the investigation report, he stated that such reports are not made public and are disclosed only through police channels. Dr Bhumika Dwivedi Ashk is a resident of DLF Colony in Ghaziabad and is an author. Her husband is Neelabh Dwivedi, and her father-in-law is the noted Hindi and Urdu writer Upendranath Ashk.

A child touched his feet and recited a Shiva mantra, which Yogi helped complete. He later visited a public school, interacted with students, distributed gifts, and held investor meetings. 3. IT raids BSP MLA’s premises enter second day, ₹1,000 crore tax evasion allegations trigger political row Income Tax Department searches at BSP MLA Umashankar Singh’s premises continued for a second day across Lucknow, Ballia, Sonbhadra, and Kaushambi. The raids relate to alleged ₹1,000 crore tax evasion. BSP chief Mayawati criticised the action, calling it politically motivated, while officials examined documents and electronic records. 4. UPI to debut in Israel: PM Modi says New Delhi, Tel Aviv elevating time-tested ties to special strategic partnership On the second day of his official visit to Israel, Prime Minister Narendra Modi began the day by paying tributes at the Holocaust Memorial Yad Vashem in Jerusalem, honoring the millions of Jews killed during Adolf Hitler’s regime. 5. Shankaracharya’s lawyer gets death threat, Varanasi court bombing warning in SMS Shrinath Tripathi, lawyer of Shankaracharya Swami Avimuktheshwaranand and a member of the Bar Council of India, received an SMS threatening to bomb the Varanasi court and kill him. Police have launched a probe. It is the fourth such threat to the court in 14 days. 6. Chandrashekhar eyes ‘cursed’ Hastinapur seat, constituency’s poll history linked to UP government formation Hastinapur seat has gained attention amid speculation that Nagina MP Chandrashekhar may contest from the constituency. BJP MLA Dinesh Khatik earlier called it “cursed” and hinted at stepping aside. Political observers link the seat’s past winners with parties that later formed the Uttar Pradesh government. 7. Ajit Pawar's nephews demand FIR against DGCA, VSR In connection with the January 28 plane crash that claimed the life of former Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Ajit Pawar, his nephews, Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SCP) MLA Rohit Pawar and Yogendra Pawar, reached Baramati on Thursday morning and approached the Baramati Rural Police Station. 8. Woman constable, 2-year-old son die as car catches fire after dumper crash in Rampur A woman constable and her two-year-old son died after their car caught fire following a dumper collision in Rampur. Her husband and brother-in-law escaped with burns. The constable was trapped while trying to save her child. Police have launched a search for the absconding dumper driver. 9. Lucknow University students protest mess food, law student faints; probe ordered, condition stable Students at Lucknow University staged a protest alleging contaminated mess food after a law student fainted and reported worms in dal. She received medical care and is stable. Authorities have ordered an inquiry, while students demand action against the mess operator. 10. IT Minister bats for fair revenue model for digital creators Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw is pushing for big changes in how online platforms operate. He believes these platforms need to step up and take responsibility for the content that appears on their sites and apps. This isn't just a suggestion; it's a call for a fundamental shift in the digital world.

stories.title: Keshav Prasad Maurya cuts short Germany visit:Returns to Lucknow after failing to secure UK visa clearance
stories.summary: There is major news regarding Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya’s foreign visit. Maurya is returning to Lucknow from Germany after being unable to proceed with his planned visit to the United Kingdom. According to information received, Maurya was part of a delegation led by IT Minister Sunil Sharma, which was scheduled to visit the UK after Germany. However, the delegation could not obtain the required UK visa. Sources said the delegation did not receive the necessary No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Government of India, due to which the UK visa was not granted. As a result, Maurya and the delegation are returning to Lucknow without completing the UK leg of the visit. Deputy Chief Minister Keshav Prasad Maurya and IT Minister Sunil Sharma held meetings with several leading industrial groups and organisations during their visit to Germany and secured important agreements and discussions across key sectors. In the semiconductor and electronics sector, they met with major German semiconductor companies. The Uttar Pradesh government aims to develop the state as India’s ‘semiconductor hub’, and sought German technological support and expertise to achieve this goal. In the defence and aerospace sector, they invited German defence firms to invest in the Uttar Pradesh Defence Industrial Corridor (UP DIC), particularly in areas such as drone manufacturing and advanced defence equipment. They also held discussions with industry leaders at the IHK Frankfurt (Chamber of Commerce and Industry), where talks focused on developing industrial parks and logistics hubs in Uttar Pradesh to strengthen infrastructure and attract global investment. Additionally, discussions were held on adopting Germany’s dual vocational training model in Uttar Pradesh’s technical institutions, with the aim of equipping the state’s youth with industry-relevant skills aligned with global standards. News is being updated…

stories.title: Over 46,000 officers and staff salaries withheld in UP:Govt orders action against employees who skipped mandatory asset disclosure
stories.summary: 46,816 officers and employees in UP will not receive their salary for this month after failing to upload details of their assets on the designated government portal. The state government had directed all employees and officers to submit declarations of their movable and immovable property. The deadline for uploading the information on the Manav Sampada portal was set for 31 January. As the specified employees did not comply, their salaries have been withheld. Chief Secretary S P Goyal has made it clear that salaries will not be released until asset details are uploaded. He also warned that departmental action would follow and vigilance clearance would not be granted. Earlier, on 1 February, salaries of 68,236 state employees had similarly been withheld for non-compliance. Annual property disclosure requirement The state has approximately 1.7 million employees. So far, 1.653 million have submitted their asset declarations. Each year, employees are required to disclose details of their movable and immovable property up to the current financial year by 31 December via the Manav Sampada portal. The government had instructed employees across all 90 departments to comply. The deadline was extended once to 31 January. However, 46,816 officers and employees have still not made their property details public. Promotion and ACP benefits affected Chief Secretary Goyal reiterated that those who failed to submit their declarations by 31 January would face consequences. In addition to salary stoppage, such employees will not be considered for promotion in the current selection year. They will also be denied the benefit of Assured Career Progression (ACP) this year. Furthermore, employees who do not disclose their assets will not receive vigilance clearance for foreign travel or for deputation to another department. The Chief Secretary stated that if salaries of non-compliant employees are released, action would also be taken against the concerned Drawing and Disbursing Officer. Asset declarations by IPS officers Separately, the central government had directed IAS and IPS officers to submit their asset details to the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) by 31 January. IPS officers have complied and submitted their declarations. Among them, IPS officer Sanjeev Tyagi is reported to be the wealthiest in Uttar Pradesh. In one case, a Deputy Inspector General declared that a parcel of land in Ghaziabad valued at ₹10 crore in 2025 is now worth less than ₹3.25 crore. Another plot purchased for ₹50 lakh ten years ago has reportedly halved in value. These valuations are based on documents signed and submitted by the officer. In another instance, a Superintendent of Police who did not own a house until last year has purchased a property in Rajasthan for ₹3.40 crore with assistance from his brother and sister. Within 12 months, its value has reportedly risen by approximately ₹60 lakh to ₹4 crore.

stories.title: 'Come closer and I’ll shoot you':Husband who murdered wife’s lover dares police with pistol in Meerut
stories.summary: Police in Meerut arrest a man accused of murdering his wife’s lover after he surrenders on Thursday following prolonged persuasion. When police surround him, he points a pistol at officers and repeatedly warns, ‘Come closer and I’ll shoot you.’ During the 40-minute standoff, he remains defiant, at times drinking water and lighting a beedi, while police continue efforts to calm him. Eventually, officials gain his trust and convince him to lay down his weapon. He is taken into custody and brought to the police station. The operation is carried out jointly by Phalauda police station and the Crime Branch. See 2 pictures Relatives blocked road demanding arrest The post-mortem of the deceased lover is conducted on Thursday, and the body is handed over to the family. Demanding the accused’s arrest, family members place the body on the road and stage a blockade, refusing to move until he is caught. The protest leads to long traffic jams on both sides of the road. Police reach the spot and attempt to pacify the family. After about 40 minutes, the family agrees following police assurance, and the blockade is lifted. Accused shot his wife's lover in broad daylight On Wednesday around 1:45 PM in Ramraj, Satendra was riding his bike when a masked assailant arrived on another bike, carrying a country-made pistol. The attacker shot him twice, first in the back near the waist, then point-blank at his temple, blowing out his brains. After the first shot, he shouted in the market, ‘Is there any mother’s son who can save him?’ before firing the second bullet. Police investigation reveals that the deceased had an affair with the accused’s wife and had eloped with her. He was reportedly planning a love marriage with her, and the two men had argued a few days earlier over the relationship. Incident caught on CCTV A CCTV footage has emerged showing how accused Pradeep murdered Surendra. In the CCTV, a young man is seen shooting. He has covered his face with a sheet. This is said to be the accused Pradeep. This incident was captured by the CCTV installed in a nearby shop, showing the firing. Meanwhile, the accused is also seen speaking. The entire video is 39 seconds long. In it, the accused is clearly seen arriving, shooting, and shouting. He carried out the crime with great fearlessness and then fled. Threatened to kill wife in 4-minute video A 4-minute video of the accused Pradeep has also surfaced, which he himself made viral. In the video, Pradeep appears to be riding a bike. A mobile phone is placed in front, on which he shot the video. In the video, he is abusing his wife and her lover Surendra. He has also threatened to kill his wife, saying that he has killed the lover and will now kill her too. "If anyone can save her, save her." I killed him, I carry a shroud with me. I have taken my revenge. Today, after a year and a half, Surendra was found. I killed him. My wife had run away, I will kill her too. I am not afraid of anyone. I am challenging SSP Meerut, SO, everyone. All the women who run away, I will kill them all. Just keep telling me. I will kill all women who leave their homes. I am evicted from my house. I have nothing to do with my family. The police administration will not be able to do anything to me. I carry a two-and-a-half-meter shroud with me. Death is hovering over my head. I am not afraid of anyone. Accused’s video confession goes viral In a video, the accused says he does not care about his death and claims he shot her three times, taking sole responsibility and stating that neither his family nor friends are involved. He shows the pistol tucked into his pants and says he will throw the weapon into a canal, urging people to make the video viral. He threatens that any woman who elopes will face the same fate and asks viewers to send the video to the SSP Meerut and Bahsuma and Falawda police stations. He declares he will kill any woman who runs away from home and asks people to inform him by phone. Calling himself dispossessed and saying death is hovering over him, he points to the cloth on his head, claiming he walks with his shroud tied. Accused threatens more killings in video In another video, the accused says, 'Death is my fate. She troubled me for one and a half years; today I killed her, now I will kill my wife too.' He claims he is not afraid of the administration and threatens to kill other women who elope if authorities fail to act, alleging that Hastinapur police station forced him to take up arms. He names SO AK Sharma and Inspector Anil Kumar, alleging they did not provide court papers and pushed him toward violence. He says the man who arranged the weapon is dead and claims the firearm came from Harisingh of Manpur village through Deepsingh, adding that the supplier is related to the deceased Surendra. He states that on February 25 he shot Surendra three times using .32, 15 and 12 bore weapons, and threatens to kill the SO, the inspector and others, while declaring he is making the video viral on social media. Accused has been arrested SSP Avinash Pandey said, Sunil alias Gaba of Bahsuma police station area was murdered yesterday. After this, the accused youth named Sunil released a video confessing to the crime. Today, the accused has been arrested from Kalawada village on the Falawda border.

stories.title: Speeding pickup runs over 5 women in Mahoba:3 die, two critical; driver flees, incident captured on video
stories.summary: In Mahoba, a speeding pickup vehicle runs over five women late Wednesday night near the RTO office on the Kanpur–Sagar Highway, killing three and leaving two seriously injured. The women were returning home on foot after cooking at a wedding ceremony at Meera Palace Hotel when the uncontrolled vehicle hits them as they approach the RTO office, triggering chaos at the scene. The driver flees with the pickup after the collision. Police, with the help of locals, rush the injured to the hospital, where two women succumb to their injuries, and one is declared dead on the spot. The two critically injured women are referred to a higher center. CCTV footage of the incident has also surfaced. See three pictures Know the full case Financial assistance for road accidents to be provided Bhagwati and Shyamrani's sons stated that their mother had attended a wedding event at Meena Palace. While returning from there, there were a total of three-four women with her. Near the Chandrika Devi Temple gate, a pickup truck ran over them from behind. Upon receiving the information, Sadar MLA Rakesh Goswami reached the hospital, met the families of the deceased, and assured them of all possible help. He said, Efforts will be made to get the financial assistance received in road accidents from the government as soon as possible. Police report that the front left side of the pickup was found damaged at the scene, with numerous tomatoes scattered along the road. Based on the broken part seized, efforts are underway to trace the vehicle. ASP Vandana Singh says a speeding pickup ran over the women near Chandrika Temple in the Bhatipura area under Kotwali Nagar limits as they were returning from a wedding function. Three women have died in the accident, while two seriously injured women have been referred to Jhansi. The pickup driver has been traced.

stories.title: IT raid at factory of former MP’s relative in Rampur:CRPF personnel secure premises; multiple units deployed
stories.summary: The Income Tax Department has carried out a raid at MN Industry, a factory owned by Bablu and Munna, relatives of former ST Hasan, the ex-MP from Moradabad. The factory is situated in Bagi village under the Kotwali Ganj area of Rampur. Bablu and Munna are known timber traders in the city. According to sources, multiple teams from the Income Tax Department entered the factory premises simultaneously at around 10 am to conduct the search operation. Personnel from the Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) have been deployed at the main gate, creating a security cordon around the premises. The gate has been sealed, and entry and exit have been completely restricted. More than 12 vehicles belonging to the raid teams are reportedly stationed inside the factory compound. As of now, the Income Tax Department has not issued any official statement regarding the action. See visuals from spot Munna and Bablu are well-known timber traders from Rampur. Former Moradabad MP ST Hassan's daughter is married to Bablu's son. They operate several timber industries in the city. It has not yet been confirmed whether they were present inside the factory during the raid. Local police or district administration officials were also not seen at the spot. The operation is still ongoing.

stories.title: Mayawati calls SP ‘drama-driven’, anti-Dalit:Slams 'PDA Day' plan on Kanshiram Jayanti, accuses party of helping BJP
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) supremo Mayawati criticised the Samajwadi Party (SP) for announcing that it will celebrate Kanshiram Jayanti as ‘PDA Day’. She called the move political drama and accused the party of trying to mislead Dalits, backward classes and minorities for votes. Mayawati said SP’s conduct, character and political face have always been anti-Dalit and anti-backward. She alleged that when BSP founder Kanshi Ram passed away in 2006 during SP’s rule, the state government did not even declare a single day of mourning in his honour. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has announced that the party will observe ‘PDA Day’ on Kanshiram’s birth anniversary on March 15, prompting a strong response from BSP. Akhilesh earlier explained 'PDA' is the name of the unity born out of shared consciousness and feeling against the exploitation and oppression of those who are "pichre" (meaning backward), Dalit and "alpashankhak" (meaning minority). Accuses SP of disrespecting Dalit icons Mayawati alleged that during SP’s tenure, names of districts and institutions dedicated to Dalit icons were changed. She cited several examples and questioned SP’s commitment towards Kanshi Ram’s legacy. She said the BSP government had created Kanshiram Nagar district in Kasganj, but SP changed its name after coming to power. Similarly, Sant Ravidas Nagar district in Bhadohi was renamed by SP. Kanshi Ram Urdu-Persian-Arabic University in Lucknow was also renamed during SP’s rule, and a government hospital named after Kanshi Ram in Saharanpur was renamed as well. She questioned whether these actions reflected respect towards Kanshi Ram and Dalit leaders. Recalls 1995 guest house attack and SP-BSP alliance tensions Mayawati recalled the June 2, 1995, State Guest House incident in Lucknow, where she said there was an attempt on her life during SP’s rule. She said the incident remains recorded in government records and history. She also stated that SP’s anti-Dalit attitude became clear during the SP-BSP alliance in 1993, when, according to her, SP did not honour alliance agreements. After the guest house incident, Mayawati’s security was tightened significantly. Blames SP for riots and helping BJP politically Mayawati accused SP of practising casteist and communal politics and alleged that both SP and BJP have benefited from each other politically. She cited the 2013 Muzaffarnagar riots during SP rule, claiming that BJP gained political advantage from the violence. She also accused SP of being anti-Muslim, saying several communal riots took place during SP governments, causing heavy loss of life, property and displacement of families. According to Mayawati, SP’s actions created opportunities for BJP to strengthen its political position, while Dalits, Muslims and backward communities suffered the most. Calls PDA Day celebration political drama Mayawati said celebrating ‘PDA Day’ on Kanshiram’s birth anniversary is an attempt by SP to gain political mileage. She accused the party of repeatedly staging political drama to secure votes from Dalits, backward classes and minorities. She warned BSP supporters to remain cautious and said SP’s actions have historically harmed the interests of Bahujan society. She also alleged that Dalits and extremely backward communities faced the most atrocities during SP governments. Who was Kanshi Ram Kanshi Ram was born on March 15, 1934, in Ropar district of Punjab during British rule. He completed his BSc degree from Government College, Ropar, in 1956 and later joined an ammunition factory in Pune as a Class One officer. During his service, Kanshi Ram witnessed caste-based discrimination, which inspired him to begin his struggle for Dalit rights. He founded BAMSEF (Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation), a non-political organisation aimed at social awareness. Later, he formed the Dalit Shoshit Samaj Sangharsh Samiti to mobilise oppressed communities. On April 14, 1984, Kanshi Ram founded the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) on Dr B R Ambedkar’s birth anniversary to fight for the rights of Dalits and marginalised groups. He later mentored Mayawati and prepared her as his political successor. Kanshi Ram gradually withdrew from active politics after 2003 due to health issues and passed away in 2006.

stories.title: Father slapped son day before murder:Dispute over ₹50 lakh led to killing in Lucknow; family questions police version
stories.summary: A dispute between a father and son ended in a shocking act of patricide, after Lucknow’s well-known pathology lab owner was allegedly shot and dismembered by his own son. Fresh details have emerged in the murder of businessman Manvendra Singh. According to sources, Singh and his 21-year-old son, Akshat Pratap Singh alias Raja, had a heated argument over money just a day before the killing. The disagreement reportedly escalated into a physical confrontation. During the altercation, Manvendra is said to have slapped his son and allegedly pointed his licensed rifle at him. The dispute is believed to have centred around ₹50 lakh that had been kept at their home. However, Akshat’s maternal uncle has rejected the police theory, suggesting that the real reason behind the murder may be different. The Bhaskar team spoke to Manvendra's family members, relatives, and neighbors. Read the full report… Dispute over ₹50 lakh Manvendra Singh, owner of Vardhman Pathology, had allegedly kept ₹50 lakh at home for the renewal of liquor shop licences. On 19 February, when he counted the cash, he found some amount missing. He questioned Akshat about it. Suspicion fell on the son because jewellery items, including a bracelet and ring previously reported missing, had earlier been recovered from him. The argument turned intense. Later that night, Manvendra returned home and slept in the third-floor room where Akshat and his daughter Kriti were staying. Murder in the early hours According to investigators, the father left the house in anger but returned later that night. He slept in a third-floor room where Akshat and his daughter Kriti were also resting. At around 4:30am on 20 February, Akshat allegedly shot his father with the same licensed rifle. Post-mortem reports later confirmed that the bullet was fired into Manvendra’s head. Police say that after the shooting, Akshat dismembered the body. Both arms were cut off from the shoulders and both legs from above the knees. The severed limbs were placed in plastic bags and dumped in bushes near a canal close to Naderganj, about 21 kilometres away. The remaining part of the body was placed inside a blue drum and hidden in the house. “He killed him to take revenge for the slap” Several people, speaking on condition of anonymity, said Akshat may have acted out of anger over the public humiliation of being slapped and threatened with a gun. “There are discussions that he was furious after the argument during the day. Perhaps he planned the murder overnight,” one local resident said. It is also being reported that Akshat’s sister Kriti woke up after hearing the gunshot. Seeing her father covered in blood, she began to cry. According to sources, Akshat told her he would surrender. Kriti allegedly responded, Mother is already gone. You have killed Papa as well. If you go to jail, what will happen to me? After hearing this, Akshat reportedly decided not to surrender immediately. Call to a friend for help Sources claim that Akshat called a close friend after the murder and informed him about what had happened. However, the friend refused to assist in disposing of the body. Akshat then allegedly carried out the plan alone. He purchased two knives, two saws, and a blue drum. He transported the severed limbs and disposed of them near the canal in Naderganj. When he faced difficulty moving the remaining body, he reportedly bought 20 litres of turpentine oil, allegedly planning to burn it. Body kept at home for three days Police investigations revealed that the torso remained inside the blue drum in a ground-floor room for three days. During this period, both Akshat and Kriti reportedly behaved normally. Kriti continued attending her examinations, while Akshat went to the Ashiyana police station to file a missing person complaint for his father. On 23 February, acting on Akshat’s disclosure during questioning, police recovered Manvendra’s body from inside the drum. Because the body parts had been separated, the final rites were performed after wrapping them in polythene sheets. Relatives dispute police claims While police suggest the argument over money and possibly academic pressure may have been the motive, relatives strongly disagree. Manvendra’s brother-in-law, S.K. Bhadauria, told reporters, It is being said that Akshat was under pressure to clear the NEET exam and become a doctor. I do not believe that. There was no such pressure. He added that Kriti was present at home during the incident. When Akshat fired the shot, she allegedly said, “What have you done?” Akshat then reportedly threatened her to remain silent. Bhadauria insisted there was no mental or family pressure on Akshat. “The truth about why he killed his father can only be told by Akshat himself,” he said. Was there another reason? Some neighbours and relatives hint that the motive could be more complicated. There have been suggestions that Manvendra may have had close relations with another woman. His wife had earlier filed a case of assault against him in 2009, though the matter was later settled within the family. She eventually died by suicide. Relatives believe ongoing family tensions might have played a role. They have urged police to examine call records of Manvendra, Akshat and Kriti to uncover the full truth. Neighbour Raghavendra Singh, who is also distantly related to the family, said, Akshat was the only son. All his demands were fulfilled. Even if he was not interested in studies, no pressure was placed on him. The NEET angle does not make sense. Another neighbour, Alpana Singh, described both siblings as calm and well-mannered. “They never misbehaved with anyone. It is hard to believe Akshat could do something like this,” she said. Ashutosh Dubey, another resident, added, When news spread that Manvendra had not been seen for days, people began searching for him. Later we were told his son had killed him. It is unbelievable. What situation could have forced him to take his father’s life? Police under scrutiny Interestingly, the usually media-active Lucknow Police has maintained distance from the press in this sensational case. Instead of holding a press conference, officials released photographs of the recovered items from the Ashiyana police station. There is speculation that unanswered questions may have led police to avoid direct media interaction.

stories.title: Child sex abuse 'confirmed' in Avimukteshwaranand case:Medical report cites victim saying, 'Shankaracharya assaulted me'
stories.summary: The medical report concerning the child victims in the sexual abuse case against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand has been received. According to police sources, the examinations have confirmed that the minors were sexually assaulted. Police conducted medical tests on the victims on Wednesday, carried out by a panel of two doctors at a government hospital in Prayagraj. The sealed report was handed to the investigating officer on Thursday and is scheduled to be presented before the court on Friday. Police sources confirmed that the questions of who committed the assault, when, and where remain the subject of active investigation. The full extent of the allegations against Avimukteshwaranand will become clear only once the inquiry is complete. Jhunsi Station House Officer Mahesh Mishra stated that since the matter is sub judice, he was unable to disclose further details. Complainant claims confirmation of assault Earlier on Wednesday, Ashutosh Maharaj, the disciple of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya who filed the case against the Shankaracharya, stated that all evidence was in hand, that the medical examination had confirmed the assault on the young students, and that justice would be delivered swiftly. Victim speaks to media for first time One of the victim students came forward publicly for the first time, speaking to Aaj Tak. He alleged that he had gone to the ashram for study purposes, whereupon he was subjected to abuse. He claimed that other children present were also assaulted. When asked who was responsible, he named Avimukteshwaranand and his disciple Mukundananda. Confirming that the abuse also occurred at the Magh Mela, he stated that he was assaulted there on 16 January. He further alleged that the Shankaracharya's disciples, Prakash and Arvind, bring children in from outside, after which they are sexually exploited. Death threat issued to Shankaracharya's lawyer The Shankaracharya's legal counsel received a death threat via a message sent to his mobile late on Wednesday night. The message threatened to blow up the Varanasi court complex with a bomb, and to kill the lawyer as well. Prayagraj Police have been stationed in Varanasi for the past four days. Whilst the Shankaracharya may be questioned, investigators have not yet reached his ashram. Background and timeline of the case

stories.title: ₹11 crore cash found at BSP MLA’s house:Costly watches and jewellery seized; second day of raid underway in ₹1,000 crore tax evasion case
stories.summary: The Income Tax Department’s raid at the premises of BSP’s lone MLA Umashankar Singh continues for the second day. Action is underway in Sonbhadra, Kaushambi and Ballia, while the raid at his Lucknow residence has concluded. According to sources, the team has recovered around Rs 11.5 crore in cash from there. Apart from this, expensive watches, gold, silver and precious jewellery have also been seized. On Wednesday, the Income Tax team conducted simultaneous raids at more than 15 locations. Sources said the department is examining files, electronic devices and other records in a case related to alleged tax evasion of Rs 1,000 crore. However, no official confirmation of the recoveries has been made. Pictures of the raid The action that began at 7.30 am on Wednesday at the Lucknow residence continued till 9 am on Thursday. Around 50 officials carried out the search operation. During this time, entry and exit of anyone was restricted. The MLA and his family members remained inside the house. Meanwhile, in Sonbhadra, 24 officials are present at the office of Chhatra Shakti Construction. The gate is locked from inside. Company employees are also inside. Officials ordered food from outside at night. On Wednesday, the officers had reached posing as wedding guests. Wedding pamphlets were pasted on their vehicles. Umashankar Singh is a three-time MLA from the Rasra Assembly constituency in Ballia. He is suffering from blood cancer. He returned last month from the United States after undergoing a blood change procedure. At present, he is in isolation at his Lucknow residence and undergoing treatment. BSP supremo Mayawati had termed the raid inhuman. Minister Dinesh Singh in the Yogi government is Umashankar Singh’s relative by marriage. He said that as the father of a daughter, he would stand by her in happiness and sorrow. A daughter cannot be abandoned, politics can be. Minister Dinesh wrote - MLA is battling for life and death Minister Dinesh Singh said - Umashankar Singh is an MLA. He is our relative. But, the question is not about being a relative. Today, his house is being raided. His daughter called. She cried and said that they are being treated mercilessly. Umashankar ji has stage four cancer. He returned from America just a day ago. He is in isolation at his home. Everyone knows very well that he has been struggling between life and death for 2 years. All his businesses have been shut down. The family is constantly running between America, Delhi, and Lucknow for his treatment. In such a situation, an organization conducts this kind of raid. If it had to be done, they could have done it earlier or later. Taking action with such insensitivity is not appropriate. The assembly session is very important for an MLA, but he could not go there even for an hour. At this time, neither a nurse nor a doctor is allowed to go to his house. If any harm comes to his life, these insensitive organizations will be responsible for it. In such situations, courts grant relief even in serious crimes on humanitarian grounds. Yet, if any organization or leader can think of inflicting such pain out of political vendetta, it is extremely sad. May God give wisdom to such people and organizations. Can leave politics, not my daughter Dinesh Singh is Umashankar Singh's relative by marriage. He posted on X, stating that- As a father of a daughter, it is my duty to stand by my daughter through thick and thin. A daughter cannot be abandoned, politics can be abandoned, and a father who can abandon his daughter cannot be trusted in politics. Mayawati said - MLA seriously ill, could have raided later Mayawati posted on 'X' late Wednesday evening regarding this matter. She wrote- Ever since Umashankar Singh joined BSP, he has fulfilled his responsibilities with complete honesty and dedication. No complaint of illegally acquiring property or any other wrong doing has been received from his area so far. Umashankar Singh has been battling a serious illness for the past two years. In such a situation, even if the Income Tax Department had received any complaint regarding him, an inquiry could have been conducted after his recovery, keeping his health in mind. We are not interfering in the work of this department. But the way action has been taken against him today during a serious illness is extremely unfortunate and against humanity. Akhilesh said - Some people went to Japan, that's why the raid happened SP chief Akhilesh Yadav said- Who reveals the names of IT officials? The raid happened at Umashankar ji's place because some people went to Japan. If they hadn't gone to Japan, there would have been no raid. The police get to know. The police leak it. The question is not that Umashankar is a BSP MLA. If someone belongs to BJP, they are not raided. Please the BJP, and you will never be raided. Police were deployed for GST at all gutkha sellers' places. A rebar dealer used to donate to BJP, but even his place was raided. Therefore, assume that BJP is not loyal to anyone. MLA owns 54 crore, has a debt of 13 crore According to the 2022 affidavit, Umashankar Singh's total assets are approximately 54.05 crore rupees. This includes movable assets worth 18.05 crore and immovable assets worth 35.99 crore. He also has a debt of 13 crore rupees. Umashankar Singh has been active in the business world alongside politics. He owns a company named 'Chhatra Shakti Constructions', which undertakes road construction work. The company has completed road construction projects at various locations. Additionally, his company has also been active in the mining sector. Along with construction and mining, he has also been involved in education and the hotel business. Umashankar's wife, Pushpa Singh, is the Managing Director of 'CS Infra Construction Limited'. The company undertakes work related to infrastructure and construction. Last year, when she fell ill, Mayawati also came to meet her. The importance of Umashankar Singh in BSP can be gauged from the fact that Mayawati tied a rakhi to him. Not only this, on March 5, 2025, when Umashankar Singh fell ill, Mayawati reached his residence to meet him. She inquired about his health and also took a picture with his family. When was Umashankar Singh in the news? 1- Complaint filed with Vigilance 11 months ago MLA Umashankar Singh came into the limelight 11 months ago in a case of disproportionate assets. Vigilance had started an investigation against him. Vigilance had started collecting details of properties purchased in his name, as well as in the names of his wife Pushpa, son Yukesh, and daughter Yamini. It included land, houses, flats, commercial and agricultural properties. Vigilance had written a letter to IG Prayagraj asking for details of the properties. Following this, the IG had instructed the concerned departments to provide information. Records were also collected from the sub-registrar offices in Varanasi. 2- Verbal spat with Minister Dayashankar last year Last year, Umashankar Singh came into discussion after a dispute with Minister Dayashankar Singh. Actually, the new bridge built at Katharnala in Ballia was opened for traffic by the PWD. Upon receiving this information, Dayashankar Singh reached Ballia. The minister had reprimanded PWD's XEN Kesari Prakash, saying - Look, don't lose your mind. I am a minister. You are working at someone else's behest. I understand everything. Are you going to contest elections from here? Is BSP going to give you a ticket? After this, Umashankar Singh retaliated by holding a press conference. He had said - if we start making accusations and providing evidence, no one will find a place to hide. If the minister has a complaint about the bridge, he should talk to the Government of India. This is a matter of National Highway. After this, Dayashankar Singh had said - Umashankar's father used to sell kerosene, while I am the nephew of Manager Singh, who is known as Malviya of Ballia. 3- Also remained in controversies regarding four-lane construction in Gorakhpur Between 2017 and 2022, Umashankar Singh had constructed the Medical College four-lane road in Gorakhpur as a contractor. During this period, a drain was also built alongside the road. It was alleged that the height of the drain was made more than the road. Due to this, many surrounding areas were waterlogged during the rain. This matter was raised in the assembly by Radhamohan Das Agarwal (RMD), the then Gorakhpur Sadar MLA. He had also filed a complaint against Umashankar Singh at Shahpur police station. 4- Stone mining case came to light in CAG report in August, 2025 In August 2025, a stone mining case related to Umashankar came to light. According to the CAG (Comptroller and Auditor General of India) report, Umashankar's wife's company 'Chhatra Shakti Infra Construction' had taken a mining lease in Sonbhadra. The company acquired the right to mine stone at an auction rate of Rs 3000 per cubic meter, while the royalty rate was Rs 160 per cubic meter. It was alleged that the company illegally mined 33,604 cubic meters of gravel. In return, the fine was recovered based on the royalty rate, whereas it should have been recovered at the auction rate. If the recovery had been based on the auction rate, the company would have had to pay more than 10 crore rupees. However, the matter was settled for 3 crore 22 lakh rupees. This resulted in a loss of crores of rupees to the government. Joined BSP in 2011, has been an MLA ever since Disqualified in 2017 On January 14, 2017, the then Governor Ram Naik disqualified him. He was accused of violating the Representation of the People Act. The matter was related to taking government contracts in his name. The Lokayukta's investigation found the allegations to be true. Later, his membership was canceled after the Election Commission's recommendation on the High Court's directive. This was the first case in the state when the membership of an MLA was terminated with retrospective effect.

stories.title: Woman constable burnt alive in car with son:Husband screams for help, fire breaks out after dumper crash in Rampur
stories.summary: A female constable and her 2-year-old son died in a fire in Rampur, UP. Her husband and brother-in-law were burnt. The constable had gone from Rampur to Nainital for a trip with her family in a Swift Dzire car. While returning, an out-of-control dumper collided with the car, causing the car to catch fire. The brother-in-law and husband somehow managed to open the gate and get out, while the female constable could not get out while trying to save her son. The husband kept screaming and shouting, but he could not save them. Hearing the screams, people from the vicinity reached the spot. Police and fire brigade were called and the fire was extinguished. After this, the female constable and her son were pulled out of the car. The child died on the spot, while the constable succumbed to her injuries while being taken to the hospital. Police admitted the husband and brother-in-law to a private hospital. The accident occurred late Wednesday night in the Ganj police station area. After the accident, the dumper driver fled. Family was returning from Nainital Dan Singh's family lives in Behatra village of Milak area. He works by renting out cars. His wife Lata was posted in the police in Kaushambi. Late Wednesday night, Dan Singh was returning home from Nainital with his wife, son Lattu, and maternal cousin Ravi, a resident of Bareilly, in a car. Dumper hit, fire broke out due to tank bursting Dan Singh himself was driving the car. The car is registered in the name of his father, Home Guard father Ingle Singh. It is being told that they had just reached near Aanga village in Kashipur after 11 PM when a dumper coming from the opposite direction hit the car from the side. Due to the collision, the petrol tank burst, causing the car to catch fire. Female Constable Trapped with Son Dan Singh and Ravi somehow managed to open the gate and get out, but they also suffered burns. The female constable was trapped in the car with her two-year-old son. Seeing the flames, people from the vicinity reached the spot. Police and fire brigade were called. The team arrived shortly and brought the fire under control. Constable died while being taken to hospital Upon receiving information about the incident, ASP Anurag Singh reached the spot. The police admitted woman constable Lata, her husband, and her brother-in-law to a private hospital, where Lata was referred to Bareilly due to her serious condition. Lata also died while being taken to the hospital. After the accident, there was a long traffic jam near Kashipur. The police cleared the jam by moving the car to the side. Injured brother-in-law narrated the entire incident while crying The injured brother-in-law, crying, said - The car was bought new only two weeks ago. We had returned from visiting Mathura two days ago. From there, we returned home on Tuesday night around 4 AM and went to sleep. On Wednesday morning, Dan Singh called. He said that we have to go to Nainital. I initially refused, saying I couldn't drive, but still, I went. On Wednesday morning at 11 AM, I reached Dan Singh's house. Dan Singh drove the car from Milak to Bilaspur, and I drove from Bilaspur to Nainital. After reaching the mountains, I handed the car back to Dan Singh. After visiting Nainital, my health deteriorated while returning from there towards Rampur. I had fallen asleep in the car when suddenly there was a loud noise. A dumper coming from the opposite direction hit the side of the car, causing the car to catch fire. Dan Singh and I somehow managed to get out, but Dan Singh's wife and son were badly burnt. Both of them died.

stories.title: Lucknow University students protest contaminated mess food:Law student faints, alleges worms in dal; probe ordered, condition stable
stories.summary: A ruckus erupted over food quality at Lucknow University on Wednesday. Female students sat on a dharna in protest against contaminated food. They also did not have dinner. They expressed their anger by fasting. The students allege that a fellow student fell ill after eating the food served in the mess. Despite informing, medical help was not received on time. No action was taken against the mess operator either. After eating mess food in Ganga Hostel in the afternoon, a third-year law student started vomiting. After this, she fainted. Angered by this, her fellow students created a huge commotion in the hostel late in the evening. The students said - "Until action is taken against the mess operator, the protest will continue." An LU spokesperson said that the affected student was consulted by a doctor. She has also been provided with medical facilities. Currently, the student's condition is stable. An investigation will be conducted into the quality of the mess food. See 3 pictures Students angry over the incident have sat on a protest against the LU administration. Now read the sequence of events in detail Worms in the dal, taste not good either Meghna Shah, a final year student of the Law Faculty, ate mess food on Wednesday afternoon. Soon after, she started vomiting severely. She fainted. Her fellow students took care of her. Meghna says that there were worms in the dal. The taste of the food was also not good. A video of this was also made. After eating the food, Meghna's health deteriorated. No Medical Help Received The students informed Warden Jahanvi and Hostel Provost Neetam Singh, but a doctor could not be made available on time. The students say that complaints regarding the quality of the mess had been made earlier as well, but no improvement was seen. The students have demanded a safe environment, clean food, and prompt medical facilities in case of an emergency. Threats Received for Protesting The situation regarding the contaminated food served in the Ganga Hostel mess is becoming serious. Late at night, another student's health suddenly deteriorated, after which she was immediately taken to the doctor. It is being reported that after eating the mess food, several students have complained of stomach pain, vomiting, and other health-related issues. The protesting students in this matter have alleged that the hostel provost, Neetam Singh, threatened them while they were staging a sit-in against contaminated food. The students say that instead of taking their complaints seriously, pressure is being put on them. After the incident, there is an atmosphere of anger in the hostel. Student's condition stable, currently out of danger Mukul Srivastava, spokesperson for Lucknow University, said, "The affected student was consulted by a doctor. She has also been provided with medical facilities. Currently, the student's condition is stable. She only has a complaint of anxiety. The quality of the mess food will be investigated. Under no circumstances will the health of the students be compromised."

stories.title: Stepmother slits three-year-old girl’s throat in Gorakhpur:Father says, 'She was jealous and accused me of loving my daughter more than her'
stories.summary: A shocking incident has emerged from a village in Gorakhpur, where a mother allegedly killed her three-year-old stepdaughter by attacking her with an axe. The brutal crime took place in Bijhara village under the Pipraich police station area. According to police and family members, the accused woman, identified as Pooja, attacked the child late at night while the father was outside the house. Within just 25 days of marriage, he killed my daughter. Under what circumstances did a mother kill her daughter? Then what did the villagers do to that mother? To find this out, the Dainik Bhaskar team reached Bijhara village in Pipraich. Read the report… The night of the murder The child’s father, Triveni Maurya, said the incident happened around midnight. He had stepped outside with his mobile phone torch on and was speaking to someone when he saw his wife leaving the house carrying a bag. “When I asked her where she was going, she just stared at me and walked away quickly,” he said. Feeling uneasy, he rushed inside. What he saw left him shattered. His three-year-old daughter, Aditi, was lying in a pool of blood. Her neck had been severed from her body. Police said the woman first tied a rope tightly around the child’s neck and then struck her four times with an axe. Disturbing scene inside the house Relatives who took reporters inside described a horrifying scene. Blood was scattered across the floor near the bed. A small prayer shelf on the wall, holding pictures of Hindu deities, had blood splashes on it. At the spot where the attack happened, there was a four-inch dent in the floor caused by the force of the blows. A blood-stained rope lay nearby, along with the child’s broken amulet. The child’s toys were still kept in one corner of the house. Father blames himself Triveni, a construction worker by profession, was seen sitting in the courtyard holding his daughter’s toy and weeping. “If I had not remarried, my daughter would still be alive,” he said. “I thought Pooja would love her like a mother. Instead, she killed her.” He claimed that his wife was often irritated by the child. “She used to eat the chocolates I bought for Aditi. When I scolded her a few days ago, she said I cared more for my daughter than for her.” The couple had been married for just 25 days. Why he remarried Triveni’s first wife, Lakshmi Devi, married him in 2012. Their daughter Aditi was born on 16 April 2023. Lakshmi passed away six months later due to illness. Struggling to manage work and childcare alone, Triveni eventually agreed to remarry after family members advised him that his daughter needed a mother’s care. He married Pooja, a 35-year-old woman from Sahjanwa, on 30 January this year. After the wedding, he brought Aditi back from her maternal uncle’s house. “At first, everything seemed fine. Aditi hugged her,” he said. “I never imagined this could happen.” Villagers caught the accused After discovering the crime, Triveni alerted neighbours. Villagers rushed to the house and later tracked down Pooja near Kusmhi forest. She was reportedly trying to flee. The villagers caught her, tied her hands and feet, and informed the police. According to police officials, the accused woman has admitted to killing the child, allegedly saying she could not tolerate her husband’s affection towards his daughter. Police investigation underway Circle Officer Ratneshwar Singh from the Chauri Chaura division confirmed that the woman has been taken into custody. The axe used in the crime has been recovered. He said the accused has remained mostly silent during questioning. Police are continuing their investigation to determine all circumstances surrounding the case. A birthday that will never be celebrated The tragedy has left the village in deep shock. Aditi was due to celebrate her fourth birthday on 16 April. Her father had been inviting relatives to mark the occasion. Instead, the family is now preparing for her funeral. The incident has sparked outrage and sorrow in the local community, with many struggling to comprehend how a mother could commit such a crime.

stories.title: How far will Alankar Agnihotri’s 'RAM' go in UP politics:Former officer explains funding model; history not favourable to bureaucrats’ parties
stories.summary: Alankar Agnihotri, a former PCS officer in Uttar Pradesh who resigned from government service, has launched a new political party named Rashtriya Adhikar Morcha (RAM). He stepped down from his post after expressing hurt over the alleged insult to Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand and opposing the University Grants Commission’s new rules. Agnihotri and his party have drawn media attention since the announcement, with supporters backing his move and presenting RAM as a platform for raising issues related to religious dignity and policy concerns. The party is currently in its initial phase and is focusing on building its organisational base and public outreach. Questions raised over future and resources Despite the early attention and support, political observers have questioned the party’s long-term viability. Analysts say running a political party requires significant financial resources, organisational strength, and sustained grassroots presence. They point out that in Uttar Pradesh’s bipolar political landscape dominated by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Samajwadi Party (SP), even established parties with a strong mass base, such as the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), have struggled to maintain their electoral relevance. In this context, experts say it remains uncertain how a newly formed party like Rashtriya Adhikar Morcha will sustain itself and what impact it will be able to make in the state’s competitive political arena. Will Alankar Agnihotri be able to make an impact in politics? Former PCS officer Alankar Agnihotri resigned nearly 16 years before retirement to enter politics, saying he wanted to work for society and provide political representation to communities he believes lack a voice. Had he continued in service, he could have retired as Secretary or Divisional Commissioner around 2041. His decision has drawn support, with people joining his party Rashtriya Adhikar Morcha (RAM) and contributing resources. However, several former IAS and IPS officers who formed political parties in the past failed to achieve significant electoral success, raising questions about RAM’s long-term prospects. Below are excerpts from Alankar Agnihotri’s conversation: Question: What are your party’s election preparations? Alankar Agnihotri: This is not just my party, it belongs to everyone. Our preparations have begun, and we are working with the goal of forming the government in 2027. We believe democracy has weakened, and people are looking for an alternative. Many voters are supporting our party. We are emerging as a political alternative, and our focus is on forming the government in the state. Question: Will you be able to challenge parties like BJP, SP, BSP and Congress? Alankar Agnihotri: We are confident about our growth. People across the state want change and want our party to move forward. We believe public support will help us establish ourselves politically. Question: Many officers before you have formed political parties but could not succeed. What makes your party different? Alankar Agnihotri: People will see the results themselves. We are working with commitment and public support, and we are confident about achieving success. Question: Where will the resources needed to run the party come from? Alankar Agnihotri: The public is supporting us and will continue to help. We will seek public funding and maintain transparency by sharing the details. Question: Is your support limited to one community? Alankar Agnihotri: Our support base includes the entire Sanatan society and all communities that believe in the constitutional system. We are working to represent broader social interests. Question: How will you compete in an environment dominated by caste-based politics? Alankar Agnihotri: We believe development should be the focus of politics. Our party aims to work with a development-oriented approach. Question: What is your response to the Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand issue? Alankar Agnihotri: I believe the matter requires a fair and independent investigation. I urge the courts to examine the issue so that the truth comes out. Question: What would you say about the status of Brahmins and Sanatan society in Uttar Pradesh? Alankar Agnihotri: This is not limited to one community. Our focus is on preserving cultural values and ensuring positive social development. We want to work towards unity and constructive progress. Political analysts note that several former bureaucrats, including Chandrapal Singh, Sulkhan Singh, SR Darapuri, and Vijay Shankar Pandey, formed political parties but did not achieve electoral success. Experts say bureaucrats have had more success after joining established political parties rather than creating new ones, making it uncertain whether Alankar Agnihotri’s party will be able to establish a lasting political presence.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar sets sights on ‘cursed’ Hastinapur seat:4-election record links constituency winner to UP government formation
stories.summary: Hastinapur assembly seat in Uttar Pradesh has once again come into political focus amid speculation that Nagina MP Chandrashekhar may contest from the constituency. The development comes months after BJP MLA Dinesh Khatik publicly said he did not want to contest again from the seat, calling it “cursed”. Two months ago, speaking at a public event, Khatik said he did not want to become MLA from Hastinapur for the third time. He referred to a mythological belief linked to Draupadi and described the seat as “cursed”. Later, he clarified that he remained committed to serving the people of the constituency. Political observers say the seat has gained attention due to changing political signals, Chandrashekhar’s possible entry, and preparations by the Azad Samaj Party (ASP). Why Hastinapur seat is politically significant? Three key factors are being cited behind the speculation over Chandrashekhar contesting from Hastinapur. First, election results from the past four assembly polls show that the party winning this seat has gone on to form the government in Uttar Pradesh. This has strengthened the perception that the constituency holds symbolic and political importance. Second, Hastinapur is a reserved seat for Scheduled Castes. Such constituencies are considered important for Dalit leadership, and parties often field prominent candidates here to consolidate their support base. Third, Chandrashekhar, who won the Nagina Lok Sabha seat, is seen as trying to strengthen his political presence in western Uttar Pradesh. Contesting and winning from Hastinapur could help him demonstrate his grassroots support beyond social media and parliamentary politics. When asked about the possibility, Chandrashekhar said decisions on candidates and constituencies would be taken by the party leadership. He added that the Azad Samaj Party is preparing to contest all 403 assembly seats in the state. ASP begins groundwork, campaign visibility increases Azad Samaj Party leaders have started increasing political activity in Hastinapur. Wall paintings with Chandrashekhar’s name have appeared in key market areas, signalling an attempt to build public awareness. Hastinapur is part of the larger political region linked to the Nagina Lok Sabha constituency, from where Chandrashekhar was elected MP. His influence is already considered strong in the area, and party leaders are trying to expand that support ahead of the assembly elections. Recently, Chandrashekhar also appointed Ravindra Singh Bhati, a Gurjar leader and national general secretary of the party, as in-charge of the Meerut division. He has been given responsibility for Saharanpur, Moradabad, and Meerut divisions. Political observers see this move as an attempt to strengthen outreach among Gurjar voters, who play an important role in Hastinapur. Bhati has been associated with several Gurjar community mobilisations and is considered an influential regional leader. Experts say caste equations and political strategy will shape contest Senior journalist Pushpendra Sharma said the speculation around Chandrashekhar’s candidature may also be part of a broader political strategy in a Dalit-dominated seat. He noted that BJP MLA Dinesh Khatik had broken the trend by winning three consecutive elections from this reserved constituency. His recent remarks about not wanting to contest again could reflect growing opposition or anti-incumbency. Sharma added that the Samajwadi Party (SP) could benefit from changing political equations if multiple Dalit leaders contest and divide votes. He also said Chandrashekhar may be aiming to establish himself as a major Dalit leader at the state level by contesting from key reserved seats. However, he pointed out that it would be difficult for a sitting MP to resign and contest an assembly election unless it serves a clear political purpose. SP also focuses on seat, Gurjar vote remains crucial Senior journalist Rajesh Sharma said Hastinapur is politically significant not only because it is a reserved seat but also due to the influence of Gurjar voters. According to him, Gurjar voters often play a decisive role in determining the election outcome. He said Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has already held meetings with Gurjar leaders and organised conferences in Hastinapur, indicating the party’s focus on winning the seat. If Chandrashekhar contests, he is likely to face candidates from SP, BSP, and BJP. Political analysts believe this could divide Dalit votes and make the contest more competitive. BJP MLA’s statement adds to political uncertainty The political debate intensified after BJP MLA Dinesh Khatik’s earlier statement about not wanting to contest from Hastinapur. He made the remark at a school function, saying he did not wish to contest again from what he called a “cursed” seat. He later clarified that his statement was misunderstood and reaffirmed his commitment to serving the constituency. Political observers believe his remarks came at a time when opposition against him was growing locally and his candidature for the next election was uncertain. Seat likely to remain centre of political contest With Azad Samaj Party increasing its activity, Samajwadi Party strengthening its outreach, and uncertainty over BJP’s candidate, Hastinapur is expected to witness a closely contested election. Chandrashekhar’s final decision will depend on party strategy. However, the growing political mobilisation indicates that the reserved constituency will remain a key battleground in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.

stories.title: Latthmar Holi played in Barsana:Veiled women strike 'huriyars' with 'lathis', lakhs gather to watch | VIDEO
stories.summary: The traditional Latthmar Holi was celebrated in Barsana, Mathura, on Wednesday, drawing massive crowds from India and abroad. Women with veils covering their faces held sticks and playfully struck men from Nandgaon, known as huriyars, who defended themselves with shields. The vibrant celebration took place in Barsana’s famous Rangili Gali, where women symbolically chased and hit the huriyars as part of the centuries-old ritual. The men tried to protect themselves while singing and teasing, following the traditional customs linked to Lord Krishna and Radha. The festive atmosphere saw heavy participation, with around 20 lakh people reaching Mathura district to witness the unique Holi celebrations. Devotees, tourists, and locals gathered along the narrow lanes, rooftops, and balconies to watch the event. Police personnel were deployed in large numbers to manage the crowd and ensure safety. During the celebrations, women also playfully struck policemen with sticks, which is considered part of the festive spirit. Latthmar Holi in Barsana is one of the most famous Holi celebrations in India and is held every year ahead of the main Holi festival. The event reflects the cultural traditions of Braj and attracts visitors from across the country and overseas.

stories.title: Can Owaisi dent Akhilesh’s Muslim vote base in Uttar Pradesh?:BSP-AIMIM alliance could hurt SP; 7 seats lost due to vote split earlier
stories.summary: After its recent electoral gains in Bihar and Maharashtra, the All India Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (AIMIM) has stepped up its political activity in Uttar Pradesh. The party’s national president Asaduddin Owaisi, along with his brother Akbaruddin Owaisi and state leaders, has begun targeting the Samajwadi Party (SP) and its chief Akhilesh Yadav. AIMIM leaders have openly challenged SP’s dominance among Muslim voters. Asaduddin Owaisi has also criticised Akhilesh Yadav and signalled the party’s intent to expand its base in Uttar Pradesh. This has raised questions about whether AIMIM can replicate its performance in Bihar and Maharashtra, and how much impact it could have on SP in future elections. AIMIM lacks the same ground presence as Bihar and Maharashtra Senior journalist Hasan Ejaz said AIMIM does not have the same organisational strength in Uttar Pradesh as it had in Bihar and Maharashtra. He explained that AIMIM’s success in Bihar was mainly limited to the Muslim-majority Seemanchal region, where the Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) lacked strong Muslim leadership. He added that criticism of Owaisi by RJD leaders also created resentment among some Muslim voters, which helped AIMIM gain support. In Maharashtra, AIMIM’s growth was linked to local political conditions and internal divisions within other parties. Its success was mainly seen in municipal corporation elections rather than parliamentary polls. SP has strong Muslim representation across Uttar Pradesh Political observers say the Samajwadi Party has a wide network of Muslim leaders across Uttar Pradesh. SP has influential leaders in most districts, especially in western Uttar Pradesh and eastern regions. Prominent SP Muslim leaders include Ikra Hasan, Shahid Manzoor, Qadir Rana, ST Hasan, Azam Khan, Mohibulla Nadvi, Rafiq Ansari, Iqbal Mahmood, Mahboob Ali and Ziaurrahman Barq in western Uttar Pradesh. In other regions, leaders such as Afzal Ansari in Ghazipur, Ziauddin Rizvi in Ballia and Zahid Beg in Bhadohi remain key faces. Analysts say this widespread representation makes it difficult for AIMIM to quickly build a strong base in the state. AIMIM contested 95 seats in 2022 but failed to win any In the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, AIMIM contested 95 seats but did not win any. The party secured about 0.5 percent of the total vote share and received around 4.5 lakh votes. Its best performance was in Mubarakpur, where it received 36,460 votes. However, the Samajwadi Party won the seat by a margin of about 29,000 votes. In Sambhal, AIMIM secured more than 20,000 votes, but SP still won comfortably. AIMIM’s weakest performance was in Thanabhawan in Shamli district, where it received only 325 votes. Despite not winning any seats, AIMIM affected the outcome in several constituencies. In seven seats, the number of votes secured by AIMIM candidates was higher than SP’s margin of defeat. Of the 95 seats contested by AIMIM, BJP and its allies won 51 seats, while SP and its allies won 44. SP taking a cautious approach unlike RJD Unlike RJD in Bihar, which openly criticised AIMIM, the Samajwadi Party has taken a cautious approach. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has avoided direct confrontation with AIMIM and has reportedly advised party spokespersons to remain restrained on the issue. Political observers say SP’s Muslim-Yadav support base and its broader social coalition strategy remain key strengths in Uttar Pradesh. Shaukat Ali leading AIMIM’s expansion in Uttar Pradesh AIMIM’s state president Shaukat Ali is the party’s main face in Uttar Pradesh. He has been holding meetings in various districts to strengthen the organisation. Shaukat Ali has announced that AIMIM will contest district panchayat elections and the 2027 Assembly elections across all 75 districts of the state. The party is also relying on the leadership of Asaduddin Owaisi and Akbaruddin Owaisi to attract voters. He has accused the Samajwadi Party of ignoring Muslim interests and said AIMIM will offer an alternative political platform. Possible impact if AIMIM and BSP align Senior journalist Syed Kasim said AIMIM could have a greater impact if it forms an alliance with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). Such a coalition could attract both Muslim and Dalit voters and create challenges for SP. However, BSP chief Mayawati has said her party will contest future elections independently and has not announced any alliance plans. Limited impact so far, but expansion plans continue Political analysts say AIMIM currently lacks the organisational strength and leadership network in Uttar Pradesh compared to SP. However, its presence could influence results in closely contested seats by affecting vote distribution. The party is focusing on expanding its base ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. Its future impact will depend on its ability to build local leadership, form alliances and gain sustained voter support.

stories.title: UP’s ‘Super cop’ accused of conspiracy by Shankaracharya:IPS officer known for 500 encounters, who once jailed Ashutosh Brahmachari
stories.summary: Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand has accused IPS officer Dr Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring with Ashutosh Brahmachari, who had filed a case against him. The Shankaracharya also released a photograph showing Sharma cutting a cake with Brahmachari, alleging it indicates a close association between the two. He claimed that the officer, known for handling encounter cases, was behind what he described as a “script” leading to his arrest. According to the Shankaracharya, the officer played a key role in the developments that resulted in legal action against him. However, records show that Sharma had earlier taken action against Ashutosh Brahmachari. While serving as Superintendent of Police in Shamli, he had arrested Brahmachari and sent him to jail in connection with a separate case. Dr Ajay Pal Sharma joined the Indian Police Service in 2011 after training as a dentist. He is widely known as an encounter specialist and has been involved in more than 500 encounters during his career. Police data indicates that 15 accused were killed in these encounters, while several others were arrested. No official response from Sharma or the police department has been issued so far regarding the Shankaracharya’s allegations. 136 encounters in 22 months Dr. Ajay Pal Sharma from Ludhiana, Punjab was a dental surgeon before becoming an IPS officer. He obtained his BDS (Dental Sciences) degree from Government Medical College, Patiala. His younger brother Amit Pal Sharma is an IAS officer. 41-year-old Ajay Pal is currently posted as Additional CP (Law and Order) in Prayagraj. Prior to this, he has served as SP/SSP in five districts. During his 22-month tenure as SP in Jaunpur, he conducted a record 136 encounters. This is the highest number of encounters during any SP's tenure in any district. Commanded these districts He has served as captain of Hathras, Shamli, Ghaziabad, Rampur and Jaunpur. In 2013, he was posted as ASP in the Kumbh Mela organized in Prayagraj. He was also given responsibility as SP Personnel and captain of UP-112 at police headquarters. Woman had made serious allegations Ajay Pal Sharma's career was not only filled with successes but also controversies. In 2020, a woman named Deepti Sharma made serious allegations against him. The woman claimed that Ajay Pal had married her in 2016 and later backed out. This case became so big that an FIR was filed against them at Hazratganj police station in Lucknow and an SIT investigation was also set up. Due to this controversy, their promotion remained stalled for a long time, though they later received a clean chit. Served as Nodal Officer in Mahakumbh Just before Mahakumbh, he was posted as Nodal Officer (Mahakumbh, Commissionerate Prayagraj) in Prayagraj. On December 22, 2024, he was made Additional CP Prayagraj. During this time, he played an important role in the successful organization of Mahakumbh. After Mahakumbh, he was given the responsibility of Additional CP (Law and Order) Prayagraj. Ajay Pal's name was not in Shankaracharya's initial allegations Ajay Pal Sharma was also present there along with other officers during the dispute at Sangam Ghat on Mauni Amavasya. In the crowd of officers, he was seen at the forefront with a loudspeaker repeatedly requesting Shankaracharya and his supporters to clear the path for coming and going. Although after Mauni Amavasya, Shankaracharya presented his views on the controversy in a press conference on January 19. He showed the names and photos of district officials, which did not include Dr. Ajay Pal Sharma's name. Ajay Pal was posted in Shamli for about one and a half years Ajay Pal Sharma was appointed as SP Shamli by the then SP government on October 17, 2016. He remained posted until March 2018. Ashutosh Pandey alias Ashutosh Brahmachari is a history-sheeter from Kandla police station in Shamli. He has 21 cases registered against him. It was Ajay Pal Sharma who had sent Ashutosh Brahmachari to jail. Additional CP Law and Order IPS Dr. Ajay Pal Sharma said- The case has been registered on court's orders. Investigation is being conducted impartially. Further action will be taken based on the evidence that comes forward. Declined to comment on the allegations made by Shankaracharya.
