stories.title: Woman cheated of ₹2.20 lakh in fake house sale deal:Beware of fraud while buying or selling a property; 7 things you must know
stories.summary: Recently, a woman was reportedly cheated out of ₹2.20 lakh by a man who promised to sell her a house in Moradabad, Uttar Pradesh. According to the police report, the man took an advance payment of ₹30,000 and later collected the remaining amount. However, he neither transferred the house to her name nor returned the money. When the woman asked for her money back, the man allegedly threatened her. Following a complaint from the woman’s son, the police are investigating the matter. Such property fraud incidents highlight the issues people usually face while buying or selling property. While buying a home is a significant challenge, selling an old house can be equally complicated. Sellers often struggle to get a fair price for their property, while buyers sometimes become victims of fraud or overcharges. Therefore, it’s crucial to be cautious. If you are planning to sell your house for the first time, here’s what you need to know: Expert Insight: Ayush Dubey, Broker Associate, Bhopal When you are buying a property Buying a property requires patience, research, and legal caution. Rushing to make a decision can lead to financial loss, while careful planning can secure a safe and profitable investment. So, before you buy the house, first do better planning, take care of all your needs like- Legal documentation checklist is the most important To avoid fraud and any kind of false trap, keep all legal and financial matters clear. Gather complete information with the agent and seller and verify the ownership. Also take care of these things- When you are selling a house Everyone wants to sell their property at a good price. However, getting the right value can feel like an uphill task. First, you publish s, then choose the right real estate website, upload photos and videos, search for buyers, and arrange multiple property visits. After considerable effort, you may finally find a serious buyer. Even then, many sellers fail to secure a good deal. The main reason behind this is lack of proper planning, research, and preparation. Without prior experience, the process becomes even more challenging. How to plan properly before selling a house? Selling a house is a lengthy and exhausting process. Smart planning is crucial. Focus on these important aspects: How to decide the right price as per market rate? Most sellers feel their property is being undervalued and expect a higher price than market standards. Therefore, the first step is to determine the correct selling price. According to broker associate Ayush Dubey, knowing the market rate is essential. The price should neither be too high nor too low compared to prevailing rates. Ways to determine market rate: After gathering this information, set your price. If you are quoting above market value, you must have valid reasons, such as: How to choose the right broker or real estate agent? Finding a trustworthy agent is a major task. To avoid fraud and secure a better deal: Research the agent: Check property s in newspapers to find local agents. Ask acquaintances about their reputation. Check track record: Speak to friends or relatives who recently bought or sold property and learn from their experiences. Verify credentials: Check online reviews and verify credentials. You may even verify records through local authorities to avoid fraud. How to prepare the house before showing it to buyers? The condition of your house significantly impacts its value. No matter how valuable the property is, if it looks unclean or poorly maintained, its perceived market value drops. Remember, first impressions matter. Before listing your house: Do photos and videos affect sales? Yes, significantly. Along with factual details, the quality of photos and videos on property websites strongly influences buyer interest. Documents required when selling a house Before selling, gather all necessary documents in one file: Legal and Financial Transparency Keep all legal and financial matters clear. Share complete information with the agent and buyer. Do not hide disputes, ongoing legal cases, home loans, or pending dues. Trying to be “smart” can backfire later. How to beware of property fraud while buying or selling a house? Property fraud cases, like the Moradabad incident, highlight the need for caution. Take care of these points- Careful planning, proper documentation, and market research can protect you from financial loss and legal trouble while buying or selling a house.

stories.title: Brain-dead patient gives new life to 3 in Lucknow:Two regain eyesight; police create green corridor, transport liver 19 km in 18 minutes
stories.summary: In Lucknow, a 42-year-old brain-dead patient gave new life to three people, while two others regained their eyesight through corneal donation. He was admitted to Apex Trauma at Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGI), where doctors declared him brain dead on Sunday, February 22. After counselling, the family agreed to donate his organs, and the process began immediately. Both kidneys were retrieved at SGPGI for transplant. King George's Medical University (KGMU) was informed about the liver, and police created a green corridor from SGPGI to KGMU. Escorting the ambulance with two vehicles, the 19-km distance was covered in 18 minutes. See 2 pictures People seen supporting the traffic Injured in an accident on February 7 Liver transplant facility available at KGMU Both kidneys were taken from the brain-dead patient at SGPGI, and kidney transplants were performed on needy patients here. However, liver transplant facility is currently not available at SGPGI. Whereas liver transplants are performed at KGMU. This was the reason why the liver was sent to KGMU by creating a green corridor. Along with this, both eyes were also sent. They will be kept in KGMU's eye bank. Women from Unnao and Mainpuri received kidneys Dr. Narayan Prasad, Head of the Nephrology Department at SGPGI, informed that both kidneys are being transplanted within the institute. Both recipients are women. One of them is a resident of Unnao and the other of Mainpuri. Both kidney transplants are ongoing. Both kidney transplants are expected to be completed by 10:30 PM. Meanwhile, the liver has been donated to a KGMU patient for liver transplant. He claimed that after about 20 years, SGPGI itself has found such a brain-dead patient whose organs can give new life to the needy. Before this, when I myself was a resident doctor here, such an opportunity arose. The good thing is that people are becoming aware of organ transplants.

stories.title: Uproar at Lucknow University, namaz offered on campus:Students protest over closure of Lal Baradari gate, heavy police deployed
stories.summary: Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha, NSUI, and AISA protested against the closure of the door of Lal Baradari Mosque at Lucknow University. On Sunday afternoon, students first knocked down the barricades towards Lal Baradari. After this, they reached near the building, chanting slogans, and offered Namaz there. In the evening, they also had Iftar there. Students offering Namaz were surrounded by other students forming a human chain. This human chain was removed when they finished their prayers. During this, a heavy police force remained deployed there. Students say that the university administration sealed the door of this mosque and erected a wall there without any notice. They demanded the opening of the sealed door. See 3 pictures Whoever creates an obstruction will not be spared. Bhavna Mishra, Registrar of Lucknow University, stated that Lal Baradari is in a dilapidated condition. The construction superintendent was asked to get fencing done there. Meanwhile, Hasanganj police were also informed in advance and asked to deploy adequate police force. Work has been started on Sunday. Legal action will be taken against anyone who creates an obstruction in this. Registrar's Office had issued a letter A letter was sent by the Registrar to the Superintendent of Works of Nirman Bhawan on February 2. It had asked for the construction of fencing. Subsequently, on Sunday, the work of building the fencing began. Following this, students from groups like NSUI, Samajwadi Chhatrasabha, and AISA protested against the construction of the fencing. Read what the protesting students said This is not a lock on the door, but on faith Mahendra, vice-president of the Samajwadi Chhatrasabha, who is protesting, said- I am a Hindu and I am protesting in support of the mosque. Namaz has been offered here at Lucknow University for hundreds of years. Sealing this mosque during the month of Ramadan is extremely shameful. This is not a lock on the door, but a lock on faith. An attempt has been made to lock down religious values. This entire act is anti-constitutional. Article-25 grants religious freedom and allows us to perform religious acts according to our religion. It is shameful that in this India, we will be stopped from worshipping and offering prayers. 'BJP and RSS want to push LU into communalism' Student Prince Prakash said that BJP and RSS want to push Lucknow University into the fire of communalism. Ever since the new Vice Chancellor came here, there has been continuous controversy. After the arrival of the new VC, BJP programs are continuously being held here. During this, only people associated with RSS and BJP are allowed to enter. When Mohan Bhagwat came, all the university gates were closed. Let alone students, professors could not enter. More than 50 classes were suspended. Students cannot roam freely in their campus. They want to turn the university campus into a BJP office. Kamlesh Tiwari is the construction superintendent here, but he pays no attention to the basic facilities of the university. The drinking water is so bad that no one can drink it. The roofs of the university building are constantly breaking. The water is bad, there are no seats in the toilets, and no one pays attention to this. Countless students' memories are associated with Lal Baradari, and it is being forcibly dismantled. It is being forcibly broken down and rebuilt. 'The door was open in the morning, I offered prayers' Tauqeel Ghazi, who was sitting on the protest, said that the mosque has been closed. The mosque door was open in the morning, I offered prayers. When I came in the afternoon, the mosque door was found closed. Forces from three police stations were deployed here, but no one from the university administration came to meet us. This mosque is 200 years old, which does not come under the university, but under ASI. Locking it without any notice is condemnable. We will not leave until we get an answer and will offer all our prayers here. RSS-BJP people came here, after which it was sealed Ahmed Raza Khan alleged that prayers have been offered here for a long time. Recently, many prominent RSS-BJP figures have visited the university campus. After this, the decision was made to seal these premises. Today, police from several stations arrived at the spot, but no one from the university administration came. There is a conspiracy to incite religious frenzy here.

stories.title: Prime Minister reacts to ‘unexpected incident’ in Parliament:Says Congress cannot secure PM post by using women MPs and seat capture
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi broke his silence on the protest by Congress women MPs in the Lok Sabha 17 days ago. The PM said in Meerut on Sunday, "Before sitting on the chair, one has to win the hearts of the people." He alleged that one cannot become Prime Minister by putting women MPs forward and occupying the seat. PM Modi asked Congress, "Have you become so hollow that you are putting mothers and sisters forward for this?" The PM further said, "Congress has become a burden for the country and its politics has become disconnected from public sentiments." PM Modi said - Congress has become a burden for the country PM Modi said, Congress's unrestrained leaders are bent on destroying the country. If you want to sit on the Prime Minister's chair, you first have to win the hearts of the people. You cannot become Prime Minister by sending women MPs and occupying the seat. Have you become so hollow that you are putting mothers and sisters forward for this? PM said, Congress has become a burden for the country. I am satisfied that regarding the incident that happened in Delhi, all the allied parties of Congress showed the courage to criticize Congress extensively. For this, I publicly express my gratitude to these allies of the opposition. Congress commits sins, its allies have to suffer the consequences He said - I humbly want to request the country's media that please, when we criticize such actions, do not create headlines like 'Modi thrashed the opposition'. By saying 'opposition-opposition', you are saving Congress. The other allies sitting in the opposition have also understood that Congress commits sins, and they have to suffer the consequences. PM gave 3 big messages Om Birla had said - An unexpected incident could have happened with PM Modi Actually, on February 4, PM Modi was to respond to the Motion of Thanks on the President's address in the Lok Sabha. When the House proceedings began at 5 pm, women MPs from the opposition surrounded the chairs of the ruling leaders. This included PM Modi's chair. After the uproar escalated, the House proceedings were adjourned without the Prime Minister's speech. The next day, on February 5, the proceedings resumed. Speaker Om Birla explained the reason for adjourning the House and postponing the PM's speech a day earlier. He said, 'When the Leader of the House, PM Modi, had to respond to the President's address, opposition MPs could have caused an unexpected incident by reaching near the Prime Minister's seat.' Birla further said, 'If this incident had happened, the tradition of democracy would have been shattered. To avoid this, I urged the PM not to come to the House. The PM accepted my suggestion.' Birla called the women MPs going up to the PM's chair against decorum. He told the opposition MPs, 'If you bring posters, the House will not function. The way women members reached the PM's seat, the country saw it. This was not appropriate. It was also not in line with the dignity of the House.' What happened before the PM's speech? BJP MP Manoj Tiwari claimed that even after repeated requests from senior ministers, the women MPs did not return to their seats. They climbed onto the place where the Prime Minister sits. They created a lot of ruckus. They could have even attacked the Prime Minister. However, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi said on these allegations that it is completely false and wrong that the women were going to attack the PM. PM inaugurated the Rapid-Metro rail in Meerut Prime Minister Narendra Modi lashed out at Congress over their protest of stripping clothes at the AI Summit. Addressing a public meeting in Meerut on Sunday, he said - India hosted the world's largest AI conference. The whole country was filled with pride, but what did Congress and its ecosystem do? They turned a global event into an arena of dirty and naked politics. Congress leaders arrived in front of foreign guests by stripping their clothes.

stories.title: Fatehpur BJP MLA digs-up road worth ₹38 lakh with shovel:Warns officials, 'I will not tolerate corruption'; locals say 'Contractor will also take his cut'
stories.summary: In Fatehpur, BJP MLA Krishna Paswan dug up an under-construction road with a shovel and reprimanded PWD officials, saying corruption will not be tolerated. Acting on complaints about poor quality, he checked the road’s thickness himself and shared the video on social media, drawing mixed reactions. One user commented, ‘There is no benefit in doing this now. In 2027, the public will press the button.’ The 4-km road is being built at a cost of about Rs 37.99 lakh. Assistant Engineer Prateek Agarwal said a complaint has been received and action will be taken after an investigation. Only 500 meters of road built so far The matter concerns the Aimapur-Ratanpur road in the Dhata development block. 500 meters of the road have been constructed. A total of 4 km is to be built. Local people had complained to MLA Krishna Paswan regarding the materials and standards being used in the road construction. Seeing the public's displeasure, Krishna Paswan arrived for inspection on February 21. She herself checked the strength of the road and the materials being used in its construction. She dug the road with a shovel and checked its thickness. The investigation revealed that the road construction was not done according to the standards. During the inspection, she also took photos and videos of the road and shared them on her Facebook account. Officials reprimanded The MLA expressed displeasure over the lack of quality. Reprimanding the officials, he instructed that the road should be constructed with full quality and according to the prescribed standards, so that the general public can get better facilities. The MLA said, "We have complained to the JE, AE, XEN, and other officials of the Public Works Department. I will also send a letter on Monday." AE said - will investigate and take action Krishna Paswan warned, saying, Any kind of negligence in the construction of roads for the convenience of the public will not be tolerated. If irregularities are found in the construction work, action will be taken against the responsible officers and contractors. In this regard, Prateek Agarwal, Assistant Engineer (AE) of the Public Works Department, said that a complaint has been received and action will be taken after investigation.

stories.title: Bride reaches for job interview right after wedding in Agra:Groom holds her hand to Vikas Bhawan; says, 'I will support my wife at every step'
stories.summary: After the wedding rituals in Agra, the bride was supposed to leave for her marital home, but the groom instead took her to attend a government job interview. She had applied earlier for an Anganwadi worker post in the Child Development Department. Coincidentally, her interview was scheduled on the same day as her farewell. Understanding her aspirations, the groom completed the rituals quickly and took her to Vikas Bhawan in Agra, where she appeared for the interview in her wedding attire. The incident is from Ladukheda. See 2 pictures Full story in detail Family members also supported Manoj said that both their families also agreed to let the bride give the interview. They expressed happiness. After this, I bid farewell to Anisha from the mandap and came directly to Vikas Bhawan by car. Anisha gave the interview in her bridal attire. stories.title: 4 UP youths killed in Kota:Car rams truck on expressway; returning after Mahakal darshan
stories.summary: Four youths from Uttar Pradesh died in a road accident on the Delhi–Mumbai Expressway in Kota district on Sunday after their speeding car rammed into a truck moving ahead. The impact was so severe that the car was completely shattered, and all four occupants were trapped inside. Police and rescue teams worked for a long time to pull the youths out of the wreckage and rushed them to a hospital. However, doctors declared all four dead on arrival. The accident took place around 3:45 pm near Chechat town under the Chechat police station area. Victims were returning after visiting Mahakal temple The deceased were identified as Shresth Bajpai (21), Pranjul Chaturvedi (26), and Ankush Dubey (25), all residents of Rura village in Kanpur Dehat district, and Ansh Pratap Singh (20), a resident of Dhaulpurwa village in Gonda district. Police said all four had gone to Ujjain to visit the Mahakaleshwar temple. They reached Ujjain on Saturday and left for Kanpur on Sunday morning after offering prayers. First see PHOTOS of the accident CCTV shows speeding car swaying before crash Kota Rural SP Sujeet Shankar said CCTV footage from the expressway showed the car was moving at high speed and swaying before the crash. Police suspect the driver may have dozed off, causing the vehicle to ram into the truck ahead. The truck driver has been taken into custody for questioning, and further investigation is underway. Bodies kept in mortuary, families informed After completing initial formalities, police shifted the bodies to the mortuary of Ramganjmandi Hospital for post-mortem. The families of the deceased have been informed, and relatives have left for Kota from Uttar Pradesh. One of the deceased, Pranjul Chaturvedi, worked on a contract basis in the electricity department in Lucknow. He was married and had a young son. Family members were devastated after receiving news of his death. Police said further action will be taken after the post-mortem and completion of the investigation.

stories.title: Man spits while making roti in a hotel:Customers in Aligarh create chaos; hotel seized, worker arrested
stories.summary: A shocking incident has come to light from Aligarh, where a hotel worker was allegedly seen spitting while making rotis. Two videos of the act have surfaced on social media. It is said that a customer recorded the video inside the hotel. The incident took place on Saturday night in the Rorawar police station area of the city. As soon as the complaint was received, teams from the police and the food department reached the hotel. Officials questioned people present at the spot and collected information about the matter. Food samples were also taken and sent for testing. Later, the police arrested the accused worker and sealed the hotel. The customer records the incident There is a hotel named Sadab Chicken Darbar in the Shahjamal area. On Saturday, some people went to the hotel to eat. After placing their food order, they sat down and started talking. During this, one of them noticed the person making rotis. He was repeatedly bending over the roti. He made a video from a distance. On closer inspection, it was found that the hotel employee, Suhail, was making rotis by spitting on them. Angry locals gather outside the hotel He called some of his other friends. After that, they started creating a ruckus at the hotel. When they asked the hotel employee Suhail about spitting on the rotis while baking them, he denied it. They argued for a long time about this. During this, someone called the police and the food department to inform them. Soon, a team from the police and the food department arrived at the scene. The police took information about the incident from the people. After that, the food department team took samples. As soon as people saw the police, they started making noise. They started demanding the closure of the hotel and the arrest of the accused. The police arrested the accused, after which people calmed down. Here’s what the video reveals On February 21, two videos of 6-6 seconds each surfaced. In which it is seen that two hotel employees are standing and making rotis. One of them is wearing a white t-shirt. He also has a beard. He is bending over and spitting on the roti before baking it. After that, he is putting the roti on the fire. He is doing this continuously without any fear. Some other people are also seen passing in front of the hotel. Police arrest the accused after the video CO Kamlesh Kumar said - A video was received on February 21. In which a person was seen spitting on a roti while making it, working at his dhaba. As soon as the information was received, the police team started an investigation. Samples were sent to the laboratory for testing. stories.title: Mayawati warns against ‘self-serving’ leaders at BSP national meet:Party to contest alone; organisational revamp ahead of 2027 UP elections
stories.summary: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) president Mayawati on Sunday cautioned party leaders against pursuing “personal interests” at the cost of the Bahujan movement, asserting that those who rose within the organisation and later distanced themselves “cannot be true well-wishers of the Bahujan society”. Addressing the party’s national executive meeting at her residence in Lucknow, Mayawati said the Bahujan mission would “never forgive” those who compromised its objectives for individual gains. More than 200 office-bearers from across the country attended the meeting. Notably, leaders from Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand were not included. The meeting began at 11 am and lasted over two hours, during which Mayawati reviewed the organisational status of each state. ‘We have to obtain the master key to power’ Mayawati said that as the BSP expands, opposition forces would intensify efforts to weaken it. “We have to move forward firmly and work towards obtaining the master key to power so that society can stand on its own feet,” she said. She accused other political parties of pursuing policies against the poor, farmers and marginalised communities, alleging that corruption and a gap between words and actions had eroded public trust. In this context, she said, the BSP’s responsibility had increased to emerge as an alternative. Read the big statements made by Mayawati... Party not dependent on big capital, says Mayawati Without naming any party, Mayawati said political outfits dependent on big industrialists and wealthy businessmen gradually drift away from public interest. “The BSP does not function on the support of big capitalists. The party runs on the contributions and hard-earned money of its own people,” she said, adding that the party was free from the pressures of electoral bonds, trusts or large donations. She said only such parties could sincerely implement the welfare objectives enshrined in the Constitution. ‘Global race pushing exploitative system into crisis’ Mayawati also spoke about international economic trends, saying that countries are competing to position themselves as “First”, which she described as deepening the crisis of the exploitative global system. In such a scenario, she said, the Union government faced the challenge of protecting the interests of farmers and the Bahujan community. Referring to trade agreements, she said that if claims of deals being made on India’s terms were “not merely on paper”, it would benefit the country. ‘Those who stand with the movement will see better days’ Invoking Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar, Mayawati said those who consider him their “supreme ideal” support the BSP’s mission with their “body, mind and wealth” according to their capacity. “I believe their good days will come. The path of social change and economic freedom will open for them,” she said. Organisational overhaul ahead of 2027 UP polls The BSP chief announced a restructuring of the party’s organisational framework ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections and upcoming polls in other states. She directed that small states be divided into two zones and large states into a maximum of four zones. Previously, some large states had up to five or six zones. Office-bearers were instructed to remove inactive functionaries and appoint new workers. She emphasised the need to complete booth-level committees where they have not yet been formed. Mayawati also reiterated that the BSP would contest all forthcoming elections independently, including the Assembly elections in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu and Kerala, and would not enter into alliances. Among those present were her brother Anand Kumar, Akash Anand and senior leader Satish Mishra. State leaders present reports Leaders from different states briefed the national president on preparations. Odisha in-charge Dauram Ratnakar said the organisation had been directed to strengthen committees from district to village level and to hold programmes on Kanshi Ram’s birth anniversary. Kerala state president Subrahmanyam said the party was preparing for Assembly elections scheduled in April and had performed well in recent panchayat polls. He said vice-presidents had been appointed and candidates would be announced soon. A Kerala leader, Jayaprakash, said the party had secured a Deputy Mayor’s post and expressed confidence of winning one Assembly seat in the state. Responding to questions about the BSP’s performance in Bihar, a party functionary said candidates were identified for all seats but some were denied tickets due to criminal backgrounds. In certain cases, nomination papers were rejected because of errors in filing Form-20, he added. Meeting held at residence after office repairs The meeting was held at Mayawati’s residence as repair work is underway at the party office auditorium following a short circuit on January 14. Construction work in the open hall of the office premises is also ongoing.

stories.title: Youth vandalises Shivling at Raebareli temple:Enters temple at midnight, strikes 15 times, smashes damru
stories.summary: A youth vandalised a Shivling at the Gaurishankar Mahadev Temple in Hamirpur village under Unchahar police station area late Friday night. The accused entered the temple around midnight and damaged religious property using a trident. The entire incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed inside the temple. According to police and temple authorities, the youth first uprooted the trident placed near the Shivling. He then threw the trident at the Shivling, which broke the damru attached to it. After this, he repeatedly attacked the Shivling with the broken trident, striking it around 15 times. The repeated blows caused visible cracks and damage to the Shivling. Temple authorities said the accused created havoc inside the temple for about 10 minutes before leaving the premises. See the pictures... Incident came to light after devotees reached temple The incident came to light on Saturday morning when devotees and temple committee members arrived at the temple and found the Shivling damaged. The trident was also lying broken near the Shivling. Temple committee vice-president Loknath Mishra filed a complaint at Unchahar police station, demanding strict action against the accused. Following the complaint, police examined the CCTV footage and confirmed the vandalism. The video, which is 7 minutes and 19 seconds long, shows the youth entering the temple in a semi-naked condition late at night. He pulls out the trident placed near the Shivling and throws it forcefully, breaking the attached damru. He then repeatedly strikes the Shivling with the broken trident. The youth can also be seen walking unsteadily inside the temple and carrying the trident on his shoulder after damaging the Shivling. Police said his behaviour suggests he may have been under the influence of intoxicants. Video surfaces on social media, tensions rise The CCTV footage surfaced on social media on Sunday, leading to tension in the area. However, police said the situation is under control. The temple is located about 37 kilometres from the Raebareli district headquarters and is considered an important religious site for local residents. Accused identified, absconding Police said the accused has been identified as a resident of nearby Poore Nandi village. He is estimated to be between 25 and 28 years old and is reportedly addicted to drugs. His name has not been disclosed to avoid tension in the area. Unchahar Station House Officer Ajay Rai said a case has been registered based on the temple committee’s complaint. Police have collected CCTV footage and launched a search to arrest the accused. “The accused has been identified and is a resident of a neighbouring village. He is currently absconding. Police teams are trying to arrest him soon,” the officer said. Police have increased vigilance in the area to prevent any law and order situation.

stories.title: 35-year-old woman dies in pain at KGMU gate:Waited 12 hours, doctors gave medicine and asked her to return after a week
stories.summary: A 35-year-old woman has died after alleged negligence by doctors at King George’s Medical University (KGMU). The woman was not admitted by doctors at the Lari department of the hospital and remained in pain for nearly 12 hours without proper treatment. She later died. The incident took place on February 19. In the past five months, two other patients have also died in similar circumstances, raising serious questions about medical care at the hospital. First, read the latest case Avida Khatoon from Gonda district had a serious heart condition. According to Avida's father Nawab Ali, they brought Avida to Lari Cardiology twice in 5 days in a critical condition. The first time, Dr. Rishi Sethi's team was consulted in the OPD. The second time, when Aavid was brought on February 18, he was shown to Dr. Akshay Pradhan's team in the OPD. Despite this, proper treatment could not be received. Family pleaded, but doctors remained unmoved The family alleges that the patient was in a very serious condition. When they went to show her in the OPD on Wednesday, they pleaded for admission citing her serious condition, but the doctors did not listen to them. A junior doctor first examined the patient, then looked at the report, gave medicine, and asked them to show her in the OPD after 7 days, but refused to admit her. During this, an acquaintance staff present on the spot also recommended admission. The resident doctor silenced him by saying, "After all, are they the doctor or someone else? Treatment will be according to the doctor. Who are you?" After a 12-hour wait, they rushed towards private [care] when According to the relatives, the patient's condition was continuously deteriorating with the passage of time. In such a situation, they hoped that seeing the deteriorating condition, the doctor would admit him. With this hope, they sat in the waiting area of Lari Cardiology with him for about 12 hours. During this time, they repeatedly pleaded for continuous admission, even in the emergency. The emergency doctors shrugged off responsibility, saying to administer the medicine prescribed by the OPD doctor. Meanwhile, on the morning of February 19, when the patient's condition deteriorated significantly. Then, with the help of a local acquaintance, they set out to admit him to a nearby private hospital. Meanwhile, on the way, the patient passed away. The weeping and wailing family members then took the body and returned to their home district. Even a year ago, the patient pleaded and died in agony. Last year too, a patient admitted to the same department died while pleading with doctors for treatment. He kept crying and writhing, begging for his life. Doctors and medical staff stood by, but no one listened. Just a few minutes later, the patient died in agony. A video related to the incident also surfaced. In it, the patient sometimes writhes, rubbing his stomach, and sometimes folds his hands before the doctor. A young man says that blood is flowing from the patient's nose and mouth, and there is no one to attend to him. Just then, a female staff member in the ward starts shouting at the young man. She throws him out of the ward. Now read about the previous 2 cases Ran for 10 hours, found no treatment anywhere An 11-month-old child in Lucknow died in his mother's lap after suffering for a long time. It is alleged that he died due to lack of treatment. The family ran around the city for about 10 hours, but could not find treatment anywhere. Actually, on Thursday morning, after his condition worsened due to fever, the family admitted the child to Lokbandhu Hospital. He remained admitted there for 6 hours. Later, when his condition deteriorated, he was referred to KGMU's Trauma Center, stating that there was no ventilator. However, the child was not admitted to the Trauma Center. The child died in the ambulance outside the Trauma Center. Doctor did not give injection, breath stopped on the stretcher In Lucknow's KGMU, during the process of bringing those injured in the Kakori bus accident to the Trauma Center, already admitted patients were removed. It is alleged that during this time, one of the already admitted serious patients died in front of everyone. A video of the patient taking his last breath in a critical condition is also going viral on social media. In the viral video, a patient is seen lying on a stretcher in the Trauma Center in a very critical condition. He dies shortly after. The relatives who accompanied the patient allege that even after 3 hours, no doctor attended to him. If they had attended to the patient even after admitting the bus accident victims, the patient would have been saved. The deceased was identified as Shravan Kumar Mishra from Hardoi.

stories.title: 34 cyber fraud suspects held in Mathura’s 'Mini Jamtara':45 absconding; SP reaches with 6 ASPs, 240 police personnel
stories.summary: Mathura police on Sunday detained 34 people during a large-scale operation against suspected cyber fraudsters in villages near the Shergarh area, which is known as a hub for online scams. More than 240 police personnel, led by SP (Rural) Suresh Chandra Rawat, carried out coordinated raids in Vishambhara and Jhanjhawali villages early in the morning. Police teams arrived in over 20 vehicles and surrounded the villages to prevent suspects from escaping. According to police, panic spread among villagers as the teams entered. Some residents attempted to flee, while others hid in nearby fields. Police chased suspects, searched houses, and detained several individuals for questioning. Five-hour operation, vehicles and suspects seized The operation lasted around five hours. Police detained 34 suspects and seized five vehicles during the raids. Rawat said around 45 suspects managed to escape. Two separate teams conducted the operation. The first team detained 23 people in Vishambhara village, while 28 suspects fled. The second team detained 11 people in Jhanjhawali, and 17 escaped. Police said eight of those detained had previously been sent to jail. Two suspects are linked to more than 18 cyber fraud cases registered in different states. Police also seized mobile phones and motorcycles during the operation. All detainees are being questioned at Shergarh police station. Villages under watch after repeated complaints Police said they had been receiving continuous complaints about cyber fraud linked to the Shergarh area for several months. Investigations traced several fraud activities to villages located near the state borders. Officials said further interrogation could help uncover a larger cyber fraud network operating from the region. Earlier, on December 11, 2025, around 400 police personnel conducted a 12-hour search operation in the same area. During that operation, police identified 42 suspects and arrested 37. Why the area is called ‘Mini Jamtara’ Several villages located within a 15–20 km radius near Mathura’s border areas are known for cyber fraud activities. The region lies close to Rajasthan, about 5 km away, and Haryana, around 15 km away. Police said the proximity to multiple state borders makes it easier for suspects to evade law enforcement. Due to repeated cyber fraud cases originating from these villages, the area has come to be known as Uttar Pradesh’s “Mini Jamtara”, a reference to Jharkhand’s Jamtara district, which is widely associated with organised cyber fraud. Police said cyber gangs operating from these villages are involved in online scams, phishing, fraudulent calls, and digital extortion targeting victims across India and abroad. Further investigation is underway.

stories.title: Akhilesh targets Rambhadracharya over FIR:Offers Deputy CMs chance to become Chief Minister with 100 MLAs
stories.summary: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav criticised the FIR registered against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand in an alleged sexual exploitation case and accused the Uttar Pradesh government of acting with political motives. He also offered that either of the two Deputy Chief Ministers could become Chief Minister if they brought 100 MLAs to his side. Addressing a press conference in Lucknow, Akhilesh said ideological differences were normal, but making such serious allegations raised questions about the government’s intentions. He also referred to Jagadguru Rambhadracharya and said a case against him had earlier been withdrawn. “This government will not survive now,” he said. FIR registered on court’s order The FIR was registered at Jhunsi police station in Prayagraj on Saturday night against Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand and his disciple Mukundanand. The case was filed after Jagadguru Rambhadracharya’s disciple Ashutosh Brahmachari presented two children before the Prayagraj POCSO court and made allegations against them. The court recorded the children’s statements on camera and had reserved its order on February 13. On Saturday, the court directed the police to register an FIR. Reacting to the development, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand said the allegations were false and added that a false case would not become true. Offer to Deputy Chief Ministers Akhilesh said Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak both wanted to become Chief Minister. He offered that either of them could take the post if they brought 100 MLAs with them. “Whoever brings 100 MLAs can become Chief Minister. They will not get a better offer anywhere else. This offer is valid for one week,” he said. Questions security decisions, refers to Rahul Gandhi Akhilesh also criticised the government over security arrangements for opposition leaders. He said the Samajwadi Party would not be intimidated even if security was withdrawn. He alleged that the BJP had earlier taken away the house and security of Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to demoralise him. He said similar actions had been taken against Samajwadi Party leaders in Uttar Pradesh. “They try to insult and demoralise political opponents, but we will continue to fight,” he said. Criticism of government over Shankaracharya issue Akhilesh questioned the government’s handling of the Shankaracharya issue and said he was not treated with respect. He referred to a protest by Shankaracharya at the Sangam and said such incidents were unprecedented. He also criticised Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak and asked why leaders did not show support when Shankaracharya was protesting earlier. Remarks on economy, Japan visit, and Gorakhpur Akhilesh criticised the state government’s claims about economic progress and questioned its policies. He also took a dig at the Chief Minister’s Japan visit, referring to earlier promises to develop Varanasi like Kyoto. He further alleged irregularities in Gorakhpur’s healthcare system and questioned the functioning of medical institutions there. Akhilesh said the Samajwadi Party would continue its campaign to connect with more people and strengthen its political movement in the state.

stories.title: 'Country knows Congress is already naked, why strip more?':Launching Meerut Metro Rail, Modi quips, 'To be PM, first win hearts'
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched a sharp attack on the Congress over its ‘shirtless’ protest during the India AI Impact Summit, accusing the party of turning a global platform into an arena for “dirty and naked politics”. Addressing a public gathering in Meerut after flagging off the Meerut Metro and the Namo Bharat rapid rail, Modi said the summit had brought pride to the country, but the protest embarrassed India in front of international delegates. Modi accuses Congress of insulting global forum Referring to the protest staged by Indian Youth Congress members at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi, Modi said leaders of the party disrespected a global event attended by representatives from over 80 countries and heads of state from nearly 20 nations. “There are some political parties that cannot digest India’s success. The world’s largest AI conference was held in India and filled the country with pride. But Congress turned a global event into a platform for dirty and naked politics,” Modi said. In a pointed remark, he added, “The country already knows that Congress is naked and exposed. Then why did its leaders feel the need to remove their clothes in front of foreign guests?” He said such actions reflected the party’s “ideological bankruptcy” and showed how weakened it had become. On February 20, Indian Youth Congress members staged a ‘shirtless’ protest at the AI Impact Summit, accusing the Prime Minister of compromising national interests in the India-US trade framework. Modi said the summit was a national platform, not a BJP event, and accused Congress of disrespecting the forum and engaging in personal attacks against him. 5 key takeaways from Modi’s address 1. “Asked Congress, SP to abandon toxic politics”: Modi said he urged Congress, SP and BSP to focus on development instead of “toxic politics”. He said metro services expanded from five cities before 2014 to over 25 today under BJP rule. 2. “Earlier infrastructure vanished in scams”: Modi alleged infrastructure projects stalled due to corruption under Congress and metro technology was imported. He said his government ended scams and pushed self-reliance. He added Meerut’s new metro and rapid rail will improve connectivity and daily life. 3. “Congress defaming the country”: Modi said Congress disrespected India by protesting during the AI Global Summit. He said the event was national, not political, and aimed at showcasing India’s technological progress. 4. “Nation condemning Congress conduct”: Modi said people across the country are criticising Congress’ actions. He accused the party of disrupting Parliament and weakening its own allies through its conduct. 5. “Congress acts, allies pay price”: Modi said criticism should target Congress specifically, not the entire Opposition. He claimed Congress’ actions harm its allies, who are forced to face the consequences. PM highlights India’s rising global stature Modi said India’s global standing had strengthened significantly, with developed countries now eager to partner and sign agreements with the country. “There was a time when the Congress government could not finalise agreements because the world hesitated to deal with a government associated with scams. Today, developed countries are eager to connect with India. The world believes India can provide solutions to 21st century challenges,” he said. He said India’s progress in emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence had enhanced its credibility and influence globally. Modi said metro services operated in only five cities before 2014, while today metro networks run in more than 25 cities, making India the third-largest metro network in the world. “When Congress and Samajwadi Party were in power, infrastructure projects were marred by scams and delays. Metro technology had to be imported. We have ended corruption and moved towards self-reliance,” he said. Meerut Metro and rapid rail flagged off Earlier in the day, Modi flagged off the Meerut Metro and the Namo Bharat rapid rail at Shatabdi Nagar station and travelled to Meerut South station, where he interacted with students. He also inaugurated and dedicated development projects worth ₹12,930 crore in Meerut and nearby areas. The Namo Bharat rapid rail corridor will cover the 82.15-km distance between Delhi and Meerut in about 55 minutes, connecting Sarai Kale Khan in Delhi to Modipuram in Meerut through 13 stations. The Meerut Metro will run between Begumpul and Meerut South with seven stations, improving intra-city connectivity.

stories.title: Husband poisons 3 children, slits wife's throat:Hangs himself after murders, bodies found 3 days later
stories.summary: In Kasganj, a man allegedly killed his wife and three children before hanging himself. Reports suggest he first poisoned the children and then slit his wife’s throat. The bodies reportedly remained inside the house for three days before anyone discovered the tragedy. Neighbours said the incident came to light when a young man visited the house on Saturday evening to deliver a wedding invitation. The visitor knocked repeatedly, calling out names, but received no response. On inquiring with neighbours, he discovered that the house had been silent for three days. Suspecting something was wrong, they alerted the police. Police broke open the iron door using chisels and hammers. Inside, they found the husband’s body hanging from a rope. The three children’s bodies were on the bed, while the wife’s body was lying on the floor. Foam was seen at the children’s mouths. The deceased were identified as Shyamveer (50), his wife Ramshri (48), daughters Prachi (12) and Akanksha (10), and son Girish. The case falls under Kasganj Kotwali jurisdiction. DIG Prabhakar Chaudhary stated that locals believe financial stress may have triggered the incident. Neighbours noted that the family had been struggling with their son’s neurological condition. Inside the house, it appeared that the stove had not been used for several days, and there were no utensils. Marriage 13 years ago, family lived in 1010 room Shyamveer married Ramshri of Nagla Vadik 13 years ago. Their elder daughter Prachi studied in seventh grade, younger daughter Akanksha in fifth, and son Girish in fourth grade. Shyamveer had two sisters who were married. Originally from Nagla Bhojraj village, he ran a welding business with his brothers before moving to Amanpur eight years ago. There, he rented a small room behind a petrol pump, measuring roughly 10×10 feet, where the family lived. The front area was used as a shop. Was troubled by son's neuro disease According to Shyamveer’s uncle, Girish suffered from a neurological disorder affecting the head veins, which required costly treatment. Recently, Shyamveer borrowed ₹1,000 from a neighbour and had sought financial help from others, but received little support. This situation reportedly left him mentally distressed. Youth arrived to give wedding card, then incident came to light Neighbours said the house had been locked for three days. The incident came to light when a young man arrived with a wedding invitation on Saturday. Upon failing to get a response, he alerted locals, who then informed the police. DIG Prabhakar Chaudhary, DM Pranay Singh, and SP Ankita Sharma visited the scene. The bodies were sent for post-mortem. SP Ankita Sharma said the police received the report at 6:30 pm. Upon breaking the iron door, they found Shyamveer hanging from a rope. The children and wife were removed afterward and sent for post-mortem. Father said - Did not get along with son, no communication for four months Shyamveer’s father, Nem Singh, stated he had divided his 12 bighas of land among his four sons three years ago. Shyamveer had not spoken to his father for the past four months due to strained relations. His in-laws allege that Shyamveer’s father never offered support.

stories.title: Rajbhar's makes strategic bid in Purvanchal:Rallying Brahmins and extremely backward communities ahead of 2027 assembly polls
stories.summary: With the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections on the horizon, political parties across the state have begun preparing for the contest. The Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) plans to demonstrate its political strength today, 22 February, by convening a massive social harmony rally in Azamgarh’s Ataurliya Assembly constituency, aiming to gather a crowd of around one lakh. Notably, the party has invited 10,000 members of the educated Brahmin community to participate. SBSP national president Om Prakash Rajbhar stated that the party’s objective is to unite all communities. “The Brahmin community conducts rituals from birth to death. They are an enlightened society and guide those who have gone astray. No one can progress without their support,” he said. While SBSP’s main base lies in Ghazipur, the party has chosen to hold the rally in Azamgarh’s Ataurliya. Questions arise: why the sudden focus on Brahmins, and what political objective does the party aim to achieve through this social harmony rally? SBSP claims to gather crowd of one lakh SBSP has claimed it will gather a crowd of one lakh at the rally, scheduled for Sunday at 11 am in Ahiroula. Leaders of allied parties, including the BJP, Nishad Party, and Apna Dal (S), have also been invited. To understand the significance of SBSP’s social harmony rally, discussions were held with Om Prakash Rajbhar and political experts closely observing Eastern UP. Five key objectives of the rally emerged: Subhaspa contested on 18 seats in 2022 In the 2022 Assembly elections, SBSP contested 18 seats in alliance with SP, winning six. Rajbhar himself contested from Zahurabad in Ghazipur, securing victories in two seats, while the party also won one seat each in Basti, Mau, Ballia, and Jaunpur. In 2017, SBSP had contested 8 seats in alliance with BJP and won 4. Rajbhar said preparations are underway for 62 seats in 2027, though exact seat allocations in alliances will be determined later. Reason for choosing Azamgarh instead of Ghazipur Although Rajbhar established his political base in Ghazipur, he is now eyeing the neighbouring Azamgarh district. In Ataurliya Assembly constituency, Rajbhar voters number only 15,000–20,000, yet SBSP is actively engaging the extremely backward communities there. Rajbhar also cites law and order concerns: SP-supporting Yadav MLAs have allegedly created an atmosphere of fear and intimidation, involving land grabs, threats, and assaults. The extremely backward communities live under this constant pressure with no effective representation. Why is Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) interested in Brahmins? SBSP's entire politics revolves around the Rajbhar community. For the past 2 years, they have been moving forward with a strategy to connect with extremely backward classes to increase their support base. For this, they are continuously holding rallies of extremely backward classes across the state. For the first time, SBSP has also appealed to Brahmins under the pretext of social harmony rallies. Senior journalist Anand Rai says - The Brahmin community is upset with the UGC and the insult of Shankaracharya at the Magh Mela and the beating of his disciples by pulling their hair. In such a situation, Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SUBHASPA) wants to send a message to the Brahmin community by inviting them to their social harmony rally that their doors are also open for them. There are a large number of Brahmin voters in Purvanchal. On many seats, if they join with Rajbhar voters, they will become decisive. SUBHASPA chief Omprakash Rajbhar is engaged in wooing Brahmins to achieve this political goal. The meaning of social harmony rally According to Anand Rai, Rajbhar began his political career with BSP, which initially united Dalits aggressively before expanding to other communities. Known as an experimental leader, Rajbhar initially used similar strategies to consolidate the Rajbhar community. In 2022, while allied with SP, Rajbhar made controversial statements against upper castes. However, after returning to the BJP alliance in 2023, his political approach shifted. Past setbacks, such as his son losing the Mau Lok Sabha seat, motivated him to unite core Rajbhar voters, extremely backward communities, and upper-caste voters. Rajbhar's goal is to increase NDA's lead in Purvanchal by expanding his own base In 2022, SP won all 10 Assembly seats in Azamgarh, delivering a blow to NDA in Basti, Ambedkarnagar, Ballia, and Mau. Rajbhar claims SBSP has a voter base of 10,000–30,000 per seat in Azamgarh. During the last elections, BJP lost by 3,000–10,000 votes on these seats while SBSP was allied with SP. Now, as part of NDA, Rajbhar asserts that the alliance can sweep all 10 seats in Azamgarh in 2027. What does Rajbhar want to achieve through the rally Senior analyst Suresh Bahadur Singh noted that Rajbhar’s claim of gathering one lakh supporters sends a message to political parties, especially BJP, that NDA’s success in Eastern UP requires SBSP. Rajbhar’s influence extends across Ataurliya, Shahganj, and Khetasarai. By mobilizing core supporters along with extremely backward communities and Brahmins, he aims to strengthen his bargaining power within NDA ahead of 2027. He stated that Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath was invited but could not attend due to PM Modi’s event in Meerut. Leaders from allied parties, including Nishad Party, are expected to participate. Rajbhar estimates that drawing 10,000 people from each constituency will achieve the one lakh target. Extremely backward communities, including Prajapatis, Pals, Nais, Gond Rajbhars, Chauhans, Mauryas, Nishads, Binds, Kevats, and Mallahs, are expected to participate. Rajbhar addressed local grievances by ensuring repair of two severely damaged roads: 21 km from Captain Ganj to Ahiroula and 9 km from Sikandarpur to Nariyanv. Work on both roads is set to start this month, winning him local sympathy. Residents attending the rally plan to express gratitude for these improvements. In conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Rajbhar also commented on SP chief Akhilesh Yadav, Nasimuddin Siddiqui, and BSP chief Mayawati. He criticized Siddiqui for lacking a strong grassroots base and described Mayawati as the unparalleled leader of Dalits today. He emphasized that if BSP allies with Congress or AIMIM in 2027, SP will be marginalized. On the question of a crowd of one lakh, Rajbhar said - There are 10 assembly seats in Azamgarh. If even 10-10 thousand people come from each assembly, the number will reach one lakh. Speaking at the local level, more people are coming from Phulpur, Atrauli and Gopalpur. Apart from Rajbhar, there is a good number of extremely backward classes in Azamgarh. This includes Prajapati, Pal, Nai, Gond Rajbhar, Chauhan, Maurya, Nishad, Bind, Kevat, Mallah in large numbers. People from all communities are participating in this rally. Garnered sympathy by getting approval for 2 dilapidated roads in Atrauli In Atrauli assembly constituency, a 21-kilometer road from Kaptanganj to Ahiraula has been dilapidated for about 15-16 years. It was not built during the SP government and no initiative was taken in the NDA government either. Omprakash Rajbhar says that when I came here recently, people said that Minister sir, please get the road constructed. About 50 village heads from the area demanded it in writing. Similarly, the 9 kilometer road of Sikandarpur-Narianv was also in poor condition. I got both roads approved. Work has started on the Sikandarpur road. Work will also begin this month on the Captainganj-Ahiraula road. Its bond will be made in 2 days. Sources say that the repair of these two dilapidated roads has created sympathy for Om Prakash Rajbhar among the people of the area. People of the area want to thank him by participating in the rally. Read what Rajbhar said about Akhilesh, Nasimuddin and Mayawati Om Prakash Rajbhar in conversation with Dainik Bhaskar openly discussed Akhilesh Yadav's PDA, Nasimuddin Siddiqui who left Congress to join SP, and Mayawati. Regarding Nasimuddin, he said that he first went to Congress. Then he used to say that he joined the party to make Rahul Gandhi the Prime Minister. What happened? Now after joining SP, he's talking about making Akhilesh the Chief Minister. What vote bank have they brought to SP? Muslims were already with SP. He's not even a leader of Azam Khan's stature in SP. Azam's voice had strength. When he spoke, it felt meaningful. There's no weight in his words. When you listen to his speeches, it seems like he's crying. He doesn't even have influence in his own community. As far as appeasing Dalits is concerned, there is no bigger Dalit leader in any party today than Mayawati. Mayawati has done a lot for Dalits. Nasimuddin was never a leader with mass support. He was a polished leader. This is today's politics. He is the type of leader who advances through sycophancy and flattery. Their job was to earn money for Mayawati and stand on one leg with folded hands at her command. In my words, these are spent cartridges. They were leaders because of Mayawati. They cannot get votes for SP in their own Banda district, let alone anywhere else. In 2024, Dalits got trapped in SP-Congress's lies and deception. Both parties secretly propagated that the constitution was in danger and reservations would end. But when Mayawati's rally happened in Lucknow on October 9, everyone's truth was exposed. If BSP forms an alliance with Congress and Owaisi's AIMIM party in 2027, SP won't even be visible in opposition.

stories.title: FIR filed against Avimukteshwaranand in child sexual abuse case:POCSO charges registered in Prayagraj; disciple also named
stories.summary: An FIR has been registered against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati in connection with the alleged sexual exploitation of minor children. The case was filed at Jhunsi Police Station in Prayagraj and also names his disciple Mukundanand. Police said a case under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act has also been registered against two to three unidentified persons. According to Jhunsi Station House Officer Mahesh Mishra, the FIR was registered following directions from the POCSO court in Prayagraj on Saturday. The order was issued by Special Judge (POCSO Act) Vinod Kumar Chaurasia after reviewing the investigation report submitted by the Prayagraj Police Commissioner. The court directed police to register a case against Avimukteshwaranand, his disciple Mukundanand, and other unidentified persons. The court had earlier reserved its order on February 13. The case was brought before the court by Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj, a disciple of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, who presented two minor children and levelled serious allegations. The children’s statements were recorded on camera in court as part of the proceedings. Speaking after the order, complainant Ashutosh Brahmachari said they had approached the police earlier but did not receive any response. He said they were forced to seek judicial intervention and expressed relief over the court’s decision. He alleged that the minors were subjected to sexual exploitation and abuse. In its order, the court noted that the allegations against the accused were serious and fell under cognisable offences, making police investigation necessary. The court cited Supreme Court rulings stating that while FIR registration is not mandatory in every case, a magistrate has the discretion to order an FIR if police investigation is required. The judge directed the concerned police station to immediately register the FIR and conduct an independent and impartial investigation in accordance with the law. The court also instructed authorities to strictly follow provisions of the POCSO Act, protect the identity and dignity of the victims, and submit the investigation report before the court. Shankaracharya said, ‘Rambhadracharya got case filed through his disciple’ Shankaracharya calls allegations fabricated, says truth will emerge After the court’s order to register an FIR, Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati denied the allegations and claimed the case was fabricated. He said the sexual exploitation charges would be proven false and alleged that the complainant, Ashutosh Brahmachari, a disciple of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, had a history of filing false cases. He further alleged that Ashutosh Brahmachari threatens people and extorts money, and claimed the FIR was part of a conspiracy due to ongoing ideological and verbal disputes with Rambhadracharya. Avimukteshwaranand said the case was filed to silence him for raising his voice on cow protection issues against the government. He added that he would fully cooperate with the legal process and expressed confidence that the truth would come out during the investigation. He also stated that if he had committed any wrongdoing, he would have regretted it, but insisted the allegations were false. He called for a swift investigation and remarked that police function under the government’s authority. Referring to criticism from Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, he claimed such public statements send indirect messages to law enforcement. Responding to allegations regarding a “Sheesh Mahal” inside the monastery, he said the premises are open and house 100–200 people, with regular movement of visitors. Ashutosh Brahmachari challenges Deputy CM and Akhilesh Yadav Complainant Ashutosh Brahmachari issued a public challenge to Samajwadi Party leader Akhilesh Yadav and the Deputy Chief Minister, urging them to accompany him on foot to Vidyamath in Varanasi. He claimed he wanted to show the fifth floor of the monastery, which he referred to as a “Sheesh Mahal,” alleging that Avimukteshwaranand lives in luxury there. He also made serious claims about the presence of female associates at the premises. Ashutosh announced that he would begin a public march seeking justice and would go door-to-door to raise awareness. He said individuals facing such serious allegations should not remain in influential positions and demanded strict legal action. Complaint was filed in court on February 8 Ashutosh Brahmachari, a disciple of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, had filed a complaint on February 8 in the Special POCSO Court in Prayagraj. In his complaint, he accused Avimukteshwaranand of sexually exploiting minor children under the guise of operating a gurukul. Based on this complaint and subsequent proceedings, the court later directed police to register an FIR and initiate an investigation under relevant legal provisions. On the court notice, Avimukteshwaranand's lawyer filed a reply on February 10. Then Shankaracharya told Dainik Bhaskar that we have given all evidence in court. We have faith in the judiciary. Since we started raising our voice for the protection of mother cow, the government and some people have not been liking it. February 13: Ashutosh Maharaj left the court crying On February 13, Judge Vinod Kumar Chaurasia heard the case. The complainant Ashutosh Maharaj advocated the case himself. He had told the judge that 2 disciples came to me and narrated their story of sexual exploitation. An FIR should be registered against Shankaracharya and investigation should be conducted. I only hope for justice from the judiciary. Shankaracharya's lawyer had opposed this. Said that these are just allegations. We need some time to prepare for the case. On this, Ashutosh Maharaj had told the judge - I am being threatened to be killed by bombing my car. I could be murdered. You should hear the statements of children who have been victims of sexual abuse. Judge cleared the courtroom, heard children's statements After this, the judge ordered the courtroom to be cleared. Only lawyers from both sides remained in the room. Then the children were brought into the courtroom. The children narrated their story of exploitation before the judge. All these statements were made inside the closed courtroom. These statements were also recorded on camera. The judge had asked - Who are you to these children? Special Judge Vinod Kumar Chaurasia had asked some questions to Ashutosh Maharaj. He had asked what relation are you to these victims? On what basis did you become their guardian? Then Ashutosh Maharaj had said that according to guru tradition, I have come for justice. When the victims did not get justice anywhere, these children contacted me. After this, the judge had reserved his decision. February 21, meaning today's date, was set to decide whether there would be an FIR against the Shankaracharya or the case would be dismissed. Shankaracharya and Rambhadracharya came face to face after dispute in Magh Mela Ashutosh Brahmachari, disciple of Jagadguru Rambhadracharya, the Tulsi Peethadhishwar of Chitrakoot, is also the main petitioner and party in the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi versus Shahi Mosque Idgah case. After the dispute in Magh Mela, Rambhadracharya and Avimukteshwaranand came face to face. Ashutosh Maharaj first complained to Police Commissioner, then went to court 6 days after January 24, i.e. Mauni Amavasya, Ashutosh Maharaj made 2 complaints against Avimukteshwaranand to the Police Commissioner of Prayagraj. First Complaint: Minor children are kept in Avimukteshwaranand's camps and gurukul. They are made to do personal service, gather crowds, work in events and carry palanquins. There are also concerns about sexual exploitation of children. Children were made to work in large events like the Magh Mela. This violates child rights and labor laws. There are also suspicions of illegal weapons in the camp. Investigation should be done into assets exceeding income and multiple bank accounts. The role of a person named Mukundanand should be investigated. Second Complaint: Ashutosh Maharaj accused Avimukteshwaranand of creating fake letterheads and documents. He said that in the Magh Mela area, Avimukteshwaranand was claiming himself to be the Shankaracharya of Jyotish Peeth. He was sending letters to officials using letterheads and documents made in the name of "Jyotish Peeth/Shri Shankaracharya Camp". These letterhead-letters are fake and misleading. They are being used to mislead the administration and general public. These letterheads have the date January 24, 2026 (Magh Shukla Panchami). Using this date, letters were issued in the name of "Sri Shankaracharya Camp". Their validity has been questioned. How did both victim children reach Ashutosh Maharaj? Ashutosh Maharaj alleged that when the administration took no action on his complaint, he filed a case in court on February 8. He had told that on behalf of my trust, a grand yagna of Mata Shakumbhari Devi was being performed at the Magh Mela for the liberation of Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi. Two disciples came to my camp, who were minors. They made several revelations before me. They expressed their desire to become disciples. Said that they are unsafe. They asked me for police protection and legal assistance. The children told me that Avimukteshwaranand and his associates kept us with them. Committed misconduct many times. All this was done for a year. Misconduct was also done in the fair area during Mahakumbh-2025. During Magh Mela-2026, both children were again subjected to misconduct. Avimukteshwaranand's disciples would pressure the children by saying that this is guru seva. This will bring blessings. The children also told that they are asked to sleep with Avimukteshwaranand as well. Where did Ashutosh Maharaj file complaints Ashutosh Maharaj said that he had filed a complaint at Jhunsi police station on January 24. On January 25, he emailed complaints to the Police Commissioner and Police Superintendent Magh Mela. On January 27, he sent a complaint by post to the Police Superintendent Magh Mela. However, no FIR was registered. After this, I started receiving threats. Then I sought shelter in court. Who is Ashutosh Maharaj? Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj was born in a Pandit family in Kandla town of Shamli. His father Rajendra Pandey worked as a conductor in private buses running on Delhi Road. Ashutosh Maharaj joined the committee of the ancient Shakumbhari Siddha Peeth Temple in Kandhla. Currently, he is also its manager. His family's uncle Pradeep Pandey is a priest in the temple. In 2022, he took initiation from Jagadguru Rambhadracharya. Since then, he has been living a life of asceticism. Know When The Dispute Started On January 18, during the Mauni Amavasya of Magh Mela, Avimukteshwaranand was going for a bath in a palanquin. That's when the police stopped his palanquin. The police asked him to walk to Sangam. However, the Shankaracharya's disciples did not agree. They started moving forward with the palanquin. This led to pushing and shoving between Shankaracharya's disciples and the police. Police took several disciples into custody. The police also beat up a sadhu at the police post. This angered Shankaracharya and he insisted on getting his disciples released. Then the officers tried to explain to them, folded their hands, but they did not agree. After this, the police took several other supporters of Shankaracharya into custody. Shankaracharya's palanquin was pulled and taken 1 km away from Sangam. During this, the palanquin's canopy was also broken. Shankaracharya could not even take a bath. After this, he sat on a protest. Despite this, when there was no hearing, Shankaracharya returned to Varanasi on January 28.

stories.title: Property greed leads to MBA graduate’s murder:Body buried at home in ‘Drishyam’-style, suspect misleads investigators with fake narratives
stories.summary: The murder case of an MBA graduate in Jhansi reads like a crime thriller. The accused had prepared a script similar to the movie Drishyam to mislead the police. Initially, he claimed that he had killed his brother, Tariq, over a dispute regarding tea and then buried the body. Using this fabricated story, he tried to protect himself. However, when the police matched evidence from the scene with his statements, the entire deception was exposed. Under intense interrogation, the accused broke down and confessed, revealing the full truth. He admitted that he had planned the murder deliberately to seize the family property. He told the police- "I wanted to grab the entire property. That's why I planned to kill my elder brother Tariq. My brother-in-law, who lives in the neighborhood, also helped. I brought him at 4 AM after waking him up. Shortly after, I woke up Tariq and attacked him with an axe. Struck twice on the head and once on the forehead with the axe. Then slit his throat with a knife. Brother died struggling. Dug a 5-foot deep pit and buried the body." The incident occurred in the Bihari Pura neighborhood under Prem Nagar police station. Tariq was murdered on 9 February, and the crime came to light 10 days later. The police arrested the accused, Masharik, who then led them to the burial site where the body was recovered. Now read the complete incident in sequence... Built a two-story luxurious house Bihari Pura is located about 5 km from Jhansi Railway Station. Mirza Aqil Beg, the father of the victims, was a primary school teacher who had built a two-storey house of 2,500 sq. ft. He died in a road accident in 2022, leaving behind two sons, Tariq Beg and Masharik. After their father’s death, the elder son Tariq was given a clerical job on compassionate grounds. Tariq, aged 40, had completed his MBA and was preparing for competitive exams, so he refused the job. It was then allotted to his younger brother, Masharik. Their mother, a retired court peon, often stayed at her parental home due to her mental health condition. Masharik married a local woman, Muskan, on 9 December 2025. How the murder mystery was solved On 9 February, both brothers were at home while their mother was away. At 4 am, Masharik called his brother-in-law, who came along. Masharik then woke Tariq, attacked him, and buried him in a five-foot-deep pit inside the house. The next day, when the mother called, Tariq’s phone was switched off. Masharik told the family that Tariq had gone out. He misled them for four days before filing a missing person report on 15 February. The family continued searching for Tariq, but Masharik showed no interest in helping. Suspicious, the maternal uncle alerted the police. On 19 February, the police summoned Masharik for questioning. Police arrived at the house with the accused, where he misled the police for 3 hours. At 12 midnight, the SSP and magistrate reached the spot. When strictness increased, the accused revealed the grave location. After this, the body was exhumed. Now read the accused's confession... Masharik told the police: "I live on the first floor with my wife, while my mother and Tariq lived on the ground floor. On 9 February at 4 am, I woke my brother-in-law and brought him to the house. Then I went downstairs where Tariq was sleeping. I knocked on the door, he didn’t open and started arguing. In anger, I hit him with an axe. Then I slit his throat with a knife. He died instantly. To conceal the crime, we buried him inside the house." The axe, knife, hoe, and shovel used in the murder were recovered from a nearby drain. Dug a 5 feet deep pit and buried the body, added salt Masharik described how he dug a 5-foot-deep pit, stripped Tariq’s body, poured 100 kg of salt over it, covered it with bricks, cleaned the blood, washed the clothes in the washing machine, burned the phone in the forest, and disposed of the weapons 3 km away. Accused's in-laws absconding On 14 February, when Tariq’s maternal uncle, Mohammad Salim, learned about the disappearance, he checked CCTV footage in the neighborhood. Masharik’s in-laws, fearing exposure, locked the house and fled. For three days, Masharik misled his family, deepening the uncle’s suspicion. The uncle informed the police, which led to Masharik’s interrogation and eventual revelation of the crime. Call Records Will Reveal the Mystery The police are also examining the call records of Masharik, his wife Muskan, and brother-in-law Talib. CDRs have been retrieved and are expected to reveal more details about the crime. Masharik admitted his brother-in-law’s involvement. Muskan and Talib remain missing. Their presence is key to fully understanding the case. Employees remove Tariq’s body from the burial site for post-mortem. Search for Wife and Brother-in-law BB GTS Murthy stated that Masharik has confessed that his brother-in-law was complicit in the murder. A case has been registered against all three individuals. Authorities are currently searching for Muskan and Talib, and the complete truth will only emerge once both are traced and questioned.
