stories.title: Film loss sparks crisis for Rajpal Yadav:20 cheques bounce; court warns of property seizure over unpaid debt
stories.summary: Bollywood actor Rajpal Yadav was at the peak of his career until 2010, delivering popular performances in hit films such as Dhamaal, Phir Hera Pheri, Golmaal, Dhol and Bhool Bhulaiyaa. He was one of the most sought-after comic actors in the industry at the time. In 2010, Rajpal decided to produce a film titled Ata Pata Lapata. Facing a shortage of funds, he reportedly borrowed ₹5 crore from a businessman to finance the project. The film, made at a cost of around ₹11 crore, was released the same year but turned out to be a major box-office failure, earning only about ₹42 lakh. Following the losses, the businessman sought repayment. However, Rajpal was unable to return the borrowed amount. The dispute eventually reached court. Over time, Rajpal sought extensions and issued multiple cheques towards repayment, but the cheques reportedly bounced. As the case progressed, the court ordered his imprisonment. Rajpal was lodged in Tihar Jail and has been granted interim bail from February 17 to March 18. During this period, he has reportedly made partial payment. Once the interim bail period ends, he will be required to surrender. If the outstanding amount is not cleared, the court may proceed with the attachment of assets reportedly worth double the borrowed sum. In today’s Sunday Big Story, we trace the entire journey of this case, from the film’s release in 2010 to the legal battle that followed. Meeting through MP, wife's emotional message Rajpal Yadav originally belongs to Kundra village of Shahjahanpur district. After studying acting at Bhartendu Academy in Lucknow and then National School of Drama in Delhi, he entered films. He started his career with the film ‘Dil Kya Kare’ in 1999. 5.1 inch tall Rajpal's comedy was loved by people. He started getting films one after another. He worked in films like Shool, Jungle, Ek Aur Ek Gyarah, Mujhse Shaadi Karogi, Hungama, Garam Masala, Waqt, Hera Pheri, Partner, Bhool Bhulaiyaa, Bhoothnath. In most of these films, he worked as a comic actor. In total, Rajpal has worked in more than 150 films across different languages. In 2010, he decided to make his own film. At that time, Rajpal met with SP MP Mithilesh Kumar Katheria from Shahjahanpur. They had a good relationship. Rajpal told him about the film Ata-Pata Lapta. He discussed arranging funds after explaining the expenses. MP Mithilesh Katheria arranged a meeting with city businessman Madhav Gopal Agarwal. They had a long discussion. Rajpal demanded 5 crore rupees. Madhav Gopal said he didn't have that much money. On the first day, no money was given to Rajpal. On next day, Rajpal Yadav's wife Radha sent several messages to Madhav Gopal on WhatsApp. These messages mentioned giving money. Many messages were emotional. This continued for 4-5 days. Rajpal would also call Madhav Gopal occasionally. Madhav Gopal got an agreement signed at his Delhi office. It was decided that whether the film runs or not, whether the censor board passes it or not, after one year Rajpal would have to pay 7.5 crores and 50 lakhs legal fees for 5 crores. Rajpal signed that agreement. He and Radha Yadav took personal guarantee. The film had many renowned artists The film's shooting began in 2011. It was a comedy film. Rajpal Yadav was in the lead role. Radha Yadav produced the film. The film starred actors like Ashutosh Rana, Asrani, Vijay Raj, Yashpal Sharma, Zakir Hussain, Manoj Joshi, Govind Namdev, and Virendra Saxena. The film was still in production when a year passed. Madhav Gopal Agarwal called Rajpal and asked how he would pay the money. Rajpal said - The film is not completed yet. Once the film is released, I will pay the money. Madhav Gopal accepted Rajpal's words and extended the agreement. This time Rajpal again signed and gave 7 blank checks. After one year, the agreement was renewed. When the agreement was extended for the second time, Rajpal told Madhav that the film would not be released without his permission. He suggested that Madhav could keep the film's negative print if he wanted. Madhav refused to do so. On October 26, 2012, the film's trailer was released. Amitabh Bachchan was invited to the release of a song from Ata-Pata Lapata. Madhav learned about this through TV. That's when he felt that Rajpal was deceiving him because the trailer was released without informing him. He filed a petition against the film in Delhi's Karkardooma Court. When Rajpal requested again, Madhav agreed. The film was released on November 2, 2012. It crashed in the first week itself. Made for 11 crore rupees, the film only earned 34 lakh rupees in the country. The film's worldwide business was 42 lakh rupees. Meaning, the film went into a loss of more than 10 crores. After this when Madhav asked for money, Rajpal's response was that the film flopped. We will pay the money later. Court sentenced wife also in 2013 In Delhi's Karkardooma Court, Justice Murlidhar was handling this case. Madhav gave them a new application on April 21. Said that we are ready to settle for 10 crore 40 lakhs. Rajpal had also shown agreement to this amount. Rajpal Yadav gave 7 new checks in Delhi High Court. When the checks were deposited on the scheduled dates, all checks bounced again. In the affidavit that Rajpal filed in court on December 2, 2013, it had his wife's signature. During court investigation, that signature turned out to be fake? The court sent Rajpal to 10 days judicial custody that same day. Since Radha Yadav had a baby in her lap, showing leniency towards her, ordered to keep her in Registrar General's office until office closing time. Also ordered Rajpal's lawyer to leave this case. Issued contempt notice to the Oath Commissioner who made the fake affidavit. While being sent to judicial custody, Rajpal told the judge, 'This is the first case of my life. I request to be given one chance. Madhav Gopal will get his money. I am ready to pay him even today.' The court did not listen to any arguments. However, after spending 3 days in Tihar Jail, Rajpal was released. On January 15, 2014, a new date was set for this case. Madhav said, ‘Cried like children for his money’ After 2014, Rajpal started distancing himself from Madhav. Madhav says that when Rajpal would come to court, it would look like a show of power. Rajpal would be accompanied by more than 50 people. It is alleged that these people would threaten Madhav. This affected Madhav and many times he would not even come to court. On the other hand, Rajpal would frequently change lawyers. In 2015, Rajpal Yadav signed the third supplementary agreement. New checks were given again. The result was the same. This time too, all the cheques bounced. In 2016, the court reprimanded Rajpal Yadav during the hearing. According to businessman Madhav, Rajpal promised to repay the amount and sought an out-of-court settlement. Madhav agreed, but the payment was never made. When this was brought to the court’s notice, the judge fined Madhav ₹25,000, stating that settlement talks cannot continue informally once the matter is under trial. Madhav said he travelled to Mumbai several times to recover his money, but Rajpal often avoided meeting him. He claimed he even broke down emotionally in front of the actor, but received no repayment. Supreme Court refuses to hear plea Rajpal later approached the Supreme Court in 2016, but it declined to hear the case. The matter then returned to the Delhi High Court. Loan or Investment Dispute In an interview, Rajpal claimed the businessman had invested in the film for his grandson, not given a loan. Madhav denied this, saying no one in his family was linked to acting. He pointed out that loan agreements, personal guarantees and blank cheques proved it was a loan — a view the court accepted. Rajpal was a well-known celebrity, and in the early stages the court appeared to take a lenient view. However, as proceedings continued and facts emerged, the court adopted a stricter stance. On several occasions, it remarked that Rajpal seemed unwilling to repay the money. Each time he appeared in court, Rajpal would fold his hands and seek more time, assuring that payment would be made later. This pattern continued until 2025. In October 2025, he paid ₹75 lakh to Madhav for the first time through two demand drafts, with an assurance that the remaining amount would be cleared soon. Did Rajpal really not have money? Rajpal Yadav has been active in the film industry for 27 years and has worked in several major projects. From just his last five films — Kathal, Dream Girl 2, Bhool Bhulaiyaa 3, Champion and Baby John — he reportedly earned ₹7–8 crore. He is said to have received around ₹1 crore each for Kathal, Dream Girl 2 and Baby John, and ₹2–3 crore for the other two films. Rajpal Yadav surrendered in court on February 5. He said in the media that I don't have money. After this, many people extended help. Also gave money. Madhav's lawyer Navneet Singh says - He had filed a fresh bail in court. The court directly said that we will not hear the case on merit. The case will be heard only when they are ready to pay the money. After staying in jail, he has given 2 crores 10 lakh rupees. 75 lakh rupees were given last year. Still have to pay a total of 6 crores 15 lakh rupees. Rajpal has said he will pay the full amount going forward. Had applied for nephew's wedding. The court has granted him bail till March 18. Rajpal came out on interim bail and reached Shahjahanpur. He says - Jail was like a meditation camp for me. Every system in the country is being upgraded. Jails should also be modernized. There should be a smoking zone in jail. We are not promoting smoking. But when it is sold in the country, there should be a separate place for it in jails and reform houses. We ourselves are victims of smoking. Trying hard to quit, but haven't been able to quit completely yet. If money not paid, property worth double loan amount will be seized Will Rajpal not have to pay money after going to jail? What will happen if money is not paid? For answers to these 2 questions, we spoke with Lucknow High Court lawyer Mukesh Sharma. He said that since Rajpal has taken the money, he will have to pay it back. He has gone to jail now because he did not pay the money on time. The checks he gave bounced. This means he is doing this deliberately. The checks bounced multiple times. This means he is also committing fraud. The court looks at this matter. That's why the Supreme Court did not hear his case. Mukesh Sharma says - According to the Supreme Court, if a person commits fraud in this way, first a case is registered against them under section 138. Then a notice is given. Then a non-bailable warrant is issued. Finally, attachment of property happens. If Rajpal does not pay this money, his property worth double the amount will be attached. It will be sold and the money will be given to those from whom it was taken. That 5 crore is worth 25 crore rupees today Madhav Gopal gave Rs 5 crore to Rajpal in 2010. He says - if we consider bank's 12%, today that 5 crore would be 24 crore 70 lakh rupees. I gave the money and remained troubled for 16 years. I cried like a child for my own money. I handed the case to senior lawyers. Spent more than 1 crore rupees for this. Received threats from Rajpal's people. For the last 5 years, I haven't even gone to court. I have faith in the court, justice will come from here. I just want my money back.

stories.title: Japan turns saffron ahead of Yogi Adityanath’s visit:Indian community prepares grand welcome with saffron flags and devotional chants
stories.summary: Ahead of Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s visit, the Japanese capital Tokyo is awash in saffron. Even before his arrival, streets have been decorated with saffron flags, turning the city into a hub of celebration. Slogans of ‘Jai Shri Ram’ echo through the streets, while every corner is adorned with saffron banners. The Indian community is energetically preparing for the welcome, chanting ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’. Cultural programmes, devotional songs, and traditional dances are being organised. Children, women, adults, and the elderly are joining hands to give the visit a festive touch. Locals say the welcome is not just an event but a vibrant display of cultural unity and devotion by Indians living abroad. The CM is set to depart for Singapore and Japan today, with the agenda of attracting investment to Uttar Pradesh. Experts believe Yogi’s visit will infuse new energy into spiritual and cultural ties between India and Japan. With existing interest in yoga, meditation, and Indian traditions, this trip could further strengthen these connections. Discussions on investment, technology, and cultural exchange are also expected during the visit, potentially opening new avenues of cooperation between UP and Japan. What did the Indian community say about Yogi's visit? Find out Will visit Hanuman temple According to Dainik Bhaskar, the CM will also visit a Hanuman temple located around 40–50 km from central Tokyo. The visit is considered significant from both cultural and religious perspectives. May wear shoes instead of sandals Typically known for wearing sandals, CM Yogi might opt for formal shoes during this foreign trip, factoring in international protocol and weather conditions. CM Yogi will travel in 600 km/h speed Maglev Will depart for Singapore today According to the CM’s office, Yogi will first depart for Singapore. His tour is scheduled for 23–24 February in Singapore and 25–26 February in Japan, aiming to attract investment, enhance industrial collaboration, and promote foreign investment in UP. Supporters view the CM’s traditional attire abroad as a symbol of India’s cultural identity on the global stage, while the opposition sees it as symbolic politics. Visited Mauritius-Myanmar after becoming CM Yogi Adityanath’s first overseas visit after becoming CM was to Myanmar from 5–7 August 2017 for an international conference. He later visited Nepal, Mauritius, and Russia. A devotee of the Nath sect, he has consistently worn saffron robes, maintaining this attire even on foreign trips and official events.

stories.title: Ashutosh Maharaj challenges Avimukteshwaranand to undergo medical test:Says, 'I will accept him as Shankaracharya', states he belongs in jail like Asaram
stories.summary: 'I challenge you (Shankaracharya). If you are pure, undergo a medical examination at a government medical college. I will then accept you as Shankaracharya. Also have your disciple Mukundanand medically examined. It will become clear whether you are truly celibate or not.' This is what Ashutosh Maharaj says after a POCSO court ordered an FIR to be registered against Shankaracharya. Following the order, Dainik Bhaskar spoke to Maharaj, who is the complainant in the case. He stated, “These are Asaram’s babas; they belong in prison. Do not defame the seat of Jagadguru Shankaracharya.” Responding to the FIR registered against him, Maharaj said, 'Fine, let us assume that, according to them, I am a criminal. But will that conceal their crime? Will young disciples not receive justice because of me?' He further alleged, 'If they are fearless, why are attacks being orchestrated against me? Why were attempts made to snatch items from my car? Why did Avimukteshwaranand offer me ₹1 crore? We have conducted a sting operation against them.' ‘We have come to seek justice. We will not step back, even if we are killed. I have saved all ethe vidence on email. Even if they murder me, no one will be spared.’ Read the full interview Have you been a disciple of Avimukteshwaranand? We were never his disciples. Our guru has been a Sanatan Dharma teacher. During the Shri Krishna Janmabhoomi campaign, we met many saints. Avimukteshwaranand was among those we were in contact with. He had given us a letter some time ago, and we raised our voice over it. At that time, we were unaware of any such alleged conduct. His disciple Mukundanand was close to us. A guru-brother’s disciple is like a nephew-disciple. That is how we were connected. When did you distance yourself from him? When we became aware of his actions, we went from door to door seeking justice for the young students (batuks). Justice has now been sought in the temple of justice — the court. How do you know about the alleged Sheesh Mahal and swimming pool in his ashram? The Sheesh Mahal is larger than a royal palace. The facilities in his room surpass those in the home of India’s Ambani. There are even facilities that should not exist in such a place. A swimming pool has been constructed. I was told that when he bathes there, female companions massage him. Who are these companions? A woman named Purnima calls him Swamishree. A former judge’s daughter informed us and sent some evidence. Sisters and disciples associated with the ashram told us that there are rooms where misconduct occurs and women are tortured. In my words, it is torture; in theirs, entertainment and revelry. What else do you know about the ashram? I sensed something was wrong. When rooms were locked, why were children inside? Why only two children daily? First, Mukundanand would enter, then the children. I stayed there several times. I saw children crying and heard sounds once or twice. Some disciples wondered if someone was being beaten. But no one could investigate because access to the upper level was restricted. The next day, some children came down with bloodstains on their dhotis from behind. At that time, no one spoke. Later, children who had escaped and reached our ashram told us what had happened. What is the ‘Pancham Tal’? Just as the Chief Minister has a ‘Pancham Tal’, they built one in their Vidyamath, a luxurious fifth-floor room where these alleged acts occurred. You plan a foot march to Varanasi. When will it begin? We will undertake a foot march to Varanasi with young disciples to expose these alleged misdeeds. I invite former UP Chief Minister Akhilesh Yadav to join. The Deputy CM also used to call frequently; he should come as well. I am ready to reveal everything. Why are 21 cases registered against you? There are two types of history-sheeters, criminals and those with politically motivated cases. The cases against me were filed during the Samajwadi Party and BSP governments. None are personal. Regarding Mata Sheetla Temple, a government receiver has been appointed. If I intended to seize it, I would have done so. Many cases are false, and in most we have been acquitted. A list released with a police seal has itself led to a case at that police station. If genuine, why file a case? Why does Shankaracharya allege you are linked to cow slaughterers? Provide evidence. Allegations are common, even against Chief Ministers. Justice is decided by the court. The case against them was registered by the court, not a police station. Is the judge lying? He examined pen drives and CDs. Were you offered bribes? We were offered ₹50 lakh, then ₹1 crore. We conducted a sting operation. We are not for sale. Is a gangrape case registered against you? I underwent a medical examination and submitted it to the court. The case dates to the BSP government era. The High Court granted a stay. The complainant was an 80-year-old woman. I was very young then. Would I assault an elderly woman? When did the alleged exploitation occur? It is not appropriate to disclose children’s details. Section 22 prohibits revealing such information.

stories.title: Aparna-Prateek seen together for first time after divorce controversy:Celebrate daughter’s birthday in Lucknow; welcome guests together
stories.summary: Following a public divorce controversy in Lucknow, Aparna Yadav and her husband Prateek Yadav, have appeared together for the first time. The occasion was their daughter Prathama’s birthday celebration, where the couple jointly welcomed guests and posed for photographs. Several BJP leaders attended, including Neeraj Singh, son of Rajnath Singh. On 19 January, Prateek Yadav shocked many by announcing on social media that he intended to divorce Aparna. In his posts, he described her as selfish and accused her of damaging family relationships. However, just nine days later, he reversed his decision, stating that the couple had reconciled. Aparna is currently with the BJP and serves as Vice-Chairperson of the Uttar Pradesh State Women’s Commission. Divorce announcement Prateek (38), step-brother of Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, made two Instagram posts within eight hours on 19 January declaring the end of his marriage. In the first, he wrote that he would divorce ‘this selfish woman’ as soon as possible, alleging she had ruined his family ties and cared only about fame and influence. He said his mental state was poor and accused her of being an “evil soul”. In the second post, he claimed that the person who had broken his relationships with his mother, father and brother cared only about fame. He described the situation as a story of broken trust built on lies and pretence. Prateek's Instagram posts... Political differences behind the rift According to family sources, tensions had existed for three years, since 2022, when Aparna left the Samajwadi Party and joined the BJP against Prateek’s wishes. On 5 February 2025, he had posted three critical messages about her on social media, later deleting them. In those posts, he alleged she had made his life “hell” and was motivated solely by money and power. Aparna broke her silence on 22 January. In a television interview, she said she was being targeted because of her political and social activism but remained strong. She alleged that some people were deliberately attempting to create rifts in relationships to exert mental pressure and push her out of public life. She described the matter as not merely personal but also political and social, suggesting attempts were being made to defame her. Reconciliation after 9 days Nine days after his announcement, Prateek posted a photograph with Aparna captioned: “All is Good. Champions are those who resolve their personal and professional problems. We are a family of champions.' In a video, he acknowledged a “fierce and dangerous dispute” on 19 January but stated they had resolved it together. He added that those unhappy with their reconciliation could “go to hell'. Marriage and family background Prateek and Aparna married on 4 December 2011 after a relationship that began in 2001 through email exchanges following a birthday party. Aparna, originally Aparna Bisht from Uttarakhand, adopted the name Aparna Bisht Yadav after marriage. She studied in Britain and is the daughter of a journalist who later became State Information Commissioner, and Ambi Bisht, a former property officer at the Lucknow Development Authority. Both parents are now retired. Prateek is the only son of Mulayam Singh Yadav’s second wife, Sadhana Gupta, a nurse. Mulayam Singh publicly acknowledged him as his son but named Akhilesh Yadav, his son from first wife Malti Devi, as political successor. The couple has two daughters. Their wedding in Saifai, Etawah, was a high-profile event attended by thousands, including Mulayam Singh Yadav and Bollywood actor Amitabh Bachchan. Aparna’s political journey Born on 1 January 1990, Aparna studied at Loreto Convent, Lucknow. She contested the 2017 Assembly elections on an SP ticket from Lucknow but lost to BJP’s Rita Bahuguna Joshi. When denied a ticket in 2022, she left SP and joined the BJP, becoming the first member of the Mulayam family to do so. Though she sought a BJP ticket from Sarojini Nagar, she did not receive one. In 2024–25, she was appointed Vice-Chairperson of the Women’s Commission. Known for her outspoken views, Aparna often diverged from the SP line, and Akhilesh Yadav did not publicly respond when she left the party.

stories.title: Government official assigned to fetch underwear:‘Royal’ protocol list in Prayagraj puts 50 officers on task
stories.summary: A ‘royal-style’ protocol prepared for a senior BSNL official’s proposed visit to Prayagraj has sparked widespread discussion. Around 50 officers were assigned duties, and a detailed chart was circulated outlining specific responsibilities for each of them. The list reportedly covered arrangements for everything from the officer’s breakfast and lunch to even personal items such as underwear. The protocol document soon went viral on social media, drawing sharp criticism and ridicule. BSNL director’s proposed Prayagraj visit sparks protocol controversy The proposed visit of BSNL Director (CFA, Consumer Fixed Access) Vivek Banjal to Prayagraj has triggered controversy after an elaborate protocol assigning duties to nearly 50 officers surfaced online. The visit was scheduled for February 25 and 26, during which the Director was to hold review meetings with officials, visit key BSNL facilities, and also travel to the Jain pilgrimage site in Kaushambi. A detailed protocol order was issued two days in advance by the Deputy General Manager (DGM) at the GM Office in the Prayagraj Business Area. It outlined comprehensive arrangements to ensure the visit was conducted smoothly. Duties assigned for every personal and official requirement To manage the Director’s visit, committees comprising around 50 officers and staff members were formed, with each group assigned specific responsibilities. The protocol covered arrangements for official meetings, logistics, hospitality, and personal convenience. One committee was tasked with preparing welcome kits containing items such as water bottles, chocolates, chips, fruit juice, glasses, and napkins. Another committee was assigned to arrange personal-use kits, which included towels, underwear, soap, shampoo, oil, slippers, and grooming items such as mirrors and combs. The protocol also ensured arrangements for daily essentials, including drinking water, refreshments, and other personal necessities during the Director’s stay. Official order directed staff to ensure successful visit The order stated that Director (CFA) Vivek Banjal’s visit to the Prayagraj Business Area was scheduled for February 25–26, alongside senior officials including the Chief General Manager of the UP (East) Circle and the Principal General Manager (CFA) of the UP (East) Circle. All officers and employees were instructed to actively participate and contribute to ensuring the successful completion of the visit. The order specifically mentioned that nominated committee members were responsible for completing the tasks assigned to them within the stipulated time. Protocol Withdrawn After Facing Public Criticism The protocol document went viral on social media, drawing criticism and sparking debate over the nature of the arrangements. Following widespread backlash and ridicule, the order was withdrawn the very next day. The incident has since raised questions about administrative practices and the extent of protocol arrangements for senior officials’ visits. The very next day after the protocol was issued, someone posted it on social media. Along with this, it was also criticized calling it a royal arrangement. Many users also made various comments about it. After this, an office order was suddenly issued by the DGM on Friday itself. It stated that the previously issued order regarding the proposed visit is cancelled with immediate effect. Also, any previously issued guidelines in this regard should be considered ineffective. Cancelled order states... It is hereby informed that the office order, which was issued regarding the proposed visit of Director (CFA) to Prayagraj BA, is cancelled with immediate effect. All concerned officers/employees are requested to take note of this cancellation. Act accordingly. Any instructions previously issued in relation to the above-mentioned order shall be considered invalid. PRO Ashish Gupta stated- An order was previously issued regarding the proposed visit. It was later cancelled. As such, the guidelines that were in place have automatically become ineffective.

stories.title: Will Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand face jail in sexual abuse case?:Under POCSO, child’s statement alone can lead to life imprisonment
stories.summary: The POCSO court of Prayagraj has ordered filing of FIR against Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati for sexual exploitation. The court gave this order based on allegations by 2 minor children. Now questions are being raised whether Shankaracharya really sexually exploited the children? What will happen after this POCSO court order? What legal options will Shankaracharya have? Will he be found guilty? If found guilty, what punishment will he get? Let's look at the answers to these questions... First, know why police had not registered the case? We spoke to Mukesh Sharma, a lawyer at Allahabad High Court's Lucknow bench. He says, police must have had some doubts about the allegations, that's why the case was not registered. The doubt was because the sexual exploitation of children was happening for a year, why didn't the victims come forward for so long? They came forward at a time when Shankaracharya was sitting on a protest against the administration. Another reason could be that the police may not have registered an FIR in such allegations considering Shankaracharya's stature. What options will Shankaracharya have if an FIR is filed? In response to this, Mukesh Sharma says, Shankaracharya can appeal against this FIR in the High Court, can demand its dismissal by calling it wrong. Even if a case is registered after this, he can get interim bail. After interim bail, the matter will be investigated, there will be no arrest. How important will the medical report be in POCSO? If an FIR is filed against Shankaracharya, the children will undergo medical examination. Ajit Yadav, a lawyer at Lucknow bench of Allahabad High Court says that in POCSO cases, while the minor's statement is sufficient, medical examination is considered the most crucial evidence. The medical examination will be based on the allegations made by both children. If such evidence is found in the medical examination, the case will proceed further. Based on that, the relevant sections under POCSO will be applied. Ajit Yadav says, this is a high-profile case, so investigating officers will tread very carefully. The children's allegations, dates, times, people involved, circumstances at that time - everything will matter. Investigation will follow FIR, then punishment will be discussed Action is expedited in cases related to sexual abuse of children under POCSO Act 2012. There is a provision to complete the hearing within 1 year from the date of cognizance. Within this one year, the investigating officer has to file a chargesheet within the first 2 to 3 months. Supreme Court lawyer Shashwat Anand says, after investigation of this case when the chargesheet is filed then arrest can happen, after this the trial will begin. Both parties will present their evidence. After a year, the court will be in a position to deliver judgment. There are several clauses in POCSO, depending on the level of offense, the court will pronounce judgment accordingly. In this case, Ashutosh Maharaj's lawyer is SK Manas. He says- Shankaracharya is considered a pillar of Sanatan culture and called God, if God himself has descended to crush the culture, imagine what could be the plight of Sanatan culture. The POCSO court has ordered the case citing 5-6 lines, which is significant in itself. CM Yogi has used the word Kalnemi for him, therefore this case is ordered to be filed not against Shankaracharya, but against Kalnemi. Clash with police in Prayagraj on February 18, sexual abuse complaint filed 6 days later On January 18, during Mauni Amavasya bath at the Prayagraj Magh Mela, Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand had a confrontation with the fair administration. Shankaracharya sat on a dharna outside his camp. Exactly 6 days after this incident, on January 24, 2026, Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj arrived at Jhunsi police station in Prayagraj with two minor Batuks. He filed his complaint, but the police took no action. The next day, on January 25, a complaint was sent via email to the Prayagraj Police Commissioner and Police Superintendent Mela. On January 27, a complaint was sent by post to Mela SP. However, no FIR was registered. After this, on February 8, Ashutosh Maharaj went to court with both children. Ashutosh Maharaj's 2 complaints against Shankaracharya- First complaint: Minor children are kept in Avimukteshwaranand's camp and gurukul. They are made to do personal service, crowd gathering, programs and carrying palanquins. There is also suspicion of sexual exploitation of children. Children were made to work in large events like Magh Mela. This is a violation of child rights and labor laws. There are also concerns about illegal weapons in the camp. Investigation should be done into assets exceeding income and multiple bank accounts. The role of a person named Mukundanand should be investigated. Second complaint: Ashutosh Maharaj accused Avimukteshwaranand of creating fake letterheads and documents. Said that in the Magh Mela area, Avimukteshwaranand was claiming himself to be the Shankaracharya of Jyotishpeeth. He was sending letters to officials using letterheads and documents in the name of "Jyotishpeeth/Sri Shankaracharya Camp". These letterheads and letters are fake and misleading. They are being used to mislead the administration and general public. These letterheads bear the date January 24, 2026 (Magh Shukla Panchami). Letters were issued using this date in the name of "Sri Shankaracharya Camp". Their authenticity has been questioned. On February 10, the lawyer on behalf of Shankaracharya filed a reply stating - since they started raising their voice for the protection of Gomata (cow), the government and some people have not been liking it. By what right did Ashutosh Maharaj become the complainant? On February 13, Judge Vinod Kumar Chaurasia heard the case. Ashutosh Maharaj told the court that two disciples came to me and narrated their story of sexual harassment. We want a case to be registered against Shankaracharya. The court first asked Ashutosh how did you become their guardian/protector? Ashutosh Maharaj said - According to guru tradition, I have come for justice. The victims did not get justice anywhere, that's why these children came to me. The court was cleared. The statements of both children were recorded in front of the judge and lawyers from both sides. The children gave statements in court- During Mahakumbh 2025, Avimukteshwaranand committed misconduct with them. The other disciples used to say that this is guru seva. This will bring blessings. Now know what the court said? The court cited several Supreme Court judgments and said that it is not mandatory to file an FIR in every case. The magistrate has to decide at their discretion whether to direct an FIR or proceed as a complaint. If police investigation is necessary in the case, it would be appropriate to register an FIR and investigate. Court's observation- The case involves allegations of serious sexual offense. POCSO Act applies. Police investigation is necessary to gather evidence. It would not be appropriate to proceed with the case only as a private complaint. The court ordered that the concerned station in-charge should immediately file an FIR. Conduct independent and impartial investigation according to law. Provisions of POCSO Act should be followed. Protect the identity and dignity of victims. Investigation report should be submitted to court. Now the two cases where accused were both convicted and acquitted Case 1: Engineer who molested around 50 children sentenced On February 20, a husband and wife were sentenced in a Banda case. The Banda court gave death sentence to the husband-wife who sexually exploited around 50 children. They used to sexually abuse children and sell obscene videos-photos abroad through dark web. The husband Rambhavan was an engineer in irrigation department, while wife Durgavati was a housewife. CBI arrested Rambhavan on November 18, 2020. Both had sexually exploited more than 50 children. On the 88th day of arrest, CBI filed a 700-page chargesheet in Banda court. The chargesheet was based on medical reports and statements of children. Case 2: Driver spent 8 years in jail, later honorably acquitted On December 7, 2025, a special POCSO court in Mumbai acquitted a 56-year-old driver. The driver had spent 8 years in jail. He was accused of sexually harassing a 17-year-old disabled girl. The court while acquitting said - The victim's side could neither explain the basic facts of the incident, nor the girl's age, mental capacity, and there were discrepancies between medical reports and her statements. Special Judge ND Khose said - The evidence presented by the prosecution is weak. The accused has already spent 8 years in jail, therefore he is being acquitted. The accused's lawyers Vaishali Sawant and Kalam Sheikh told the court that there was an old dispute between the victim's family and the accused. Due to which he was falsely implicated.

stories.title: Stray dogs maul 8-year-old girl to death in Lucknow:Body found 500 meters away from house in a field, flesh hanging
stories.summary: Stray dogs killed an 8-year-old girl by mauling her in Lucknow. The blood-soaked body of the girl was found in a field about 500 meters away from home. Her face was completely mutilated. Pieces of flesh were hanging from various places. The incident occurred around 6 PM on Sunday in Tarauna village of the Rahimabad police station area. The deceased was identified as Anshika. She was a class 1 student. She had left home alone when the dogs attacked her. Some women from Tarauna village had gone towards the fields in the evening. During this time, they saw someone lying on the ground in the field. The women got scared and came to the village to tell people about this. Upon receiving the information, villagers reached the field with sticks. The villagers saw that Anshika's blood-soaked body was lying in the field. Dogs were sitting in a pack at some distance The villagers said that after this, we informed Anshika's family members about this. The family members reached the spot and brought the body home with our help. They also informed the police. The villagers said that where Anshika's body was lying, fierce dogs were sitting at some distance from there. Those dogs were from the neighboring village. Face badly mauled, flesh torn apart Villagers said that no one saw when the dogs were mauling the girl. But looking at the girl's body, it's clear that she was attacked by dogs. There were marks of dog bites on the girl's face. Her face was completely mauled. Pieces of flesh were torn out in several places. There were dog paw prints at the spot where the body was found. Anshika was the youngest among 3 siblings Anshika was the youngest of three children of her parents. Her father, Dilip Kashyap, said that Anshika had left home in the evening. A while later, they received news of her death. Mother Soni fainted upon seeing the body. Other family members are also in terrible condition, crying continuously.

Saharanpur man kills friend to fake his own death:Body burnt in car as part of plan to dodge rape case
stories.summary: A young man killed his friend to fake his own death in Saharanpur. He placed the body in a car, poured petrol, and set it on fire. The accused did this to escape punishment in a rape case. After the incident, the accused fled to Dehradun. To hide his identity, the main accused got his hair cut. He got a new SIM card and called his brother to file a missing person report, so that police would consider him dead. The brother filed the missing person report. On February 25, a burnt body was found in an Alto car near the Kali River in Amrapur forest by the roadside. When police investigated, the case was uncovered. On February 28, four people, including the main accused, were arrested. During interrogation, the accused confessed to their crime. The case belongs to the Gagalhedi police station area. SSP Abhinandan said that on February 25, the village head of Chaurakhurd informed the police that a burnt Alto car was standing near a culvert on the Chandpur road. In which there was a burnt body of a person. The police and the field unit reached the spot and started an investigation. The car was identified based on its burnt number. Investigation revealed that the car had been sold multiple times. The young man named Arjun had last purchased it on February 16, 2026. Meanwhile, Arjun's brother Vijay Sagar reached the police station and informed that Arjun has been missing since February 24. His phone is switched off. Police started the investigation. Meanwhile, on February 27, Babita, a resident of Mohammadpur Kandhela village, reached the police station with her son Akshay and other family members. She said that my son Rohit has been missing for 5 days. Arjun, whose body was found in the car, was Rohit's friend. He used to visit his house. DNA test revealed the body was Rohit's Babita had told the police that Rohit had borrowed ₹1.60 lakh from Arjun. Which he was unable to repay. Police became suspicious. Police intensified the investigation. Police conducted a DNA test on the dead body found in the car. DNA matched with the family members. The dead body found in the car was Rohit's. Police handed over the body to the family. Now police started searching for Arjun. Police began monitoring Vijay Sagar, the brother who had filed Arjun's missing report. The number was put under surveillance. Meanwhile, it was discovered that Arjun was alive. He was living in Dehradun. On February 28, Arjun came to meet his younger brother Vijay Sagar. Police arrested both of them near the Badkala flyover. Now read the accused's confession... When the police interrogated him, Arjun told the truth. Arjun said - In 2024, I raped a minor in Dehradun. I went to jail in that case. I was afraid that I might get sentenced. So I made a plan to fake my death to escape. In jail, I met Sarik. He was imprisoned in a kidnapping case. Friendship with Rohit began in July 2025 A year later, I got out of jail on bail. Then I started working at a private finance company in Jhabreda. During this time in July, I became friends with Rohit. I got him addicted to alcohol. Then I lent him about ₹1.60 lakh. After this, on the night of February 24, I took Rohit with me. My other companions, Robin and Sarik, were also with me. We made Rohit drink alcohol. When he was intoxicated, we strangled him to death with a muffler. After this, we placed the body on the driver's seat of the Alto car, poured petrol, and set it on fire. So that it would appear that Arjun died in an accident. Police have recovered a Kia Sonet car from the accused.

stories.title: ‘No action for cows, we will launch religious fight’:Shankaracharya adds, 'Yogi not proving himself to be Hindu'
stories.summary: ‘40 days time was given, 30 days have passed, but Yogi has not proved himself as a true Hindu. No effort has been made for ’Gau Mata'. Therefore, we will have to declare a religious war for the dignity of 'Gau Mata'. We will have to draw a line to see who is in favour of the cow and who is against it.' It has become necessary that after 40 days, on the 41st day, we should go to Lucknow and announce the beginning of the religious war for the dignity of ‘Gau Mata’. In the remaining 10 days, there will be a final wait of hope. After that, on March 11, after the period of 40 days is over, it will be necessary to make the announcement.' Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand said this while targeting CM Yogi. He said that from March 11, they will declare a religious war in Lucknow to declare ‘Gau Mata’ as the national mother. Regarding Israel and America's attack on Iran, Shankaracharya said that when hypocrisy increases, such wars happen. If there is a religious war, there will be no need for such physical wars. We responded in 12 hours; they couldn't respond even in 30 days Shankaracharya said - We were asked to explain within 24 hours how we could call ourselves Shankaracharya? We answered in 12 hours. After that, to investigate whether some 'Kalnemi' have entered our society. We had asked Adityanath ji, who is handling the responsibility of the Chief Minister wearing saffron clothes, to explain how you are a real Hindu. Tell us in 40 days. When 10 days passed, we assessed whether these people did anything in these 10 days or not. When 20 days passed, we assessed again. Today, after 30 days have passed, we have again assessed whether they have gained any clarity about being Hindu. Have they done anything about the demand of the country's Sanatani people regarding ‘Gau Mata’? Sadly, 30 days have passed, and so far, no such effort has been seen from their side for ‘Gau Mata’. Yes, during this time, Yogi was abroad for almost a week. Now, he can say that I wasn't even here. However, you cannot make excuses to go abroad by ignoring the sentiments of the majority of people in your country. Therefore, it has been confirmed that no effort was made by them. Read what he said about the America-Israel and Iran issue Shankaracharya said - Wars keep happening all the time. Sometimes with weapons, sometimes for power balance. Every country keeps making plans against the others. But just because there's a war somewhere, should we abandon protecting our dharma? Should we give permission to slaughter and eat cows because war has broken out? Sell them, satisfy the British. Cut up our mother cow and serve it to them. This is why our ancestors participated in the freedom struggle to drive out the British. So that when they leave, we can slaughter cows and send them. This is such a despicable thing. This war is happening because religious wars have stopped. When there is religious war, people will have respect for religion in their minds. The hypocrisy that is happening in the name of religion will end. Such wars happen when hypocrisy increases. The President of America says that we should get the Nobel Peace Prize. He also makes all the arrangements for war. This is hypocrisy. When such hypocrisy spreads in the world. When hypocrisy is not controlled, such wars happen. Therefore, religious war is very necessary, so that such material wars do not happen. People should not suffer loss of life and property. We do not wish for peace; let the heat come out, so that peace happens automatically. Therefore, let it happen. Read the latest case of ongoing controversy regarding Shankaracharya in detail There was a dispute between Shankaracharya and the administration on Mauni Amavasya on January 18 at the Prayagraj Magh Mela. 8 days later, on January 24, Jagadguru Rambhadracharya's disciple Ashutosh Maharaj filed a complaint with the Police Commissioner. In this, allegations of sexual exploitation of children were made during Magh Mela-2026 and Mahakumbh-2025. A petition was filed in the Special POCSO Court on February 8, alleging inaction by the police. On February 13, 2 children were presented in court. Their statements were recorded on February 21. On the court's orders, an FIR was registered at Jhunsi police station the same day. Shankaracharya, his disciple Mukundanand, and 2-3 unknown persons were named as accused in the FIR. On February 24, Shankaracharya accused Prayagraj Additional Commissioner Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring against him. He also filed an anticipatory bail petition in the Allahabad High Court. On the 27th, the High Court granted bail to Shankaracharya.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:US, Israel dropped 1,200 bombs on Iran within 24hrs; UP village linked to Khamenei’s legacy more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest updates from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. US, Israel dropped 1,200 bombs on Iran within 24hrs The Israeli Air Force said it dropped more than 1,200 bombs on Iran over the past day in joint strikes with the United States, including the attack that killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. 2. BLO found hanging in Fatehpur school; denied leave for daughter’s wedding A Shikshamitra working as a Booth Level Officer (BLO) for SIR duty in Fatehpur allegedly died by suicide inside the school where he was posted. The incident came to light around 5 PM on Saturday. According to reports, the school peon found him hanging from a noose in a classroom and immediately alerted the family and police. 3. UP village linked to Khamenei’s legacy; mentor’s roots traced to Barabanki After reports of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s death, a village in Barabanki, Uttar Pradesh, has drawn attention for its historical link to Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khamenei. Residents of Kintur village claim Khamenei’s ancestors belonged to their village and were known in Iran as “Musavi Hindi.” Locals say several descendants later moved to Iran and contributed to religious and social developments there. 4. Mob attacks US embassy in Pak’s Karachi, 12 dead The United States and Israel continued airstrikes on Iran for the second consecutive day, intensifying tensions across the Middle East. Iran has reportedly retaliated with strikes targeting US military bases in Israel and across nine countries in the region. 5. Protests in Lucknow after Khamenei’s death; Shia community raises slogans Following the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an attack by the United States and Israel, protests erupted in Uttar Pradesh. In Lucknow, thousands from the Shia community took to the streets. Women were seen crying and beating their chests as protesters raised slogans of “Khamenei Zindabad” and “Down with America and Israel.” 6. Attackers flee to Delhi after slitting YouTuber Saleem Wastik’s throat YouTuber Saleem Wastik from Loni on the Delhi-Ghaziabad border is battling for his life after two unidentified attackers entered his house and slit his throat. He is admitted to Guru Teg Bahadur (GTB) Hospital in Delhi with multiple knife wounds and remains in critical condition. CCTV footage tracked the attackers for about 2.5 km before they fled towards Delhi. 7. 17 killed in blast at Nagpur's detonator manufacturing company A massive explosion occurred on Sunday, 1 March 2026, at SBL Energy Limited, an ammunition manufacturing company located in Raulgaon, Katol taluka of Nagpur, Maharashtra. In this explosion, 17 workers were killed, and 18 were injured. Many of the injured are in critical condition. 8. 7-year-old Vaishnavi dies of burns in Lucknow; village mourns A wave of grief swept a Barabanki village after seven-year-old Vaishnavi, who had suffered 60% burns, died after a week at Lucknow’s trauma centre. Just days before Holi, her body was brought home for the last rites. Villagers gathered in the narrow lanes in tears, praying that no family should face such tragedy. 9. March likely to bring intense heat wave; temperature may touch 40°C Winter officially ends on March 1, but this year rising temperatures are already raising concerns. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), March could be among the warmest months on record, with temperatures in Uttar Pradesh likely to touch 40°C and the summer expected to be harsher than last year. 10. Banks will not operate for 18 days in March 2026 In March 2026, banks will not operate for a total of 18 days in different states across the country. According to the calendar issued by the RBI, banks will remain closed for 11 days at different locations next month, in addition to 5 Sundays and the second and fourth Saturdays.

stories.title: Wife murdered by strangulation, body dumped in drain:Husband deletes CCTV footage to escape crime; had love marriage 5 years ago
stories.summary: A 28-year-old woman was allegedly murdered by her husband in Kanpur, who strangled her to death and dumped the body in a drain to destroy evidence. According to police, the accused wrapped the body of his wife, Akriti Singh alias Ruby, in a blanket and threw it into a drain located about 500 metres from their house in Saraimeeta area of Panki. He also placed stones on the body to prevent it from floating and to conceal the crime. Body spotted in drain, police informed The incident came to light on Saturday morning when passersby noticed a human head in the drain and immediately alerted the police. Officers reached the spot, recovered the body and sent it to the mortuary for post-mortem examination. Later that night, Akriti’s brother identified the body and confirmed her identity to the police. See 2 images- Love marriage five years ago Police said Akriti had married the accused in a temple five years ago after a love relationship. The couple had been living together in the Panki area since then. Initial investigation suggests there were ongoing domestic disputes between the couple, which eventually led to the murder. Husband and two relatives arrested Police have arrested the accused husband along with his two brothers, who are suspected of helping him dispose of the body. All three are currently being interrogated. During questioning, the husband confessed to strangling his wife. CCTV footage deleted to hide evidence Investigators also discovered that CCTV footage from the house had been deliberately deleted in an apparent attempt to destroy evidence and mislead the investigation. Police said further questioning and forensic examination are underway, and additional legal action will follow based on the findings. Frequent fights over jewellery worth lakhs, says victim’s brother The victim’s brother said Akriti had married Nitin of her own choice five years ago, and the family had supported the marriage. She regularly visited her maternal home, where their mother had given her jewellery worth several lakhs. According to the brother, Akriti would wear the jewellery during family functions but would later return it to her maternal home for safekeeping. However, her husband Nitin often objected to this and insisted she bring the jewellery back with her. When Akriti refused, he would question her decision. She reportedly told him she feared he might sell the jewellery and spend the money, which led to frequent arguments between the couple. Police mediation on February 26, murder committed after returning home The brother further revealed that Nitin had assaulted Akriti on February 26. Following the assault, Akriti approached the Panki Temple police post and filed a complaint. Police called both Akriti and Nitin to the police post and facilitated a compromise between them. After the mediation, the couple returned home. However, later that same day, Nitin allegedly assaulted Akriti again. He then strangled her to death, wrapped her body in a blanket, and dumped it in a drain located about 500 metres from their house. He also placed stones over the body to prevent it from floating and to conceal the crime. Body found in drain, police alerted by passersby On the morning of February 28, passersby noticed a body in the drain and immediately informed police by calling the emergency helpline number 112. Police from Panki police station reached the spot and recovered the body. Initial attempts to identify the victim were unsuccessful, and the body was sent to the mortuary. Later, family members identified the deceased as Akriti Singh alias Ruby, after which police intensified the investigation and arrested the accused husband and his relatives. Police conducting postmortem today Late Saturday night when family members got information about the incident through social media, they contacted Panki police. When police showed the photo to brother Rahul, he identified the body as his sister Akriti Singh aka Ruby. Today on Sunday, police are conducting the postmortem. After postmortem, police will hand over the body to Akriti's family. Then the last rites will be performed. Husband Confessed - Murdered by Strangulation Police arrested the accused husband Nitin Savita, brother-in-law Deepu and Rahul late Saturday night. Father-in-law Suresh Master was also taken into custody but was released due to poor health. DCP MS Kasim Abdi said- The accused are being interrogated. The accused husband has confessed to murdering by strangulation and disposing of the body. Accused Deleted Home CCTV Footage DCP said - Action will be taken based on the complaint from the maternal family. How did he take the body from house to drain? Did anyone else help in this? What was the main reason for murder... investigation is ongoing on these and other points. The accused has deleted the footage from home CCTV cameras. Footage from other nearby cameras is being examined.

stories.title: Boyfriend Ends Life After Girlfriend’s Death in UP's Sultanpur:Leaves note saying 'life meaningless without her'; couple buried together
stories.summary: A lover committed suicide after his girlfriend's death in UP's Sultanpur. Both were in a relationship for 3 years. The girlfriend died in a road accident on the afternoon of February 25. Upon hearing the news, the young man was heartbroken. He reached her home to see her one last time and learned that she had been buried. The young man named Vineet went straight to the cemetery. He started digging the grave. When people present there stopped him, he left and never returned. Two days later, on February 28, his body was found hanging in a garden. The family buried him near his girlfriend's grave. Meanwhile, Vineet's Instagram post has come into light. It said “Hello brothers this is my last video. What will I live for now when my life is no longer in this world. Please forgive me brothers, bye". Understand entire step by step sequence of events Vineet (25), a resident of Ghatampur, was the youngest of three brothers. He had studied till fourth grade. His father died 5 years ago. He met Arpita in a clothing store where they both used to work and gradually fell in love. According to Vineet's brother Swamitt, Arpita died in a road accident on February 25. She had gone to the market with her brother, where a car hit their bike. Swamitt said “When Vineet learned about Arpita's death the next day, he was shocked. He went to her house to see Arpita for the last time. There he fainted while crying. Then we brought him back home”. Vineet was very disturbed after Arpita's death According to Vineet's sister in law Kajal “He was very disturbed since Arpita's death and stopped eating and drinking. He wasn't talking to anyone. He went there again in the evening. Found out that she had been buried. After this, he went to Arpita's grave where he started digging her grave”. She further added “When people stopped him, he ran away. Then he didn't return. He was searched extensively but couldn't be found. After this, we filed a missing person report for Vineet at the police station”. Police found Vineet's location in a garden After the filing of missing report police searched for Vineet for two days but couldn't find him. Police tried to trace his phone where his location was found in a garden 8 km away from the village. When family members and police reached there, they found his body hanging. Police found a love letter from his pocket Police lowered the body and searched the surroundings. Police also found a love letter from his pocket. After this, the body was sent for post-mortem. On Saturday evening, after the post-mortem, the body came home and family members performed the last rites and his body was buried right next to Arpita's grave.

stories.title: How a UP village shaped Khamenei’s legacy:Supreme Leader's mentor had roots in Barabanki, known as 'Musavi Hindi' in Iran
stories.summary: After reports of the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, a village in Uttar Pradesh’s Barabanki district has come into the spotlight due to its claimed historical connection with Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khomeini. Residents of Kintur village say that the ancestors of Ruhollah Khomeini, who led Iran’s 1979 Islamic Revolution, belonged to their village. Locals claim that several descendants of this village later went to Iran and played a role in religious and social developments there. According to villagers, people from Barabanki used to travel to Iran on religious pilgrimages during the time of the Nawabs. They also say that Syed Ahmad Musavi, the grandfather of Ruhollah Khomeini, lived in Kintur village during the 18th and early 19th centuries before moving abroad. Following the news of Khamenei’s death, Syed Nihal Miyan, who claims to be a descendant of Khomeini and lives in Kintur, expressed deep sorrow. He said Khamenei stood for humanity beyond religion and community, and his death was a great loss. Another local resident, Dr Rehan Kazmi, described Khamenei’s death in the Israeli attack as “martyrdom” and called it an irreparable loss. Khomeini’s grandfather had roots in Barabanki According to local accounts and historical references, Syed Ahmad Musavi, the grandfather of Ruhollah Khomeini, was born in Kintur village in the early 19th century. The village has long been known as a centre of Shia Islamic learning. In 1830, Syed Ahmad Musavi left British India on a religious journey to Najaf, a major Shia religious centre in present-day Iraq. He later settled in Najaf and eventually moved to the Iranian city of Khomein. To preserve his Indian identity, he added the word “Hindi” to his name and became known as Syed Ahmad Musavi Hindi. Iranian records still mention this name. He later bought a house in Iran and married Sakineh. The couple had four children, including a son whose descendants later included Ruhollah Khomeini, the architect of Iran’s Islamic Revolution. Today, residents of Kintur village say this historical link remains a matter of pride and has once again drawn attention after the reported death of Iran’s Supreme Leader. Religious influence and heritage linked to Musavi family The Musavi family, to which Iran’s former Supreme Leader Ruhollah Khomeini belonged, is believed to be descended from the seventh Shia Imam, Imam Musa al-Kazim. Because of this lineage, the family held a respected position in Shia religious circles and was known for its spiritual leadership. Syed Ahmad Musavi, Khomeini’s grandfather, played an important role in preserving this religious legacy. He later settled in the Middle East and died in Karbala in 1869. His teachings and ideology continued to influence his family and future generations, including Ruhollah Khomeini. Even today, villagers in Kintur claim that descendants of Khomeini’s family continue to live in the ancestral house in Barabanki, maintaining the historical and cultural connection between the village and Iran. The Iranian revolution of 1979 and Khomeini’s leadership In 1979, Ruhollah Khomeini led the Islamic Revolution in Iran, which ended the rule of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi and established Iran as an Islamic Republic. Following the revolution, Khomeini became the country’s Supreme Leader. Despite holding the highest position of power, Khomeini was known for his simple lifestyle. He lived in a modest single-storey house and reportedly avoided using public funds for personal comfort. His leadership and ideology played a major role in shaping modern Iran’s political and religious structure. Rise of Ali Khamenei after Khomeini’s death Ayatollah Ali Khamenei was born on July 17, 1939, in Mashhad, Iran. Inspired by Khomeini’s teachings, he actively participated in the Islamic Revolution and became one of Khomeini’s trusted associates. After Khomeini’s death in 1989, Khamenei was appointed as Iran’s Supreme Leader. He remained in this position for decades, becoming one of the most influential figures in Iran’s political and religious system. While Khamenei himself did not have direct links with India, his mentor Khomeini’s ancestral roots in Uttar Pradesh have continued to attract attention. Historical importance of Kintur village in Barabanki Kintur village in Uttar Pradesh’s Barabanki district holds historical significance due to its claimed connection with Syed Ahmad Musavi. From this village, Musavi travelled abroad and eventually settled in Iran, where his descendants went on to influence the country’s history. Several Shia families in the village still recall their ancestral links to Iran. Syed Nihal Kazmi, a 70-year-old resident, claims that his great-grandfather, Mufti Mohammad Quli Musavi, and Syed Ahmad Musavi were cousins. Locals say this connection remains an important part of the village’s identity, and recent developments in Iran have once again brought attention to Kintur’s historical and religious heritage.

stories.title: Lord Krishna plays Holi in Mathura's Gokul:Rides in a palaki from Nand Bhavan to Murlighat, chants of 'Jai Radhe Jai Krishna' echoes.
stories.summary: The atmosphere has turned festive in Braj with people immersed in celebration of Holi with their beloved Lord Krishna. Folk songs are being sung in every home and the temples are echoing with the chants of “Jai Radhe Jai Krishna”. On Sunday (March 1st), people gathered to celebrate Holi with Lord Krishna's form in Gokul. They have brought abir, colors and sticks with them and are accompanied by their family members and friends. Lord Krishna played ‘Chhari-mar Holi’ marking the beginning of the festivities The palaki ride emerged from Nand Bhavan, where Lord Krishna in his child form was seated in his palaki. From here the palaki reached to Murlidhar Ghat where it is believed that Lord played flute for the first time. At the ghat Lord Krishna played ‘Chhari-mar Holi’ (Holi with sticks) with the Gopis, marking the beginning of Holi celebrations in Gokul. ‘Chhari-mar Holi’ is celebrated in memory of Lord Krishna's childhood form and his divine plays. This festival is specially celebrated keeping the image of ‘Bal Gopal’ (child form of Lord Krishna) at the center. Therefore, small sticks called ‘Chhari’ are used instead of large sticks called ‘Lath’.

stories.title: ‘Only death will free me from SIR’:BLO found hanging in Fatehpur school; wrote he was denied leave for daughter’s wedding
stories.summary: A Shikshamitra, who was working as a Booth Level Officer (BLO) for SIR duty in Fatehpur, allegedly died by suicide inside the school where he was posted. The incident came to light on Saturday evening around 5 PM. According to information, the school peon saw the teacher hanging from a noose inside a classroom. He immediately raised an alarm and informed the family members as well as the police. Police reached the school soon after. The classroom door was open, and the teacher was found hanging inside. He was taken down and rushed to a nearby hospital, but doctors declared him dead. During the initial investigation, police found a suicide note kept on the teacher’s table. Further inquiry is underway.. It read: I am fed up with work. My daughter's wedding is on March 8th. I am not getting leave. That's why I am committing suicide. After dying, I will be free from SIR. After the teacher's death, villagers and family members created a ruckus at the hospital. Upon receiving this information, officials arrived and somehow pacified the family. After this, the body was sent for a post-mortem. The case is from the Bindki Kotwali area. ADM Avinash Tripathi stated: The suicide note that was found will be investigated. Further action will be taken after the post-mortem report is received. First, read the BLO's suicide note I, Akhilesh Kumar, am fed up with the BLO's work. For this work, I made rounds of officers, SDM and EO sir. My daughter is getting married. I said that someone else should be assigned the duty, but no officer or employee was willing to listen. The event is on March 8. Despite having so much work, I am continuously doing the BLO's work. My household chores remained incomplete. How much work can I, a single person, do? Distressed by this, I have been forced to take my own life. The Election Commission is responsible for me and my family. After my death, I will be freed from SIR. Taught children all day, found hanging in the evening In Aliabad village, Akhilesh Savita (50) lived with his wife Manju Devi, daughter Divyanshi (20), and son Divyansh. Akhilesh was a Shikshamitra (para-teacher) at the village's primary school. He was deployed for BLO work in SIR. His daughter Divyanshi's wedding was scheduled for March 8. He was asking for leave for this. It is alleged that he was not getting leave. On Saturday, he reached school at 9 AM. He taught the children. The children were dismissed at 3 PM. After this, he started doing SIR work. The other teachers went to their respective homes. The school peon arrived at 5 PM. He saw the teacher's body hanging. He called the family and the police. The family took him to Bindki CHC, where doctors declared him dead. Family members protested for 4 hours Villagers and family members started shouting slogans against the district administration. Upon receiving information about the incident, Bindki DSP Gaurav Sharma reached the CHC with the Kotwali police force. Officials pacified the family for 4 hours. After this, the family members finally agreed. Police sent the body for post-mortem. After the post-mortem, family members loaded the body into a car and took it to the village. Akhilesh's brother Bhupesh Kumar said- My brother was worried about leave for several weeks for his daughter's wedding. I myself went for leave, but he committed suicide because he didn't get it.

stories.title: UP on high alert as Shia protests erupt over Khamenei:People take to streets; gulf flights cancelled across region
stories.summary: After the death of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei in an attack by the United States and Israel, protests have begun in Uttar Pradesh. In Lucknow, thousands from the Shia community came out onto the streets. Women were seen crying and beating their chests. Protesters raised slogans of “Khamenei Zindabad” and “Down with America and Israel”. A woman shouted- Those who have treachery in their blood have killed Khamenei through deception. Khamenei was my lion. If one Khamenei is killed, thousands of Khameneis will rise... Israel and America are deceivers. The All India Shia Personal Law Board has announced three days of mourning. The board’s general secretary, Maulana Yasoob Abbas, said people will put up black flags at their homes and wear black clothes. Religious gatherings will be organised in Khamenei’s name. A large crowd gathered outside Jamia Millia Islamia in southeast Delhi, where people assembled to offer prayers at a nearby mosque following reports of the killing of Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in a joint U.S.–Israel strike. The gathering witnessed people expressing grief and solidarity, while groups of students and local community leaders also staged a protest, raising slogans and voicing support for the late Iranian leader.
