stories.title: 5 dogs maul 6-year-old boy in Jalandhar:Bitten all over the body while mother was away, child succumbs to injuries
stories.summary: A six-year-old boy from Bahraich, Uttar Pradesh, was brutally attacked and killed by a pack of five stray dogs in Jalandhar, Punjab. The child had accompanied his mother to the fields to deliver food to his father, who was working there. When the boy went into the field to relieve himself, the dogs surrounded him and launched the attack. The animals inflicted the most bites on his head, but his entire body was mauled. Hearing his cries, his parents rushed to his aid and managed to rescue him from the dogs’ clutches. The severely injured boy was immediately taken to Civil Hospital in Jalandhar for treatment, but he succumbed to his injuries. He lived with his parents in Gila Gakhla, Sultanpur Lodhi, and was their only child. Son had gone to deliver food to father with mother The boy’s father, Muneer, said he was sowing potatoes in the fields while the boy came with his mother to deliver food. After asking to go to the bathroom, the child went into the field, where he was attacked by a pack of five to six stray dogs. The dogs bit him all over, leaving him bloodied and unconscious. His uncle confirmed that the family tried to rescue the child after hearing his cries. They took him to Sultanpur Lodhi before referring him to Civil Hospital, Jalandhar, where he was declared dead. The boy was the only child of his parents, making the loss devastating for the family. Police response Following the tragic incident, local police arrived at the hospital to investigate. The incident highlights the dangers posed by stray dogs in rural areas and has left the family in shock.

stories.title: SC hearing sees humour and sharp courtroom exchange:CJI makes festive remark; later reprimands lawyer over petition
stories.summary: An interesting incident occurred during a case hearing in the Supreme Court on Friday. While setting the next date for the case, Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant made a light-hearted comment about Allahabad (now Prayagraj) in open court, which became a topic of discussion. The case was listed for a hearing before the Supreme Court. The Chief Justice's bench was deciding the next hearing date and discussing the cause list. During this, the CJI said that this matter should be listed after the Holi holidays. It should be kept after next week. During this, he also said, It's Allahabad brother... it will take a week for the bhang intoxication to wear off. His comment has become a topic of discussion in Prayagraj. Actually, during Holi, some people traditionally consume bhang in Prayagraj and many surrounding districts. The hearing was ongoing in the Supreme Court in the case of Suresh Devi vs High Court of Judicature at Allahabad. Humorous tone, not part of the order This conversation in court was completely informal. It was not part of any judicial order, nor did it have any connection with the legal issues of the case. Such light comments are sometimes made during regular proceedings. Their purpose is to keep the atmosphere light. This comment has no impact on the merits of the case or the hearing. Case still pending in SC The Suresh Devi vs High Court of Judicature at Allahabad case is still pending in the Supreme Court. Its next hearing will be held on a date fixed by the Supreme Court after the Holi holidays. Prayagraj's Holi is famous across the country The festival of Holi is celebrated with great enthusiasm in Prayagraj, and its Holi is discussed throughout the country. Especially the historic Loknath Chowk's Holi often makes headlines. In Prayagraj, Holi is played for three days. On the third day, in some areas, people play "Kapda Faad" (cloth-tearing) Holi. Another incident occurred... When CJI severely reprimanded the lawyer In another case, CJI Suryakant severely reprimanded a lawyer. In the case of Puran Chandra Sen vs State of Rajasthan, CJI Suryakant asked the lawyer, "Didn't the High Court impose a fine on them? You're not wearing a band; it looks like someone has come to wrestle." To this, Justice Bagchi said that the High Court has imposed a fine. Then the CJI asked how many years have you been practicing law, to which the lawyer replied that he had been practicing since 1995. CJI Suryakant got angry just hearing this and asked who made the mistake of giving you a license. Please don't file such petitions. People trust you. If you file all this, how will people trust you? To this, the lawyer said that RSS is against the ideal constitution, to which Justice Bagchi replied that if you put more pressure, we will have to increase the cost. Your ideology or politics, etc., may have different opinions, but this does not constitute an offense, nor can you ask to file an FIR against any authority. Please step back, don't embarrass yourself. Now read the courtroom live... CJI Suryakant: Didn't the High Court impose costs on them? Not wearing proper attire.. looks like someone has come to wrestle. Justice Bagchi: HC has imposed costs. CJI: How many years have you been practicing law? Advocate: Since 1995... CJI: Who made the mistake of giving you a license? Please don't file such petitions. People trust you. If you file such things, how will people trust you? Advocate: RSS ideals are against the Constitution. Justice Bagchi: If you put more pressure.. We'll have to increase the costs. Your ideology or politics may differ, but this doesn't constitute an offense or allow you to demand an FIR against any authority. For argument's sake, if Parliament passes an illegal law, is that a crime? Please withdraw, don't embarrass yourself. CJI: The petitioner, who is a practicing lawyer and present in person, states that after realizing his mistake, he does not wish to pursue the petition filed under BNSS. He also promises that he will not file any such complaint, application/petition in any court. CJI: The petitioner further requests that this court take a lenient view and exempt him from the costs imposed by HC and further proceedings against the petitioner. Considering the petitioner's remorse and his undertaking, we direct that para 16 of the impugned HC judgment shall remain stayed indefinitely. This appeal was against the Rajasthan High Court order, which had imposed a fine of ₹50,000 on a lawyer. The lawyer had demanded registration of an FIR against the Prime Minister, Home Minister, and others regarding the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019. The High Court had dismissed the petition, called it a misuse of procedure under Section 528 BNSS, and said that courts cannot be used to pursue cases filed with "wrong intentions".

stories.title: ₹1,000-crore UP fraudster arrested in Dubai:ED to bring Shine City promoter Rashid Naseem to Lucknow; 554 FIRs filed in UP
stories.summary: The promoter of Shine City Group and main accused in the alleged thousand-crore fraud, Rashid Naseem, has been arrested by Dubai Police. The action, taken at the request of the Enforcement Directorate and Economic Offences Wing, is being seen as a major breakthrough against the long-absconding accused. Naseem, who fled the country in 2019, faces allegations of cheating worth ₹800–1000 crore and hundreds of cases. The process to bring him back to India has now sped up. According to sources, Naseem was caught in the United Arab Emirates through coordination between Indian agencies. Proceedings against him were underway under money-laundering and organised economic crime charges. His location had been tracked for a long time and extradition efforts were ongoing, after which Dubai Police detained him. Action in Dubai on request of ED and EOW Through Shine City Group, Naseem allegedly collected huge sums from people by luring them with real-estate and high-return investment schemes. It is alleged that after payments stopped, he fled to Dubai in 2019. Police records show that around 554 FIRs have been registered against Naseem and his companies. He is accused of cheating people of ₹800–1000 crore in the name of investments. Investors were promised attractive returns, plots and houses, but later neither money was returned nor possession of land given. After cases kept mounting and police pressure increased, Naseem fled the country. Lookout notices and other legal procedures were then initiated against him. Property worth ₹1,000 crore already seized Government agencies have seized assets worth hundreds of crores belonging to Naseem and linked firms. In an audio released in 2021, Naseem himself claimed the government had already taken possession of property worth about ₹500 crore, now valued at nearly ₹1,000 crore. In the same audio he also claimed about ₹300 crore was stuck between farmers and brokers. He said legal complications arose due to some brokers absconding and registry disputes. Investigating agencies, however, are independently verifying these claims. Brother arrested earlier A reward of ₹5 lakh each was announced on Naseem and his brother Asif, earlier ₹50,000 each. Rewards of ₹1 lakh each were also declared on five other accused linked to the company. Asif has already been arrested from Prayagraj. On court directions, both EOW and ED are pursuing the probe. After Naseem’s arrest, investigators expect disclosures about a wider financial network. Syndicate operated from Dubai Agencies say Naseem ran the entire racket from Dubai, investing heavily there while continuing operations in India through associates. After arrest and bail in Nepal in 2018, he shifted to Dubai. Because he avoided arrest for years, his international contacts are being examined. Investigators are also tracing channels used to send fraud money abroad. Syndicate operated from Dubai Probe agencies claim Naseem ran the entire network while sitting in Dubai. He allegedly made major investments there and continued operations in India through associates. After being arrested and granted bail in Nepal in 2018, he moved to Dubai. Because he evaded arrest for years, his international links are also under scrutiny. Agencies are examining through which channels the fraud money was sent abroad. Declared absconder in April 2025 A special PMLA court in Lucknow declared Naseem an absconder in April 2025. After that, attachment and seizure of properties intensified. Illegal assets in several districts including Prayagraj and Lucknow have already been taken over by authorities. The main accused in the Shine City scam, Rashid Naseem, has been arrested by Dubai Police. An ED team will now bring him to Lucknow. About ten months ago, a special court in Lucknow had declared him absconding. Police have registered around 554 FIRs against Naseem and his companies. He is accused of cheating people of ₹800–1000 crore in the name of investments. He allegedly collected money promising lucrative returns and then fled India in 2019. Dubai Police acted on the request of ED and EOW. Indian agencies coordinated in the UAE to catch him. His location had been traced for a long time. Where cases are registered The alleged mastermind of the Shine City scam, Rashid Naseem, is a resident of GTB Nagar, Kareli in Prayagraj. Most cases against him are registered in Lucknow, where the company’s headquarters was located — including Gomtinagar, Vikasnagar, BKT, Mohanlalganj and Gosainganj. Apart from this, several cases are registered in Prayagraj because the promoters’ original residence was there. Cases have also been filed in different police stations of Varanasi, where action under the Gangster Act was also initiated. How was the scam carried out? Shine City Group is accused of running Ponzi and pyramid schemes to collect money from investors in the name of real-estate investments, plots, houses, flats and other attractive plans. Investors were promised high returns, but it was allegedly a Ponzi scheme in which money from new investors was used to pay old ones. Investors neither received promised plots or properties nor returns. In many cases, plot documents were found fake. Money-laundering charge The company allegedly transferred investors’ funds into accounts of various shell companies, directors and associates. These funds were used to purchase land, office space and real-estate projects, later suspected to be part of money laundering. Investigation found more than 34 shell firms were created to mislead investors. A probe by RERA found that while only 58 plots were registered in Lucknow, bookings for 3,000 were shown. What action has been taken so far? Initial investigation of the Shine City scam was conducted by local police. But when cases kept increasing, all were transferred to EOW. Later, based on cases registered in Uttar Pradesh, the ED also began its probe. So far 62 people have been arrested in the case, including Asif Naseem (Rashid’s brother and MD) in November 2021; Himanshu Kumar in July 2024; Manish Jaiswal (Vice-President) in September 2024; and Gyan Prakash Upadhyay, Mohammad Akram, Shashi Bala, Abhishek Singh, Durga Prasad, Uddhav Singh, Amitabh Srivastava and Meera Srivastava. ED’s action so far The ED began its money-laundering investigation in January 2021 based on 554 FIRs. Assets worth ₹266.70 crore have been seized so far, including 24 agricultural lands worth ₹47.80 crore in Mohanlalganj (Lucknow), six residential plots worth ₹16.5 crore in Barabanki, commercial properties worth ₹9.27 crore in Rewari (Haryana), and assets worth ₹20 crore in Patna (Bihar). Where Shine City projects are located Shine City projects were launched in several cities including Mohanlalganj in Lucknow (Shine Valley Sector-1, Jawahir City Project), Kanpur, Prayagraj, Barabanki, Varanasi and Kaushambi.

stories.title: ₹1,600 crore withdrawn from 12 banks in 2.5 years:Agencies suspect laundering and possible anti-national links
stories.summary: In connection with the ₹8 lakh robbery in Kanpur’s Shyam Nagar, the Police Commissioner made a major disclosure on Friday. It emerged that nearly ₹1,600 crore in cash had been withdrawn over two-and-a-half years from 68 accounts across 12 banks in the city. On the day of the incident, tannery businessman Mahfooz withdrew ₹3.20 crore from IDBI Bank’s Phoolbagh branch, after which his cash carriers divided the money in a small room in Jharkati. The remaining ₹24 lakh was handed to Wasid and his associate Arshad, who were on their way to deliver it to Mahfooz’s house. Police suspect that such huge cash withdrawals could be linked to money laundering, anti-national activities, or tax evasion, and letters are being sent to central agencies for investigation. The Police Commissioner said six accused in the robbery — Abdul Rahman, Shubhan Khan, Lareb Siddiqui and Mohammad Zeeshan among them — were arrested and jailed, while two suspects, Yaseen and Mujahid, were caught after a late-night police encounter on Thursday in which both were shot in the leg in retaliatory action. Robbery took place in Shyam Nagar on February 16 The Police Commissioner said Wasid and Arshad worked as cash carriers. On 16 February, four bike-borne assailants robbed them in Shyam Nagar. During the attack, the criminals beat them with pistol butts and left them seriously injured. After the incident, the injured men first claimed ₹25 lakh, then ₹12 lakh, then ₹8 lakh had been looted, and later denied any robbery had taken place. 3.20 crore rupees withdrawn on the day of incident When police began investigating, injured Wasid initially said they had withdrawn ₹8 lakh from the Phoolbagh branch of IDBI Bank. But bank verification showed ₹3.20 crore had actually been withdrawn that day from the account of Mahfooz, a tannery trader from Jajmau. Further inquiry revealed that between 2023 and 2025, about ₹850 crore had been withdrawn from nearly 14 accounts in the same bank, all linked to Shivang Tannery in Jajmau. Checks of PAN numbers and email IDs revealed Mahfooz and his associates held 68 accounts in 12 banks, from which around ₹1,600 crore cash was withdrawn in about two-and-a-half years. Investigators are probing where this money went, whether it was used for anti-national activities or tax evasion. Letters are being sent to GST, Income Tax, ED and other agencies to examine all angles. Got APMC certificate made to get GST exemption The Police Commissioner said investigation also found that funds in these accounts came from 12 enterprises in Kanpur, Unnao and Fatehpur. He added Mahfooz had obtained an APMC certificate claiming his firm operated in agriculture to secure GST exemption. The probe also revealed serious negligence by banks: under rules, withdrawals above ₹10 lakh require generation of an STR report, but preliminary findings show banks failed to generate such reports. Rahman and Shubhan did the reconnaissance Police said the robbery had been planned for about a month. Rahman played the main role. His friend Arun Soni used to carry cash for Mahfooz, from whom Rahman gathered information. Rahman and Shubhan then surveyed the bank. On the day of the incident, Mahfooz withdrew cash and handed it to carriers. After division in Jharkati, Wasid and Arshad left with ₹24 lakh for Mahfooz’s house, and the attackers began following them. After they reached Shyam Nagar, the robbers assaulted them with pistol butts. Police said Rahman and Shubhan did not trust even the robbers and stood about 100 metres away tracking them. After the robbery, the biggest share went to Rahman and Shubhan. Following the crime, the gang travelled to Jama Masjid, Kashmir and Nepal. Police recovered ₹11 lakh from them. Mahfooz asked the court - Am I not wanted As Mahfooz’s syndicate began to unravel after the incident, he went absconding. The Police Commissioner said Mahfooz has not cooperated so far and was pressuring victims not to file reports. Since the incident, he has withdrawn another ₹1 crore. His location is being traced. He also filed a petition in court asking whether he was wanted in any case. Money deposited in accounts from these firms -Azam Enterprises - 118 Crore -Alfisha Enterprises - 133 Crore -Aarti Enterprises - 99.60 Crore -Faiz Enterprises - 104 Crore -Kasif Enterprises - 68.25 Crore -Shama Enterprises - 124 Crore -Sammoh Enterprises - 117 Crore -Raja Enterprises - 64 Crore -Saira Enterprises - 14 Crore -Shabnam Enterprises - 151 Crore Accounts found in these banks The Police Commissioner said accounts linked to Mahfooz and his associates were found in HDFC Bank, RBL Bank, IndusInd Bank, Bank of Baroda, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Union Bank of India, Axis Bank, Bandhan Bank, Bank of India and ICICI Bank, among others.

stories.title: Watched YouTube to dispose of father's body:Brought a blue drum to fit it in the car; troubled relationship angle surfaces
stories.summary: A startling disclosure has come to light in the murder of a prominent pathology owner in Lucknow. Police sources state that after killing Vardhman Pathology proprietor Manvendra Singh, his son Akshat Pratap Singh, also known as Raja, allegedly watched multiple online videos to understand how to dispose of the body. He is said to have ordered tools online and then attempted to conceal the remains. To transport them, he purchased a blue drum sized to fit inside his car, along with heavy plastic sheets and 20 litres of turpentine oil. When he realised he might fail, he phoned a lawyer connected to the family and sought a meeting. At the same time, Akshat allegedly tried to mislead both police and relatives by acting as though he was searching for his father. To appear worried, he made 135 calls to various people so it would seem he was anxious about his father’s disappearance. Police say these facts emerged during questioning. He was sent to jail on 25 February after the case was revealed. However, relatives and neighbours say they do not believe the police version. Social media posts from people close to the family also point to long-standing tensions within their relationships. Bought a car-sized drum to dispose of the torso According to police sources, after the killing around 4:30 a.m. on 20 February, Akshat spent two days trying to dispose of the body. After managing some parts, he searched markets for a drum. He told investigators he went to three different shops in his car before finding a drum that could fit inside it. He brought it home and waited for the surroundings to become deserted so he could take it out unnoticed. Police are collecting CCTV footage and billing records of the purchased items. Watched on YouTube, also ordered supplies online Police sources said he watched online videos after the murder to figure out how to dispose of the body, as he could not lift it alone because of its weight. He allegedly ordered tools online for this purpose. Made 135 calls to mislead Investigators said that after the murder, he also attempted to avoid suspicion by going with an acquaintance to Ashiyana police station to file a missing report for his father. During that time, he called numerous people so it would not appear that he was involved. Call detail records are being analysed to find out whom he contacted and whether he sought help from anyone. Lawyer uncle, need to meet you alone... According to police sources, after committing the murder, Akshat realized that he could be caught. He then tried to meet a lawyer connected to the family. He called them and insisted on meeting alone. However, due to being busy in court, the lawyer could not meet him. Meanwhile, Akshat had also admitted to killing his father in front of some close people. Friend posts on Facebook - 'Children's minds were poisoned' A neighbour and family acquaintance, Anshuman Dubey, wrote a lengthy social media post pointing towards strained ties. He stated that Akshat was 11 years old when his mother died by suicide, after which her relatives blamed Manvendra and relations never improved. He said distance developed between the father and children, and relatives influenced the children against him. He also mentioned that the father’s friendship with a woman was widely discussed, which damaged his image in the children’s eyes. The post further indicated that the son was close to a girl and may have spent large sums of household money on her, causing disputes over finances and relationships between father and son. Did not eat food in jail, stayed awake all night After being sent to judicial custody on 25 February, Akshat reportedly stayed awake the entire night and did not eat food, appearing uneasy, according to jail sources. stories.title: Mother-in-law slaps bride thrice, video surfaces online:Woman insists on staying with lover, confession made on wedding night
stories.summary: An uproar broke out in Hamirpur when the bride refused to live with her husband just hours after marriage. On 21 February, she had come to her in-laws’ house for the first time after the wedding. She refused to let her husband touch her. She clearly stated that she would live only with her lover. Due to her insistence, a meeting of both families was called at the groom’s house. Everyone tried to persuade her. While explaining, the mother-in-law lost her temper and slapped her several times in front of everyone. A video of the incident has also surfaced, showing her slapping the bride three times in a second. After this, the bride is heard crying and saying, “Hit me more, beat me, kill me.” When the matter was not resolved in the council, both sides reached the police station. There too, attempts were made to convince her, but the bride did not agree. On 23 February, with the consent of both sides, the bride and groom decided to live separately. The bride’s mother-in-law lost her temper while trying to reason with her and delivered three rapid slaps. To defend herself, the daughter-in-law confronted her mother-in-law and a scuffle began. Now know the full matter Laldeewan, a resident of Rambagh in Hamir town, had married his son Dharm Kushwaha (26) to Mithlesh, daughter of Budh Singh from Bilrakh village under Rath police station limits. The wedding took place on 21 February at a guest house according to Hindu rituals. On 22 February, Mithlesh arrived at her in-laws’ house after her farewell. At night, family members tried to take her to groom Dharm’s room. However, she refused to enter. When the family insisted, she went inside but refused to let her husband touch her. Dharm informed his family about this. When relatives questioned Mithlesh, she said she loved another man and wanted to spend her life with him. She said she would live only with her lover Kallu, a resident of Gohand, and not with her husband. She alleged that the marriage with Dharm had been forced upon her. When Mithlesh reached the police station, her mother and aunt tried to persuade her, but she did not agree. After this, the in-laws called Mithlesh’s family. Persuasion continued throughout the night of 22 February. During this, her mother-in-law lost her temper while explaining and slapped Mithlesh three times in a second. Mithlesh cried and said, “Hit me more, beat me to death. But I will live only with my lover.” Family members tried hard to convince her, but nothing worked. The next morning, 23 February, both sides reached the police station. Talks continued between them. Later, the bride and groom agreed to live separately. Both families then decided to complete legal formalities for separation. Station in-charge Rakesh said neither side submitted a written complaint. Both decided by mutual consent to live separately. For now, the matter has ended with a mutual settlement. Read what is shown in the video A 72-second video of the bride has surfaced. In it, she is seen sitting with other women. One woman, while explaining, slaps her twice. Others then tell the woman not to hit her. The bride gets agitated and repeatedly asks them to hit her. Meanwhile, other women tell her that if she did not want to stay there, she should not have married. The bride replies that she was forced into the marriage and had no choice. After the uproar at her in-laws’ house, the bride is currently staying at her parents’ home.

stories.title: Woman climbs 250-foot mobile tower demanding marriage with lover:Threatens to consume poison if he doesn’t return
stories.summary: A young woman climbed a 250-foot-high mobile tower in Uttar Pradesh’s Maharajganj district on Friday morning, demanding that her lover marry her. She claimed they had been in a relationship for 12 years and accused him of running away from marriage. She also threatened to consume poison in his name if he did not return. The incident took place in Domakati village under Nichlaul police station limits and lasted nearly five hours before police managed to persuade her to come down. Girl throws emotional note from tower While sitting atop the tower, the woman threw down a handwritten note containing the mobile numbers of her lover Farooq and his family members. In the note, she wrote that she loved him deeply and questioned why he was avoiding marriage after being in a relationship for so long. She warned that if he did not return, she would consume poison in his name. She also appealed to him to come back and said she did not feel like living anymore. Police used the phone numbers provided in the note to contact Farooq and his family. Lover summoned from Nepal According to police and family members, Farooq, 22, had gone to Nepal after an argument with the woman, identified as Zora, 18. Nepal is located about 6 kilometres from their village. Zora’s father, Ramzan, a farmer from Piparpati Badhya village, said the couple had been in a relationship for years and their marriage was fixed about a year ago after both families agreed. However, Farooq had recently gone to Bengaluru for work. When he returned three days ago, he refused to marry, which led to a dispute between the two. After the argument, he left for Nepal. Troubled by this, Zora left her house around 5 am on Friday without informing anyone and climbed the mobile tower located about 2 kilometres away. Police and villagers try to convince her Villagers spotted her on the tower and informed police. Officers reached the spot and tried to convince her to come down, but she refused and insisted that Farooq be called to the spot. Police contacted Farooq and asked him to return immediately. He arrived at around 9:30 am and tried to persuade her to come down. However, she refused, saying she feared he might run away again. Police then assured her that they would help resolve the matter and told her she would not be abandoned. After hours of persuasion and assurances, she finally agreed to climb down. Police take both into custody As soon as she came down, police took both Zora and Farooq into custody and brought them to the police station for further inquiry. Nichlaul Station Officer Akhilesh Verma said the woman was safely brought down after counselling and persuasion. “Both have been brought to the police station. Their age and documents are being verified. Further action will be taken based on the family’s complaint,” he said. Police said they are currently examining the legal aspects, including age verification and consent, before deciding on further steps. The situation in the village has now returned to normal

stories.title: 11,000-watt electric shock hits man in UP:Lineman perched on a 25-foot pole to replace transformer, charred to death in fire |VIDEO
stories.summary: A lineman died after suffering an electric shock and catching fire while replacing a transformer in Sonbhadra district of Uttar Pradesh. The incident occurred on a 25-foot-high electricity pole in Lohota village under the Ghorawal police station area. According to eyewitnesses, the lineman had climbed the pole to install a new transformer. During the work, he reportedly received a powerful shock of 11,000 volts. The electric shock caused a short circuit, and flames broke out immediately. Within seconds, the lineman’s body caught fire. His helper present at the spot tried to rescue him, but the lineman had already suffered severe burns. Villagers alleged that the lineman had taken an official shutdown of the power supply before starting the work. However, the electricity supply was allegedly restored while he was still working on the pole, leading to the accident. A video of the incident has also surfaced, showing the lineman engulfed in flames on the pole. Authorities have been informed, and further investigation is underway to determine how the power supply was restored during maintenance work. Heart-wrenching images- Lineman dies after high-voltage shock in Sonbhadra: complete sequence of events Santosh Kumar (40), a resident of Bisahar village, was working as a contract lineman with the electricity department. He lived with his wife Bindu (35) and two sons, Adarsh (15) and Shivam (18). On Thursday evening, Santosh went to Lohota village to install a new transformer. He reached the spot at around 7 pm and began preparations for the work. Shutdown taken before starting work According to his colleagues, Santosh had followed safety procedures. Before climbing the pole, he informed the power house and requested a shutdown to ensure there was no electricity supply during the installation. After receiving confirmation, he climbed the 25-foot-high pole and started mounting the transformer. Power supply suddenly restored While Santosh was working on the pole, the 11,000-volt high-tension supply was suddenly restored without any notice, colleagues alleged. He received a powerful electric shock and got stuck to the pole. A short circuit occurred immediately, and flames broke out. Within moments, Santosh was engulfed in fire while still on the pole. Helper called department, but rescue came too late As soon as the incident happened, helper Matrulal called the electricity department and requested an urgent shutdown. After the supply was cut, he climbed the pole to put out the fire. However, Santosh had already suffered severe burns. With the help of local villagers, he was brought down from the pole and rushed to the district hospital. Doctors referred him to the Trauma Centre in Varanasi due to his critical condition, but Santosh died on the way. The incident has triggered anger among villagers and colleagues, who alleged negligence in restoring the power supply during maintenance work. Authorities have started an investigation into the matter. In this case, the helper who was present with Santosh accused the electricity department of negligence. He said the lineman was working on the line at the time. The department was aware of this, so he questioned on whose orders and why the power supply was restored. Negligence claimed to have cost a life Sonbhadra’s Executive Engineer (XEN) M.B. Thakur said two linemen were working at different locations. Santosh and Matru were together at one site, while Rajesh Sahu was working at another. According to Thakur, after completing his task, Rajesh Sahu restored the power supply. The line became live, leading to the accident. He said the matter is under investigation and further action will be taken based on the findings.

stories.title: Three-day Holi holiday in Uttar Pradesh:4 consecutive days off including Sunday, salaries to be paid before festival
stories.summary: Good news for 1.7 million employees in Uttar Pradesh: the Yogi government has declared a three-day holiday for Holi. Orders were issued on Friday, confirming that March 2, 3, and 4 will be official holidays. Since March 1 is a Sunday, this creates a continuous four-day holiday from Sunday to Wednesday. February 28, i.e., Saturday, has been designated as a working day. All government departments will remain open, and regular work will continue on this day. Salaries must be paid before Holi Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath has directed that all employees, including outsourced, contractual, and sanitation workers, must receive their salaries or honorariums before Holi. He has warned officials that no negligence will be tolerated in this matter. The CM issued these instructions after returning late Thursday night from a foreign tour to Singapore and Japan. Major pay raise for Shiksha Mitras and Instructors Prior to this, the government had announced a significant pay increase for 1.7 lakh Shiksha Mitras and instructors. Shiksha Mitras will now receive ₹18,000 per month, while instructors will get ₹17,000 per month. Previously, Shiksha Mitras received only ₹10,000 and instructors ₹9,000. CM highlights government’s initiatives CM Yogi Adityanath stated in the assembly that the step was taken in the interest of para-teachers and instructors. During the SP government, they received only ₹3,000. His government had increased it to ₹10,000 in 2017, and now, considering inflation, an additional ₹8,000 has been added at once. He also announced 75,000 jobs in the health department, underlining the government’s focus on employee welfare.

stories.title: Allahabad HC stays Shankaracharya’s arrest in sexual abuse case:Order on anticipatory bail reserved; state lawyer says he could influence case
stories.summary: The Allahabad High Court has stayed the arrest of Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati. Justice Jitendra Kumar Sinha has reserved the order on his anticipatory bail plea, with the next hearing scheduled for the third week of March. The Shankaracharya had filed the anticipatory bail plea on February 24 in connection with a case alleging sexual exploitation of Batuks (young disciples). In court, the state government’s lawyer opposed the bail, while the Shankaracharya’s counsel argued that the case involves a religious leader, not a criminal, and claimed the entire matter is a conspiracy. The government lawyer argued that Shankaracharya is very powerful and could influence the case if granted bail. After the stay on arrest, a celebratory atmosphere was reported at his monastery. Petition filed by Ramabhadracharya’s disciple The case was initiated after Ashutosh Brahmachari, a disciple of Swami Ramabhadracharya, filed a petition under Section 173(4) in the district court. Following the order of Special Judge (Rape POCSO Court) Vinod Kumar Chaurasia, police at Jhunsi Police Station registered an FIR against Swami Avimukteshwaranand over allegations of sexual abuse of Batuks. Lawyer who received bomb threat, accused arrested Meanwhile, police have arrested the accused who threatened to blow up Shankaracharya’s lawyer, Srinath Tripathi, with a bomb. The accused, Ajit Kumar Saroj, was arrested from Rasipur village in the Jansa police station area within about 20 hours. Police said the accused is a law student and also practices in the Varanasi court. During questioning, he admitted that he sent the threatening message to falsely implicate his neighbour. Tripathi received the threat late Wednesday night. The message sent to his mobile phone said, “We will blow up the Varanasi court with a bomb, and you too.” Visitor meets Shankaracharya, calls allegations baseless On Thursday afternoon, a Muslim man met Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand in Varanasi and said the allegations against him were baseless and should not have been made. How the case unfolded The controversy began during the Magh Mela in Prayagraj on January 18, during Mauni Amavasya, when a dispute took place between the Shankaracharya and the administration. On January 24, eight days later, Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj submitted a complaint to the Police Commissioner. The complaint alleged sexual exploitation of children during Magh Mela-2026 and Mahakumbh-2025. Alleging police inaction, a petition was filed in the Special POCSO Court on February 8. Two children were produced in court on February 13, and their statements were recorded on February 21. On the same day, the court ordered Jhunsi police to register an FIR. The FIR names Shankaracharya, his disciple Mukundanand, and two to three unidentified persons as accused. Shankaracharya alleges conspiracy, seeks legal relief On February 24, Shankaracharya accused Prayagraj Additional Commissioner Ajay Pal Sharma of conspiring against him. He then filed an anticipatory bail petition in the Allahabad High Court. On February 26, the medical report related to the case became public. According to police sources, the report indicates sexual abuse of children. Meanwhile, one of the alleged victims appeared before the media for the first time and claimed he was exploited when he had gone for studies. Responding to the medical report in Varanasi, Shankaracharya questioned the investigation and criticised Ashutosh Maharaj. He alleged that false stories were being spread to create pressure and said he was not afraid of the allegations. Further hearings in the Allahabad High Court and the ongoing police investigation are expected to determine the next course of action in the case.

stories.title: Mayawati to field 100 candidates in next month:Bets on Brahmin-Muslim equation; leads early ticket race
stories.summary: As the much-awaited 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections draw closer, political parties have begun sharpening their strategies. In this race, Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) chief Mayawati has stepped up preparations, planning to announce more than 100 candidates within the next month as part of an aggressive early election strategy. So far, BSP has announced four candidates from different regions of Uttar Pradesh — Purvanchal, Bundelkhand, and Western UP. Among them are two Muslim and two Brahmin leaders. This shows that BSP is focusing on a Brahmin-Muslim political combination for the 2027 elections. BSP's strategy is to declare candidates/assembly in-charges for more than 100 seats by March 2026. How effective will BSP's strategy be? How much impact will the Brahmin-Muslim equation have? Read this report… Focus on Brahmin-Muslim-Dalit vote bank In the 2022 Assembly elections, BSP won only one seat but finished second in 18 seats. This time, the party wants to strengthen its position by announcing candidates early and building strong local support. Mayawati has openly appealed to Brahmins and Muslims to support BSP. She says that if Muslims (about 19% of the population) and Dalits (around 20%) vote together, their combined support could reach nearly 39%. If Brahmins (9–11%) also join, the vote share could reach close to 50%, which can help win many seats. Muslims have traditionally supported the Samajwadi Party (SP), while Brahmins are often considered core voters of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). BSP is now trying to attract voters from both parties. Four announced candidates The four candidates announced so far come from different political backgrounds. Some were previously with the Samajwadi Party or the BJP. BSP believes local caste equations — especially Dalit-Muslim and Brahmin-Dalit combinations — can help them win in these constituencies. Target: 100+ candidates by March 2026 According to party sources, BSP aims to finalise candidates in most constituencies by mid-2026. By March, over 100 seats may have declared candidates or assembly in-charges. Several constituencies where BSP finished second in 2022 are also likely to see early candidate announcements. Muslim leaders joining BSP BSP has recently welcomed several Muslim leaders who left SP. The party claims more prominent Muslim faces may join soon. Responsibilities given to senior leaders Mayawati has assigned specific caste outreach responsibilities to senior leaders: Party leaders will soon begin district-level tours and meetings with workers to strengthen the organisation. Overall strategy BSP’s strategy for 2027 is clear: With this plan, Mayawati hopes to revive BSP’s political strength in Uttar Pradesh and challenge both SP and BJP in the next assembly election.

stories.title: Rinku Singh performs his father's last rites:Elder brother Sonu lights the pyre, Virat Kohli offered condolences
stories.summary: India cricketer Rinku Singh suffered a personal loss after his father, Khanchand Singh, passed away on Friday following a long battle with liver cancer at the age of 60. His father had been fighting the disease for some time, and his condition worsened in recent days, leading to his hospitalisation in Greater Noida. He breathed his last this morning at around 4:36 AM. Rinku Singh arrived in Aligarh, leaving the Indian team midway through their T20 World Cup campaign. The Indian cricketer was seen carrying his father's mortal remains on his shoulder before the funeral. 3 pictures from the funeral Rinku's elder brother Sonu lit up the pyre of the his father, according to Hindu traditions. Khanchand Singh was admitted to Yatharth Hospital in Sector Omega One, Greater Noida, after his health suddenly deteriorated. He was diagnosed with stage-four liver cancer and was being treated in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU). Despite the doctors’ efforts, he could not recover. The tragic news comes at a time when Rinku Singh is part of India’s squad during the ICC Men’s T20 World Cup 2026. The cricketer had briefly left the team’s training camp to be with his father during his critical condition before rejoining the squad. Rinku's father was on a ventilator support for a few days. Rinku’s fiancé and Machhlishahr MP Priya Saroj’s father, Tufani Saroj, spoke to Bhaskar over the phone. He said, "Priya has been with Rinku’s family for several days. We had also gone there at night. While returning, we received the news of his father’s death." What Rinku Singh's father told Bhaskar in his last interview In his last interaction with Bhaskar on the India vs Pakistan match, Rinku's father said he was very happy with his son's performance. "It was a good game. I wasn't feeling well, but now I'm good. I watched the entire match, Rinku is a star now. If he had played more balls, he would scored even more. Father played a key role in Rinku’s journey Rinku Singh has often spoken about the struggles his family faced during his childhood. His father, Khanchand Singh, worked as a gas cylinder delivery man to support the family. In an earlier interview, Rinku shared that he and his four brothers also helped their father by delivering cylinders to homes and hotels on motorcycles. Despite financial hardships, the family always supported Rinku’s cricketing dreams. He and his brothers would even collect money together to buy a cricket ball and play matches in their neighbourhood. Their sacrifices and support played a big role in helping Rinku rise from a humble background to represent India at the highest level. Rinku left team camp to be with his father As soon as Rinku Singh received news about his father’s serious condition, he rushed to the hospital on Tuesday morning, around 10 am. At that time, he was in Chennai with Team India during the T20 World Cup preparations and had to leave the practice session immediately to be with his family. After spending time with his father and family, Rinku returned to Chennai on February 25 and rejoined the Indian team. stories.title: What does Shankaracharya’s ‘Sheesh Mahal’ look like?:3-storey building; mirrors on all sides, Mukundanand says there is no swimming pool
stories.summary: Srividya Math in Varanasi has come under national attention after serious allegations were made against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand. Jagadguru Rambhadracharya’s disciple, Ashutosh Brahmachari Maharaj, alleged that the monastery was built like a “Glass Palace” with luxury facilities, including a swimming pool. Following these claims, a case was registered against the Shankaracharya under sexual harassment and POCSO provisions. The allegations led to widespread debate among followers and raised questions about the monastery’s structure and facilities. To verify the claims, a Dainik Bhaskar team visited the Srividya Math and spoke to residents and disciples. Entry restrictions, security and interior layout Security guards were posted outside the monastery. Visitors were allowed entry only after registering their name, address and mobile number. Inside, the main hall had tiled and stone flooring, with carpets placed across the room. The walls were painted in yellow and ochre shades. Several rooms were visible through glass panels installed in doors and partitions. Some followers were seen meditating inside. According to residents, the Shankaracharya was in meditation in a separate private room, where entry is restricted. Disciple Mukundanand said the monastery has multiple floors. The ground floor is used for discourses and meditation. The first floor houses children who study there. The upper floor is reserved for the Shankaracharya. The roof has bathing facilities for children. ‘Mirror palace’ claim and explanation by disciple Mukundanand acknowledged that mirrors were installed across several halls and walls. He said the monastery has many mirrors, which is why people refer to it as a “Mirror Palace”. He denied allegations of a swimming pool inside the building. He said the Ganga flows next to the monastery, and during high water levels, the river reaches the premises. He added that anyone could visit and verify the absence of a swimming pool. A silver throne was also shown inside the monastery, where the Shankaracharya sits in the evening to meet visitors. Author alleges luxury, restricted areas and swimming pool Writer Dr Bhumika Dwivedi, who stayed at the monastery for about two months in 2022 during her research, made several allegations. She claimed the monastery had luxury facilities, including air-conditioned rooms, LED televisions, expensive carpets and marble construction. She alleged that some areas were restricted and controlled by a female associate of the Shankaracharya. According to her, certain rooms and floors were inaccessible to common residents. She also claimed there was a swimming pool on the top floor and an elevator leading to restricted sections. Dwivedi further alleged that children from poor families were made to perform work inside the monastery and that strict control was maintained over access and movement. Shankaracharya and disciple deny allegations Mukundanand rejected the accusations and called them false. He said the monastery follows religious activities and is open to visitors. Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand also denied the claims. He said the allegations were baseless and made out of frustration. He added that any investigation findings would be released by authorities, not individuals. Background of leadership and succession Swami Avimukteshwaranand became head of Jyotishpeeth Badrinath after the death of his guru, Shankaracharya Swami Swaroopanand Saraswati, on September 11, 2022. Swaroopanand Saraswati had served as Shankaracharya of Dwarka and Jyotishpeeth. The controversy surrounding Srividya Math continues, with allegations and counterclaims raising questions that may be resolved through investigation.

stories.title: Lathmar Holi begins in Nandgaon:Women beat Huriyars with sticks; 1 million reach Nand Baba Temple for Gulal celebrations
stories.summary: In Mathura, Lathmar Holi is being played on Thursday at Rangili Chowki in Nandgaon. Decorated friends of Radharani are showering sticks on the 'huriyare' (men who play Holi) who have come from Barsana. The 'huriyare' are blocking their attacks with their shields. During this, a lot of abeer and gulal is also being thrown. Along with this, people are dancing. Around 10 lakh people from India and abroad have reached Nandgaon to witness Lathmar Holi. Lord Krishna spent his childhood in Nandgaon, while Radha ji grew up in Barsana. The distance between these two villages is only 8 KM. It has been a tradition since the Dwapar Yuga that first, Krishna's friends from Nandgaon go to Barsana to play Holi. The next day, the 'huriyare' from Barsana come to Nandgaon to play Lathmar Holi. Before this, Lathmar Holi was played in Barsana on Wednesday (February 25). At that time, the friends of Krishna who had gone from Nandgaon were heavily beaten with sticks by the friends of Barsana. See 4 pictures of Barsana During Lathmar Holi, a lot of abeer, gulal, and colors are also being thrown.

stories.title: Varanasi police arrest father-son linked to codeine cough syrup syndicate:₹25,000 reward announced on each; ₹13.53 crore property already seized
stories.summary: Varanasi police arrested Manoj Yadav, owner of Syndicate Enterprises, and his son Lakshya Yadav for their alleged involvement in the illegal codeine cough syrup trade. Both were arrested late Thursday night from Tengra turn in the Ramnagar police station area. A Special Investigation Team (SIT) was also present during the operation. Police had announced a reward of ₹25,000 each for information leading to their arrest. Both accused are residents of Ausanganj in the Jaitpura police station area. Police said they were involved in buying and selling codeine cough syrup using fake e-way bills. They also carried out transactions with Shelly Traders, a firm linked to Bhola Jaiswal, father of main accused Shubham Jaiswal. Cases registered in Ramnagar and Kotwali police stations ACP Kotwali Vijay Pratap Singh said Manoj Yadav already has a case registered at Kotwali police station for illegal cough syrup trade. Another case against Manoj and Lakshya is registered at Ramnagar police station for illegal supply of cough syrup. Police said the accused traded cough syrup worth lakhs of rupees and had been absconding for several days. Both will be produced in court and sent to jail. Police also said the accused invested money earned from the illegal trade into real estate. Manoj Yadav is linked to a real estate firm named MSS Pharma. Close links with Bhola Jaiswal and Shelly Traders According to police, Manoj Yadav is a close associate of Bhola Jaiswal, who is currently in Sonbhadra jail. Manoj allegedly purchased and supplied large quantities of cough syrup through Shelly Traders. Police said Manoj met Bhola and Shubham Jaiswal through the Saptasagar medicine market. The cough syrup was transported using fake documents. Mastermind Shubham Jaiswal still absconding Police said Bhola Jaiswal has already been arrested in the case, but the main accused, Shubham Jaiswal, is still absconding. He is believed to be abroad. Police said a Red Corner Notice will be issued against him soon. ACP Singh said this is the first time both father and son have been arrested together in the case. Police are continuing interrogation and further investigation. Property worth ₹13.53 crore seized Earlier, on February 24, 2026, Varanasi police seized properties worth ₹13.53 crore belonging to Manoj Yadav. Police also pasted a court notice outside his house and made a public announcement. Police said Manoj Yadav was part of the cough syrup syndicate and had acquired assets through illegal activities. His immovable properties and bank accounts linked to the crime have been frozen as part of legal action.

stories.title: Law student arrested for threatening Shankaracharya’s lawyer:Confesses he sent message to frame neighbour, arrested within 20 hours
stories.summary: Police have arrested a law student for sending a bomb threat to senior advocate and Bar Council of India member Srinath Tripathi, who represents Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand. The accused was arrested from Resipur village under Jansa police station area in Varanasi within 20 hours of the complaint. The Varanasi Police Surveillance Cell tracked the mobile number used to send the threat and detained the accused, identified as Ajit Kumar Saroj. He is a law student and also practices under a lawyer at the Varanasi court. Police said he confessed during interrogation that he sent the message to falsely implicate his neighbour. He is being sent to jail under relevant legal provisions. Threat message warned of blowing up court and lawyer The threatening message was sent from an unknown number at 2:23 AM on Thursday. It read: “We will blow up Banaras court with a bomb and you too.” Advocate Srinath Tripathi said he saw the message in the morning while checking his phone and immediately informed senior police officials. He later went to court, where police officers met him and assured him that the accused would be identified soon. Case registered, number traced through surveillance Joint Commissioner of Police Alok Priyadarshini said a case was registered at Bhelupur police station based on Tripathi’s complaint. The SOG-1 team and surveillance unit were assigned to trace the number. Bhelupur police station in-charge Sudhir Kumar Tripathi said the number was traced to Ajit Kumar Saroj, a resident of Resipur village. Police teams reached the location and arrested him. Accused sent threat to frame neighbour, say police During questioning, the accused told police that he sent the threatening message to frame his neighbour due to a personal dispute. Police said further legal action is underway. Police also noted that the Varanasi court has received four bomb threats in the last 14 days. Three of those threats were sent through emails to the district judge. The IT cell is investigating those emails and trying to identify the senders.

stories.title: Hooting at Savarkar tribute event as Aparna Yadav mentions Modi:Protesters object, accuse PM of dividing society through UGC rules
stories.summary: State Women’s Commission Vice President and BJP leader Aparna Yadav faced protests in Lucknow while speaking at a floral tribute programme on Veer Vinayak Damodar Savarkar’s death anniversary. Aparna was addressing the event on nationalism, Hindutva and women empowerment at the Indian Medical Association auditorium. When she mentioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s name during her speech, some people present in the auditorium started hooting and protesting. The protesters alleged that the Prime Minister had divided society through UGC rules. Despite the disruption, Aparna Yadav appealed for calm and continued her speech. Former MP Sadhvi Pragya Thakur attended the programme as the chief guest. The event was organised by Savarkar Vichar Manch, and its members were present in large numbers. Aparna Yadav said – chose BJP, not dynasty politics Aparna Yadav said she joined the Bharatiya Janata Party after leaving the Samajwadi Party to promote nationalism and oppose dynasty politics. She said women’s safety in Uttar Pradesh has improved through the ‘Mission Shakti’ campaign. She also announced that a statue of Veer Savarkar would be installed. Aparna described Savarkar as a great revolutionary and demanded that he be awarded the Bharat Ratna. Now read what Sadhvi Pragya said… ATS tortured for 13 days Sadhvi Pragya Thakur said that standing against injustice is true courage and dharma. Referring to her arrest in the Malegaon blast case, she alleged that the Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) illegally detained and tortured her for 13 days. She said she was pressured to name some senior leaders. She added that some people helped bring out the truth and thanked them. A person who divided the country cannot be the ‘Father of the Nation’ Sadhvi Pragya praised Savarkar and said repeated efforts are needed to awaken the nation. She said those who understand the nation and their duty deserve respect like Savarkar. Commenting on Mahatma Gandhi, she said a person responsible for the country’s partition cannot be called the ‘Father of the Nation’. Those with nationalist views were persecuted Sadhvi Pragya said people with nationalist views faced persecution. Referring to her election from Bhopal, she said she considered it an ideological battle and won with public support. She also spoke about the sacrifices made by the families of revolutionaries, especially women in Savarkar’s family. She said despite social pressure and hardships, they remained committed to their cause. She called on the youth to put national interest above everything else.

stories.title: Income Tax raids on BSP MLA Umashankar Singh spark row:Yogi minister protests, officials fear exposure of irregularities
stories.summary: Income Tax Department raids on properties linked to Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) MLA Umashankar Singh have triggered a major political controversy in Uttar Pradesh. Leaders across parties have reacted strongly, with allegations and counter-allegations over the timing and motive of the action. The raids continued for the second consecutive day at several locations connected to Singh, who represents Rasda constituency in Ballia district. Officials have not yet released details of what was recovered during the operation. Minister calls raids politically motivated Dinesh Pratap Singh, minister of horticulture and agricultural export in the Yogi Adityanath government and Umashankar Singh’s relative, termed the raids politically motivated. His daughter is married to Umashankar Singh’s son. He said the action appears driven by political revenge rather than evidence. However, BJP sources said his remarks have drawn objections within the party, and senior leaders have taken note of his statements. Considered influential despite being lone BSP MLA Umashankar Singh is the only BSP MLA in the Uttar Pradesh Assembly and has been considered politically influential for several years. He first became MLA in 2012 after joining BSP in 2011 and was re-elected in 2017 and 2022 from Rasda. Despite being in the opposition, Singh has been seen as having strong influence in departments such as Public Works Department (PWD) and mining. Political observers say his reach in administrative matters is widely discussed in political circles. Questions have also been raised in the past over tenders and mining leases linked to firms associated with him. In one case, a major PWD tender was cancelled after media reports highlighted the issue. Opposition leaders question timing of action BSP chief Mayawati publicly defended Singh. In a post on X, she said Singh has worked with honesty and dedication since joining the party. She added that there have been no complaints from his constituency about illegal property or wrongdoing. Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav also criticised the raids and questioned their timing. He suggested that government agencies act selectively and alleged political bias in such actions. Akhilesh also made remarks about the timing of the raids, linking them to political developments and foreign visits by senior leaders. He accused the BJP of using central agencies for political purposes. Close ties with ruling establishment under scrutiny Umashankar Singh has often supported the BJP and NDA in key votes. He voted in favour of NDA candidates in the Presidential and Vice-Presidential elections and supported the BJP in the 2024 Rajya Sabha polls. His political and personal connections with leaders in the ruling establishment have drawn attention, especially after the raids. His influence became evident when a bridge built by his firm was inaugurated in Ballia, leading to a dispute with Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh. There have also been allegations that officers close to him received key postings in certain districts, though no official confirmation has been made. Political implications ahead of elections Political analysts believe the raids could have wider political implications. As the only BSP MLA in the Assembly, Umashankar Singh plays a key role in maintaining the party’s presence in the House. Some experts believe the raids may be aimed at examining financial links and gathering evidence related to contracts and political funding. Others say central agencies do not conduct such operations without evidence. The Income Tax Department has not issued an official statement on the findings so far. The raids and the political reactions have intensified debate over the use of investigative agencies in politically sensitive cases in Uttar Pradesh.

Pakistan poverty explodes, inequality at 27-year high as economic crisis deepens
stories.summary: Pakistan's poverty has surged to an 11-year high of 29%, with 70 million people now in extreme poverty. Income inequality has also reached a 27-year peak of 32.7. These increases are attributed to IMF stabilization policies, natural disasters, and weak growth, leading to a 12% fall in real household income over seven years.

stories.title: Ajit Pawar plane crash: Rohit Pawar writes to PM Modi, demands Aviation minister's resignation
stories.summary: NCP (SP) leader Rohit Pawar has urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to seek the resignation of Civil Aviation Minister K Ram Mohan Naidu pending an inquiry into the January 28 plane crash that killed Ajit Pawar. Pawar alleged potential links between the aircraft's owner, VSR, and the minister's party, demanding an independent probe into the incident and possible conspiracy.

UAE launches pioneering gene therapy to treat autism and rare brain disorders in children
stories.summary: The UAE has launched two gene therapy projects targeting the root causes of autism and rare brain disorders, marking a significant shift from symptom management to biological repair. Collaborating with global experts, these initiatives aim to enhance treatment effectiveness and safety for children with conditions like BPAN, paving the way for future inherited disease therapies.

stories.title: Streamer Clavicular breaks silence on Polymarket 20% prediction during Piers Morgan Uncensored after charges were dropped
stories.summary: Clavicular reacted after Polymarket predicted a 20 percent chance he could be charged with a crime by June 30. Speaking on the Piers Morgan Uncensored, he said he would try to stay out of trouble. His recent Arizona arrest was dismissed, but controversy and online speculation continue to follow him.

The Butterfly Effect: How Hamas attack on Oct 7 destroyed Iran's Axis of Resistance
stories.summary: That day, a terrorist organisation’s desire to imbibe a little culture by paragliding into a music festival ended up rewriting the world order. The story that followed could have been directed by Quentin Tarantino: gory, non-linear, with all threads interconnected and a few perverts thrown in. Israel’s furious response, with help from Uncle Sam, led to the dismantling of Iran’s Axis of Resistance, tangentially hastened Trump’s return to the White House, and reminded Russia, China, and even Europe who is Daddy.
